question: Which dance from Gujarat is performed with sticks during Navratri?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dandiya Raas**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• **Dandiya Raas** is a traditional folk dance originating from the state of **Gujarat**, India, and is performed during the **Navratri festival**. 

• The dance is characterized by the use of **decorated wooden sticks**, known as **Dandiyas**, which participants strike together rhythmically to the beat of the music. 

• **Dandiya Raas** represents the dramatization of the battle between the goddess **Durga** and the demon **Mahishasura**, symbolizing the victory of good over evil. 

• It is a group dance, traditionally performed in a circular formation, with dancers energetically moving in sync with the music, often accompanied by vibrant traditional attire. 

• This dance form is widely popular not only in Gujarat but across India, particularly during the **9-day Navratri celebrations**, making it a significant cultural tradition. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Garba:** 
 

• Another popular dance form from **Gujarat**, performed during **Navratri**. 

• Unlike Dandiya Raas, Garba involves circular movements performed without sticks and emphasizes graceful hand and foot movements. 

• Garba is performed in honor of **Goddess Durga**, and participants usually dance around a centrally placed **light or deity**. 
 
 

• **Kolattam:** 
 

• Kolattam is a traditional stick dance from the state of **Tamil Nadu**. 

• It is performed in groups with synchronized stick movements, and while it shares similarities with Dandiya Raas, it is culturally distinct. 

• Kolattam is often associated with temple festivals and is performed to devotional songs. 
 
 

• **Perini Shivatandavam:** 
 

• Perini Shivatandavam is a historic dance form from **Telangana**, dedicated to **Lord Shiva**. 

• This dance is considered a warrior dance, traditionally performed to invoke the spirit of Shiva before going to war. 

• Unlike Dandiya Raas, it does not involve sticks but focuses on vigorous movements and expressions. 
 
 

• **Navratri Festival:** 
 

• Navratri is a **9-day Hindu festival** celebrated across India, dedicated to the worship of the **Goddess Durga**. 

• It is marked by fasting, prayers, and cultural events, including folk dances like **Dandiya Raas** and **Garba**. 

• Navratri celebrations differ across regions, showcasing the diversity of India’s cultural heritage. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Significance of Dandiya Raas:** 
 

• The sticks used in Dandiya Raas symbolize the **sword of Goddess Durga**. 

• The dance promotes **community bonding** as it is performed in groups, often fostering joy and unity among participants. 

• The music accompanying Dandiya Raas is typically traditional folk songs, often sung in **Gujarati**, adding authenticity to the cultural experience. 
 
 

• **Modern Adaptations:** 
 

• While traditionally performed in villages, Dandiya Raas has gained popularity in urban areas and is now organized in large-scale events. 

• Modern Dandiya events often include **fusion music**, combining traditional beats with contemporary tunes to attract younger participants. 

• The attire has evolved to include vibrant and stylish costumes inspired by Gujarati tradition, enhancing the visual appeal of the dance.

question: Which of the following dances is typically performed during weddings in Kerala?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Oppana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oppana** is a popular social dance form that originated in the **Malabar** region of **Kerala**, specifically within the **Muslim** community. It is a vital part of wedding celebrations, performed to entertain the bride and groom. ***Hence, the correct answer is Oppana.***
 
• The dance is typically performed by a group of **10 to 15 women**, including musicians. The bride, dressed in traditional finery and **gold ornaments**, sits in the center while the dancers move rhythmically around her, clapping their hands.
 
• The songs sung during the performance are known as **Mappila Pattu**. These songs are a blend of **Malayalam** and **Arabic** influences, reflecting the unique cultural heritage of the **Mappila** Muslims of **Kerala**.
 
• The performance usually takes place on the **Maidani** (henna) night or the day of the wedding. While it is predominantly a female dance, a male version also exists to entertain the groom during the **Nikah** festivities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hojagiri**: This is a traditional folk dance from the state of **Tripura**. It is performed by the **Reang** community during the **Hojagiri festival** or **Laxmi Puja**. The dancers, usually **4 to 6 women**, perform acrobatic movements while balancing **bottles** or **earthen lamps** on their heads. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Giddha**: This is a famous folk dance of women in the **Punjab** region of **India** and **Pakistan**. It is often performed during the harvest festival of **Baisakhi** and at **weddings**. It is characterized by its energetic pace and the singing of **Boliyan**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Dhamyal**: Also known as **Dhamal**, this dance belongs to the state of **Haryana**. It is performed by men, particularly in the **Ahirwal** region (districts like **Mahendragarh** and **Jhajjar**), during the **Phalguna** month to celebrate the harvest. It is said to be one of the oldest dance forms, dating back to the **Mahabharata** era. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kerala** is home to several other community-specific wedding dances, such as **Margamkali**, which is performed by the **Syrian Christian** community.
 
• The **Mappila Pattu** songs used in **Oppana** cover various themes, including **religion**, **romance**, and **social life**, and have been a part of **Kerala's** literary tradition for over **seven centuries**.
 
• The term **Oppana** is believed to be derived from the **Arabic** word **Affna**. Geographically, the dance is most prominent in the **Northern** districts of **Kerala**, such as **Kozhikode**, **Kannur**, and **Malappuram**.
 
• In modern times, **Oppana** has gained immense popularity beyond weddings and is a staple performance in the **Kerala School Kalolsavam**, which is the largest youth arts festival in **Asia**.

question: Which of the following is a dance from Chhattisgarh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bison Horn Maria**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Bison Horn Maria** is a prominent tribal dance performed by the **Maria tribe** (specifically the **Dandami Maria**) of the **Bastar** district in **Chhattisgarh**. The dance is named after the unique headgear worn by the male dancers, which features the horns of a **wild bison**. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***

• **Gaddi Nati** is a traditional folk dance belonging to the **Gaddi** community of **Himachal Pradesh**. It is typically performed during festivals like **Shivratri** and other local fairs to celebrate the harvest or religious occasions in the **Himalayan** region. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

• **Baiga Pardhoni** is a dance performed by the **Baiga tribe**, who are primarily located in the **Maikal Hills** of **Madhya Pradesh** and parts of **Chhattisgarh**. It is specifically a wedding dance performed to welcome the **Baraat** (groom's procession). While it exists in Chhattisgarh, **Bison Horn Maria** is the more iconic and widely recognized dance associated with the state's tribal identity in this context. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

• **Bagurumba** is a popular folk dance of the **Bodo** tribe in **Assam**. It is also known as the **Butterfly Dance** because the rhythmic movements of the dancers' arms resemble the flapping of wings. It is performed during the **Bwisagu** festival in **mid-April**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Chhattisgarh**, often referred to as the **Rice Bowl of India**, was formed on **1 November 2000**. The state is home to a significant tribal population, accounting for approximately **30.6%** of its total inhabitants.

• The **Bastar** region is the cultural heart of the state, where various tribes like the **Gond**, **Abujhmaria**, **Muria**, and **Halba** reside. The **Bastar Dussehra** is a world-famous festival celebrated here for **75 days**, making it the longest festival in the world.

• Other significant folk dances of **Chhattisgarh** include **Raut Nacha**, a ceremonial dance of the **Yaduvanshi** community performed during **Dev Uthani Ekadashi**, and **Panthi**, the traditional dance of the **Satnami** community.

• **Pandwani** is a world-renowned folk ballad form from **Chhattisgarh** that depicts the stories of the **Pandavas** from the **Mahabharata**. Famous exponents like **Teejan Bai** have brought international recognition to this art form.

• The **Maria** tribe is known for its artistic skills, including **wood carving** and **terracotta** work, which are often showcased during their festivals and community gatherings.

**Important Points__**

• In the **Bison Horn Maria** dance, the male dancers wear a headgear made of **bison horns**, **peacock feathers**, and **cowrie shells**. They carry a long cylindrical drum called the **Dhol** to maintain a powerful rhythm.

• The women participating in the **Bison Horn Maria** dance carry **iron rattling sticks** known as **Tirududi**, which they strike on the ground in synchronization with the drum beats to create a unique auditory experience.

• The **Baiga** tribe is recognized as one of the **75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)** in **India**. Their **Pardhoni** dance often features a person wearing a **tiger mask** or a **bull mask** made of wood and straw to entertain the wedding guests.

• The **Gaddi** shepherds of **Himachal Pradesh** perform the **Nati** dance in a slow, circular motion, reflecting their calm and steady lifestyle in the **Dhauladhar** range.

• **Bagurumba** dancers in **Assam** wear traditional **Bodo** attire, including the **Dokhona** (wrap-around dress) and **Jwmgra** (scarf), and the dance is a tribute to nature and the beauty of the **Brahmaputra** valley.

question: Bihu songs are a part of which Indian state's folk tradition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Bihu songs**, known as **Bihu Geet**, are a core component of the folk tradition of **Assam**, a state in **Northeast India**. These songs are performed during the **Bihu festival**, which is the most important cultural celebration for the **Assamese community**.

• The songs are traditionally characterized by themes of **love**, **eroticism**, **nature**, and the **agricultural cycle**. They reflect the joys and sorrows of the rural life of **Assam**.

• **Bihu songs** are accompanied by the **Bihu dance**, which involves energetic steps and rapid hand movements. This folk tradition is inclusive, performed by both young men and women in the open fields or **Bakori**.

• The musical accompaniment for these songs includes traditional instruments like the **Dhol** (a percussion instrument), **Pepa** (a hornpipe made from buffalo horn), **Gogona** (a reed/bamboo instrument), **Toka** (a bamboo clapper), and **Bahi** (flute).

• The tradition is deeply rooted in the **fertility cult**, where the music and dance are believed to stimulate the **earth's fertility** and ensure a **bountiful harvest**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Assam.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Punjab**: This northern state is famous for folk traditions like **Bhangra** and **Gidda**. **Bhangra** is typically performed by men during the **Baisakhi** festival to celebrate the harvest, while **Gidda** is a graceful dance performed by women.

• **Gujarat**: Known for its vibrant folk dances such as **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas**, which are performed extensively during the **Navratri** festival. These traditions involve circular movements and the use of sticks (Dandiya) to honor **Goddess Durga**.

• **Odisha**: This state is home to the classical dance **Odissi** and various folk traditions like **Sambalpuri**, **Chhau**, and **Ghumura**. **Sambalpuri** songs and dances are particularly famous for their rhythmic beats and the use of the **Mahuri** and **Dhol**.

• **Assam's Three Bihus**: The state celebrates three types of Bihu in a **year**. **Bohag Bihu** (or **Rongali Bihu**) in **April** marks the **Assamese New Year**; **Kati Bihu** (or **Kongali Bihu**) in **October** is a more solemn observation related to crop protection; and **Magh Bihu** (or **Bhogali Bihu**) in **January** is a harvest festival centered around feasting.

**Important Points__**

• In **April 2023**, **Assam** created a **Guinness World Record** when over **11,000** dancers and drummers performed the **Bihu dance** and played the **Dhol** at the **Sarusajai Stadium** in **Guwahati**.

• The **Pepa**, an essential instrument in **Bihu songs**, is traditionally crafted from the horn of a **dead buffalo**, and its piercing sound is synonymous with the **spring season** in **Assam**.

• **Bihu Geet** are often composed in **couplets** that rhyme, making them easy to improvise and pass down through **oral tradition** across **generations**.

• The **Government of India** and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** actively promote **Bihu** as a vital part of India's **intangible cultural heritage**.
</ul

question: Zangtalam is the folk dance of which Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zangtalam **is a traditional community dance performed by the **Paite tribe of Mizoram**.
 
• This vibrant dance involves both men and women singing and dancing in unison to the** rhythmic beat of drums.**
 
• During the performance, male dancers typically form a line in front of the female dancers, who adorn themselves in colorful attire, necklaces, and earrings.
 
• The drummer serves as the leader and conductor of the dance, directing the movements of the performers.
 
• **Zangtalam **is characterized by its elegant and rhythmic steps, creating a captivating spectacle for spectators.
 
• The Paite tribe, indigenous to the region, migrated from Myanmar to Mizoram during the late 19th century.
 
• They have established communities in more than 20 villages across various districts of **Mizoram, including Saitual, Champhai, Aizawl, and Khawzawl.**

• **Mizoram**, a state located in northeast India, has **Aizawl **as its seat of government and capital city.
 
• Situated in the southernmost part of India's northeast region, Mizoram is the only landlocked state, bordered by three of the Seven Sister States: Tripura, Assam, and Manipur.
 
• It shares a 722-kilometer (449 mi) border with the neighboring countries of Bangladesh and Myanmar.
 
• Mizoram was part of Assam until 1972 when it was established as a Union Territory.
 
• In 1986, the Indian Parliament enacted the 53rd amendment of the Indian Constitution, facilitating the establishment of the State of Mizoram on 20th February 1987, marking it as India's 23rd state.

question: Which festival celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Janmashtami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Janmashtami** is a Hindu festival celebrated to mark the birth of **Lord Krishna**, who is considered the eighth avatar of Lord Vishnu.
 
• The festival is observed on the eighth day (**Ashtami**) of the Krishna Paksha (dark fortnight) in the month of **Bhadrapada**, as per the Hindu calendar.
 
• This day usually falls in the months of **August or September** in the Gregorian calendar. *Hence, the correct answer is Janmashtami.*
 
• **Celebrations:** Devotees perform rituals like fasting, singing devotional songs, and reenacting episodes from Krishna's life. **Dahi Handi**, a popular tradition, involves breaking a pot filled with curd, symbolizing Krishna's childhood activities.
 
• The festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm across India, especially in regions like **Mathura** (Krishna’s birthplace), **Vrindavan**, and **Dwarka**. Temples dedicated to Lord Krishna are beautifully decorated.
 
• **Historical Significance:** Lord Krishna is believed to have been born to **Devaki** and **Vasudeva** in a prison in Mathura. His birth signifies the victory of good over evil, as he destroyed his tyrant uncle **Kansa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ganesh Chaturthi:**

 
 
• This festival celebrates the birth of **Lord Ganesha**, the deity of wisdom and prosperity. It is celebrated in the month of **Bhadrapada** (August–September).
 
• The festival is particularly popular in states like **Maharashtra** and involves worshipping clay idols of Ganesha and immersing them in water after several days of rituals.
 
 
 
• **Ram Navami:**
 
 
• This festival marks the birth of **Lord Rama**, an avatar of Lord Vishnu. It is celebrated on the ninth day of **Chaitra Navratri** (March–April).
 
• Devotees recite the **Ramayana**, perform prayers, and organize processions in honor of Lord Rama.
 
 
 
• **Navratri:**
 
 
• Navratri is a nine-day festival dedicated to the worship of **Goddess Durga**. It is celebrated twice a year: **Chaitra Navratri** (March–April) and **Sharada Navratri** (September–October).
 
• The festival involves fasting, dancing (like Garba and Dandiya in Gujarat), and worshipping the nine forms of Durga.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Janmashtami Celebrations Worldwide:**

 
 
• Apart from India, Janmashtami is celebrated by the **Indian diaspora** in countries like the **United States, Canada, United Kingdom, and Australia**. ISKCON temples play a major role in organizing events globally.
 
• ISKCON celebrates the festival with **kirtans, bhajans, and Bhagavad Gita discourses**. They also organize large-scale Dahi Handi events.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Fasting:**
 
 
• Fasting on Janmashtami symbolizes devotion and discipline. Devotees often fast until midnight, which is believed to be the hour of Krishna’s birth.
 
• Midnight prayers and celebrations are accompanied by the recital of **Bhagavad Gita** verses and Krishna’s life stories.
 
 
 
• **Places of Major Celebrations:**
 
 
• **Mathura:** The birthplace of Krishna witnesses grand celebrations, including processions and rituals in temples like the **Krishna Janmasthan Temple.**
 
• **Vrindavan:** Famous for its connection to Krishna’s childhood, it hosts events like Raslila performances depicting episodes from Krishna’s life.

question: Which Indian festival is celebrated to mark the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwali**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Diwali**, also known as **Deepavali**, is celebrated to mark the return of **Lord Rama**, his wife **Sita**, and his brother **Lakshmana** to their kingdom, **Ayodhya**, after **14 years** of exile. *Hence, this option is correct.*

• **Holi** is the **Festival of Colors**, celebrated to mark the arrival of spring and the victory of **Prahlada** over the demoness **Holika**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

• **Navratri** is a festival spanning **nine nights** dedicated to the worship of **Goddess Durga** and her nine different forms. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

• **Dussehra**, or **Vijayadashami**, marks the day **Lord Rama** killed the demon king **Ravana**, occurring exactly **20 days** before **Diwali**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

• The return of **Lord Rama** to **Ayodhya** is celebrated by lighting thousands of **earthen lamps** (**diyas**), symbolizing the victory of **light over darkness** and **good over evil**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Diwali** is observed on the **Amavasya** (new moon day) of the month of **Kartik** in the **Hindu Lunisolar calendar**, which usually falls in **October** or **November**.

• The festival is a **five-day** celebration that begins with **Dhanteras**, followed by **Naraka Chaturdashi** (**Chhoti Diwali**), **Lakshmi Puja**, **Govardhan Puja**, and ends with **Bhai Dooj**.

• In **Jainism**, **Diwali** marks the **Nirvana** (final liberation) of **Lord Mahavira**, the **24th Tirthankara**, which took place in **527 BCE**.

• In **Sikhism**, the day is celebrated as **Bandi Chhor Divas** to commemorate the release of **Guru Hargobind Ji**, the **sixth Sikh Guru**, from the **Gwalior Fort** in **1619**.

• In **West Bengal** and **Odisha**, the day is also celebrated as **Kali Puja** to honor **Goddess Kali**, the destroyer of evil.

**Important Points__**

• The life and journey of **Lord Rama** are detailed in the ancient Indian epic **Ramayana**, composed by **Sage Valmiki**.

• **Ayodhya**, the birthplace of **Lord Rama**, is located on the banks of the **Saryu River** in the state of **Uttar Pradesh**, **India**.

• During the festival, people decorate their homes with **Rangoli** (artistic floor patterns) and prepare various **sweets** to share with friends and family.

• **Goddess Lakshmi**, the deity of **wealth** and **prosperity**, and **Lord Ganesha**, the remover of obstacles, are the primary deities worshipped during **Lakshmi Puja**.

• The festival is a **national holiday** in several countries, including **India**, **Nepal** (where it is called **Tihar**), **Sri Lanka**, **Mauritius**, **Fiji**, and **Guyana**.
</ul

question: Which harvest festival is celebrated in Punjab during January?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lohri**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Lohri** is a popular **harvest festival** celebrated primarily in the **Punjab** region of the Indian subcontinent. It is observed with great enthusiasm by both **Sikhs** and **Hindus** to mark the end of the peak winter season.

• The festival is celebrated every year on the **13th of January**, just a day before **Makar Sankranti**. It signifies the sun's entry into the northern hemisphere, known as **Uttarayana**, leading to longer days and shorter nights.

• It is traditionally associated with the harvest of **Rabi crops**, particularly **sugarcane**. Farmers in **Punjab** and **Haryana** offer prayers and thanks to the **Almighty** for a successful harvest and pray for prosperity in the coming season.

• The central ritual of **Lohri** is the lighting of a **bonfire** after sunset. People gather around the fire, sing traditional folk songs, and perform **Bhangra** and **Gidda**. Offerings of **til** (sesame seeds), **gajak**, **gur** (jaggery), **popcorn**, and **rewri** are thrown into the fire as a tribute to the **God of Fire (Agni)**.

• The festival is also deeply linked to the legend of **Dulla Bhatti**, a local hero who lived during the reign of **Emperor Akbar**. He is remembered for rescuing young girls from being sold into slavery and arranging their marriages. The famous folk song **Sunder Mundriye** is sung during the celebrations to honor his bravery.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Pongal**: This is a **four-day** harvest festival celebrated in the state of **Tamil Nadu**. It usually falls between **January 14th and 17th**. It is dedicated to the **Sun God (Surya)** and involves the ritual of boiling fresh rice in milk in a clay pot until it overflows, symbolizing abundance.

• **Bihu**: Specifically **Magh Bihu** (also known as **Bhogali Bihu**), is the harvest festival of **Assam** celebrated in **January**. It marks the end of the harvesting season in the month of **Maagha**. People build temporary huts called **Meji** and **Bhelaghar** from bamboo and thatch, which are burned the next morning.

• **Makar Sankranti**: This is a major pan-Indian festival that marks the transition of the **Sun** into the zodiac sign of **Capricorn (Makara)**. While it is celebrated on **January 14th or 15th**, it is known by various names such as **Uttarayan** in **Gujarat** (famous for kite flying), **Poush Sankranti** in **West Bengal**, and **Khichdi** in **Uttar Pradesh**.

• **Vaisakhi**: Although it is also a harvest festival in **Punjab**, it is celebrated in the month of **April** (usually **April 13th or 14th**). It marks the ripening of the **wheat (Rabi) crop** and also commemorates the formation of the **Khalsa Panth** by **Guru Gobind Singh** in **1699**.

**Important Points__**

• **Social Significance**: **Lohri** holds special importance for families that have recently celebrated a **wedding** or the **birth of a child**. The 'first Lohri' of a new bride or a newborn is celebrated with extra fervor and grand feasts.

• **Traditional Cuisine**: The traditional dinner served during **Lohri** consists of **Sarson da Saag** (mustard greens) and **Makki di Roti** (cornbread), which are seasonal staples in **North India**.

• **Geographical Reach**: While it is the primary festival of **Punjab**, it is also widely celebrated in **Delhi**, **Himachal Pradesh**, and **Jammu** due to the significant **Punjabi** diaspora and cultural influence in these regions.

• **Environmental Aspect**: In recent years, there has been a growing awareness to celebrate **Eco-friendly Lohri** by reducing the size of bonfires to prevent excessive air pollution, while still maintaining the cultural essence of the festival.
</ul

• Stupas are a symbol of **Buddhism**.
 
• They are mound-like or hemispherical structures containing relics (typically the remains of Buddhist monks or nuns) and are used as a place of meditation.

• **Buddhism** was founded by Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha, in the 5th century BCE in ancient India.
 
• The core teachings of Buddhism include the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path, which guide individuals towards enlightenment.
 
• Buddhism emphasizes the importance of meditation, ethical conduct, and wisdom in achieving spiritual goals.
 
• There are several branches of Buddhism, including Theravada, Mahayana, and Vajrayana, each with its own unique practices and interpretations of the Buddha's teachings.
 
• Buddhism has a significant cultural and historical impact on many countries in Asia and has also spread to other parts of the world.

question: The festival of Navratri is associated with the worship of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Goddess Durga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The festival of **Navratri** is one of the most significant **Hindu** festivals, primarily dedicated to the worship of **Goddess Durga**. The word **Navratri** is derived from **Sanskrit**, where **'Nava'** means **nine** and **'Ratri'** means **nights**.
 
• The festival spans over **nine nights** and **ten days**, during which **nine** distinct forms of the **Goddess**, known as **Navadurga**, are invoked and worshipped.
 
• It celebrates the victory of **Goddess Durga** over the buffalo demon **Mahishasura**. This battle signifies the triumph of **Dharma** (righteousness) over **Adharma** (evil). ***Hence, the correct answer is Goddess Durga.***
 
• While there are **four** seasonal **Navratris** in a **year**, the most prominent one is **Sharada Navratri**, which typically falls in the **lunar month** of **Ashvin** (corresponding to **September** or **October** in the **Gregorian calendar**).
 
• Each of the **nine** days is associated with a specific **color** and a specific incarnation of the **Goddess**, including **Shailaputri**, **Brahmacharini**, **Chandraghanta**, **Kushmanda**, **Skandamata**, **Katyayani**, **Kaalratri**, **Mahagauri**, and **Siddhidhatri**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regional Celebrations:**
 
 
• In **West Bengal**, **Odisha**, and **Assam**, the festival is celebrated as **Durga Puja**, where grand **pandals** are created to house clay idols of the **Goddess**.
 
• In **Gujarat**, the festival is marked by traditional dances known as **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas**, where people dance in circles around a lamp or an image of the **Goddess**.
 
• In **North India**, the **Ramleela** (dramatic enactment of the **Ramayana**) is performed, culminating in **Dussehra**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Tenth Day:**
 
 
• The **tenth** day is celebrated as **Vijayadashami** or **Dussehra**. It marks the day **Goddess Durga** killed **Mahishasura** and also the day **Lord Rama** defeated the demon king **Ravana**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Navratri:**
 
 
• **Chaitra Navratri:** Celebrated in the **month** of **Chaitra** (**March**-**April**), it marks the beginning of the **Hindu New Year** (**Vikram Samvat**).
 
• **Magha** and **Ashada Navratri:** These are known as **Gupta Navratri**, which are observed primarily by **Sadhakas** and **Tantriks** for spiritual practices.
 
 
 
• **Symbolism:**
 
 
• **Goddess Durga** is often depicted with **eight** or **ten** arms, riding a **lion** or **tiger**, and carrying various weapons, representing her **Shakti** (feminine power) and protective nature.
 
 
</ul

question: Lohri, a popular festival of North India, is mainly associated with:
solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Sugarcane harvesting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lohri** is a vibrant festival celebrated mainly in **Punjab** and parts of **North India**. It is observed on **13th January** every year.
 
• The festival marks the end of the **winter solstice** and is a celebration of the harvest season.
 
• **Sugarcane harvesting** plays a central role in Lohri celebrations. Farmers celebrate the successful harvest of sugarcane, which is one of the primary crops in Punjab and Haryana. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*
 
• During Lohri, people light a bonfire and offer items like **jaggery**, **rewari**, **popcorn**, and **sesame seeds** to the fire as part of the rituals, symbolizing gratitude for the harvest.
 
• Although Lohri is associated with the harvest season, it is specifically tied to the harvesting of sugarcane rather than rice or mangoes. *Hence, option 1 and option 4 are incorrect.*
 
• The festival is also associated with the **winter solstice**, as it marks the transition to longer days. However, the primary focus is on sugarcane harvesting. *Hence, option 2 is partially correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 3) Sugarcane harvesting.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lohri Festival:**

 
 
• Lohri is considered a festival of farmers and is celebrated with great enthusiasm in **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and parts of **Delhi**.
 
• It is a harvest festival that is celebrated after the sowing of the **rabi crops**. Farmers thank **God** for the bountiful harvest.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Sugarcane:**
 
 
• **Sugarcane** is one of the most important crops in Punjab and Haryana. Its harvest marks the beginning of Lohri celebrations.
 
• Sugarcane is used to make **jaggery**, which is a key offering during the rituals of the festival.
 
• Products like **rewari** and **gachak**, prepared using sugarcane and sesame, are distributed among family and friends during Lohri.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Elements:**
 
 
• Traditional songs and dances such as **bhangra** and **gidda** are performed around the bonfire.
 
• The festival is also an occasion for family gatherings and sharing joy.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context:**
 
 
• Lohri is predominantly celebrated in **Punjab** and northern regions of **India**, where sugarcane is a major crop.
 
• The festival reflects the agrarian lifestyle and traditions of these areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Festivals Related to Harvest:**

 
 
• **Pongal:** Celebrated in **Tamil Nadu**, it marks the harvest of rice and other crops.
 
• **Makar Sankranti:** Observed across India, it signifies the sun's transition into the zodiac sign of Capricorn and is associated with harvest celebrations.
 
• **Bihu:** Celebrated in **Assam**, it marks the harvesting of paddy.
 
 
 
• **Historical and Social Significance:**
 
 
• Lohri is an occasion to celebrate unity, express gratitude to nature, and share prosperity among the community.
 
• The festival has evolved as a cultural symbol of **joy** and **togetherness** in North India.

__
 
• **Huthri **is a **harvest festival** and is celebrated in **Karnataka**.
 
• This harvest festival, literally **meaning “new rice crop”**, is celebrated in Kodagu when the paddy is ready to be harvested in the months of **November- December**.
 
• The ceremonious cutting of the new paddy crop by the head of the family falls on a full moon night and is accompanied by chants of **“Poli, Poli, Deva**” (O God, give us a bountiful harvest).
 
• A single shot is fired to summon **Lord Iguthappa**, the presiding **deity **of the **Kodava people**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **state celebration**, or **Nadahabba**, of the Indian state of **Karnataka **is called **Mysore Dasara**.

 
 
• The celebration lasts for** ten days**, with **Navaratri**, the first nine nights, and **Vijayadashami**, the last day.
 
• The celebration is held on the** tenth day of Ashvina**, the Hindu month that corresponds to **September and October** in the Gregorian calendar.
 
 
 
• An **annual buffalo race** known as the **Kambala**, Kambla, or Kambula takes place in the Indian state of **Karnataka **in the southwest.
 
 
• It is **traditionally **supported by **Tuluva landlords **and households in the coastal regions of Kasaragod, Kerala, and Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka, together referred to as Tulu Nadu. 
 
• The Kambala **season **generally starts in **November **and** lasts until March**.
 
 
 
• **Hampi Utsav**, **Hampi festival** also known as the **Vijaya Utsav**, is one of the largest celebrations of the ancient **Vijayanagar empire** now in **Hampi**, **Karnataka**.
 
 
• The **festivities **take place every year at the** Virupaksha Temple**, commemorating the culture, traditions of the bygone era.
 
• With the beautifully carved **ruins of Hampi** serving as the backdrop, the rich culture of this region is shown through folk song and dance performances.

subject: GK
question: The basic layout of early temples mentioned in the passage typically included:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dome, Garbhagriha, Pillars**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Garbhagriha**, which literally translates to **'womb-house'**, is the most essential part of an early temple. It is a small, square, and windowless chamber that houses the **main deity** or the **idol**. In the earliest stages of temple architecture, such as during the **Gupta Period**, the **Garbhagriha** was a simple room with a single entrance, designed to provide a secluded space for worship. ***Hence, this component is a correct part of the basic layout.***

• **Pillars** were fundamental structural elements used to support the **Mandapa** (assembly hall) or the entrance porch of the temple. Early structural temples, like **Temple 17 at Sanchi** (dating to the **5th Century CE**), featured a flat roof supported by four sturdy **pillars**. These **pillars** often had elaborate carvings and served both functional and aesthetic purposes in early temple design. ***Hence, this component is a correct part of the basic layout.***

• The **Dome** (or the early **Shikhara**) refers to the superstructure built over the **Garbhagriha**. While the very first temples had flat roofs, they soon evolved to include a pyramidal or curvilinear tower to signify the sacredness of the space. In early architectural contexts, the rounded crowning element or the **Amalaka** atop the spire gave it a **dome-like** appearance, distinguishing the temple from secular buildings. ***Hence, this component is a correct part of the basic layout.***

• The combination of a **Sanctum (Garbhagriha)**, **Pillars** for the porch, and a **Superstructure (Dome/Shikhara)** established the standard architectural vocabulary for Indian temples that would persist for centuries.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Nagara Style**: This style of temple architecture is primarily found in **North India**. Its most prominent feature is the **Shikhara**, which is a beehive-shaped tower that curves inward. The **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** at **Khajuraho** is a classic example of this style, featuring multiple **mini-shikharas**.

• **Dravida Style**: Prevalent in **South India**, this style is characterized by a pyramid-shaped tower called a **Vimana**. These temples are often enclosed within high boundary walls with massive gateways known as **Gopurams**. The **Shore Temple** at **Mahabalipuram** is one of the earliest examples of **Dravidian architecture**.

• **Mandapa**: This is the **assembly hall** where devotees gather for prayers and rituals. In larger temples, there can be multiple **Mandapas** (such as the **Maha Mandapa** and **Ardha Mandapa**) leading toward the **Garbhagriha**.

• **Pradakshina Patha**: A **circumambulatory path** that allows devotees to walk around the **Garbhagriha** in a clockwise direction. This path can be open (**Nirandhara**) or enclosed (**Sandhara**).

**Important Points__**

• **Gupta Architecture**: The **Gupta Dynasty** (**4th to 6th Century CE**) marked the transition from **rock-cut caves** to **freestanding structural temples**. The **Dashavatara Temple** at **Deogarh** is significant as it is one of the earliest temples to feature a **Shikhara**.

• **Vesara Style**: This is a **hybrid style** that combines features of both **Nagara** and **Dravida** architecture. It was popularized by the **Chalukyas of Badami** and the **Hoysalas** in the **Deccan region**.

• **Jagati**: Many early temples were built on a **raised platform** called a **Jagati**, which elevated the sacred structure above the ground level.

• **Amalaka and Kalasha**: The **Amalaka** is a stone disc with ridges on the rim that sits atop the **Shikhara**, and the **Kalasha** is the pot-like finial that crowns the entire structure.
</ul

solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagara style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kandariya Mahadeva temple **exemplifies **Nagara-style architecture,** also known as the idol Nagara style, and is renowned as one of** India's finest temples.**
 
• It stands as a prominent example of central Indian architecture and follows the** Panchayatana style**, akin to Kalinga architecture in its arrangement.
 
• Commissioned by** King Dhangadeva of the Chandela dynasty** in 999 CE, the temple is dedicated to the deity Shiva.
 
• Situated in the Khajuraho village at an altitude of 925 feet, it enjoys convenient accessibility via road, rail, and air routes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Originating in northern India during the **5th century CE, the Nagara style **is widespread in regions such as **Malwa, Rajputana, and Kalinga, **spanning states like Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal.
 
• The term "Nagara" denotes "city," reflecting the style's association with urban architectural principles.
 
• Nagara temples typically feature a square or rectangular layout, with a central shikhara (tower-like spire).
 
• These spires often assume a pyramidal shape, with the curvature of the Latina less pronounced.
 
• Nagara temples boast a distinct fusion of indigenous elements and influences from Central Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian architecture,** also known as the Southern Indian temple style, is a distinctive architectural tradition in Hindu temple architecture that evolved in Southern India, reaching its pinnacle by the sixteenth century.
 
• **The Ahom architectural style** is characterized by its amalgamation of diverse cultural, traditional, and religious influences.
 
• **The pagoda structure **is inspired by the stupa, an ancient Indian commemorative monument with a hemispherical, domed shape, which served as the basis for its design.

subject: GK
question: Which temple is known for its erotic sculptures and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khajuraho Temples**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Khajuraho Group of Monuments** is a collection of **Hindu** and **Jain** temples located in the **Chhatarpur district** of **Madhya Pradesh**, India. They are world-renowned for their **Nagara-style** architectural symbolism and their **erotic sculptures**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Khajuraho Temples.***

• These temples were built by the **Chandela dynasty** between **950 AD** and **1050 AD**. The construction of these temples is considered the pinnacle of architectural achievement during the **medieval period** in India.

• The site was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1986** because of its unique artistic creation and historical significance. The sculptures depict various aspects of daily life, mythical stories, and symbolic values.

• The **Brihadeshwara Temple**, located in **Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu**, was built by **Raja Raja Chola I** in the **11th century**. While it is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, it is known for its **Dravidian architecture** and massive **Vimana**, not primarily for erotic sculptures. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• The **Sun Temple, Konark**, located in **Odisha**, was built by **King Narasimhadeva I** of the **Eastern Ganga Dynasty** in the **13th century**. It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** shaped like a giant chariot, but the primary theme is the **Sun God, Surya**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Meenakshi Temple** is a historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the **Vaigai River** in the temple city of **Madurai, Tamil Nadu**. It is dedicated to **Goddess Meenakshi** (Parvati) and **Lord Sundareswarar** (Shiva). Although it is an architectural marvel, it is not currently a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Architectural Style:** The Khajuraho temples are built in the **Nagara style**, characterized by a beehive-shaped tower called a **Shikhara**. The temples are made of **sandstone**, and the blocks were put together with **mortise and tenon joints**, held in place by gravity.

• **The Erotic Art:** The erotic sculptures, often called **Mithuna**, represent about **10%** of the total carvings on the temple walls. These are interpreted as a celebration of **Kama** (desire), which is one of the four goals of human life (**Purusharthas**) in Hindu philosophy, alongside **Dharma**, **Artha**, and **Moksha**.

• **Religious Diversity:** The site is unique because it contains both **Hindu** and **Jain** temples in close proximity, indicating a high level of **religious tolerance** and harmony during the **Chandela rule**.

• **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple:** This is the largest and most ornate temple in the Khajuraho complex. It is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is decorated with more than **800 sculptures** depicting gods, goddesses, musicians, and erotic couples.

• **Rediscovery:** After the decline of the **Chandela dynasty** in the **13th century**, the temples were largely forgotten and covered by dense forests. They were rediscovered by a **British engineer** named **T.S. Burt** in **1838**.

**Important Points__**

• **Number of Temples:** Historical records suggest that there were originally **85 temples** spread over **20 square kilometers**. Today, only about **25 temples** remain in a reasonable state of preservation.

• **Geographical Location:** The temples are situated in the **Vindhya Mountain Range** in central India. The nearest major city is **Jhansi**, and the site is a major hub for **cultural tourism** in **Madhya Pradesh**.

• **Khajuraho Dance Festival:** Every year in **February or March**, the **Madhya Pradesh Kala Parishad** organizes a week-long festival of **classical Indian dances** (like **Kathak**, **Bharatanatyam**, and **Odissi**) against the spectacular backdrop of the **Chitragupta** and **Vishwanatha** temples.

• **Classification:** The temples are generally divided into three geographical groups: the **Western Group** (most famous), the **Eastern Group**, and the **Southern Group**. The **Lakshmana Temple** and **Matangeshvara Temple** are other significant structures within these groups.
</ul

question: In North Indian temple architecture, which element denotes the superstructure or tower above the sanctum and the pillared mandapas?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Shikhara.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shikhara **is a Sanskrit word that means mountain peak. It is the most prominent and visible part of a **Hindu temple of North India**. In South India, it is the same as Vimana.
 
• Shikhara is the rising tower in the Hindu temple architecture of North India.
 
• It is also used in Jain temples.
 
• **Shikhara is over Garbhagriha**. Garbhagriha is the innermost sanctuary of a Hindu and Jain temple where the primary deity of the temple is kept.
 
• Shikhara can be classified into **three main forms - Latina, Sekhar, and Bhumija**.
 
• Shikharas form an element in the many styles of Hindu temple architecture, the three most common styles are the Nagara, the Vesara, and the Dravidian. By at least 600 CE in Odisha, the Latina form of shikhara was well established.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Kalasha**__

 __
 
• The Kalasha is an essential element in Hindu temple architecture.
 
• It is a **pot-shaped structure that crowns the topmost point of the temple.**
 
• Often made of metal or stone, the Kalasha symbolizes purity, abundance, and auspiciousness.
 
• It represents the cosmic axis connecting the earthly and celestial realms.
 
• In North Indian temples, the Kalasha is commonly found atop the Amalaka.
 
 
 
• **Amalaka**__
 __
 
• It is a disc-shaped stone structure positioned at the pinnacle of the temple.
 
• It serves as a **base for the Kalasha****.**__
 
• Commonly seen in North Indian temples, the Amalaka adds architectural elegance.
 
• Its circular form represents the wheel of time or the sun disc.
 
 
 
• __**Antarala (Vestibule)**__
 
 
• The Antarala is a **transitional area connecting the Garbhagriha (sanctum) and the temple’s main hall (Mandapa).**
 
• It acts as a passage for priests and devotees during rituals.
 
• The Antarala often features intricate carvings and decorative elements.

question: The Mimamsa school of philosophy is primarily concerned with which aspect of the Vedas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rituals and Dharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mimamsa** school, also known as **Purva Mimamsa**, is one of the **six orthodox (Astika) schools** of Indian philosophy that accepts the authority of the **Vedas**.
 
• The primary focus of this school is the **interpretation of the Vedas**, specifically the **Samhita** and **Brahmana** portions, which deal with the performance of sacrifices and ceremonies. ***Hence, the concern with Rituals and Dharma is the defining characteristic of this school.***
 
• It defines **Dharma** as the set of duties or **moral obligations** and **rituals** prescribed by the **Vedic injunctions** (Vidhis). According to this philosophy, following these rituals is essential for maintaining the cosmic order and achieving **heaven (Svarga)**.
 
• The school was founded by **Sage Jaimini**, who authored the **Mimamsa Sutras** around the **3rd to 2nd century BCE**. This text serves as the foundational document for the school's logical and linguistic analysis of **Vedic texts**.
 
• Mimamsa emphasizes that the **Vedas** are **eternal (Nitya)** and **authorless (Apaurusheya)**, meaning they were not created by humans or even a divine being, but are self-existent truths.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Distinction from Vedanta:** While **Purva Mimamsa** focuses on the **Karma-kanda** (ritualistic section) of the Vedas, **Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta)** focuses on the **Jnana-kanda** (knowledge section) found in the **Upanishads**, dealing with meditation, the nature of **Brahman**, and **Atman**.
 
• **Concept of Apurva:** This school introduced the unique concept of **Apurva**, which is the **unseen potency** or latent force created by the performance of a ritual. It is this force that eventually produces the **result (Phala)** of the ritual at a later time, even after the physical act is finished.
 
• **Epistemology (Pramanas):** The Mimamsa school is renowned for its deep **linguistic analysis** and theory of knowledge. It accepts up to **six Pramanas** (valid means of knowledge), including **Shabda** (verbal testimony), **Arthapatti** (presumption), and **Anupalabdhi** (non-perception), which were later expanded upon by scholars like **Kumarila Bhatta** and **Prabhakara**.
 
• **Role of Language:** For Mimamsakas, **language (Shabda)** is the only means of knowing **Dharma**, as human senses cannot perceive moral or spiritual duties. They developed sophisticated **hermeneutical rules** for interpreting ambiguous Vedic sentences to ensure rituals are performed correctly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atheistic Tendencies:** Early Mimamsa was essentially **atheistic** in the sense that it did not believe in a **creator God** who manages the universe. Instead, it argued that the universe is **eternal** and governed by the laws of **Karma** and **Rituals**.
 
• **Goal of Liberation:** In its early stages, the goal was the attainment of **heaven** through rituals. However, later scholars like **Kumarila Bhatta** (c. **7th century CE**) shifted the focus towards **Moksha (liberation)**, aligning it more closely with other Indian philosophical systems.
 
• **Other Schools Comparison:** Unlike **Yoga**, which focuses on **Meditation**, or **Vaisheshika**, which focuses on **Atomic theory** and **naturalism**, Mimamsa remains strictly **orthoprax**, meaning it prioritizes correct **action (ritual)** over abstract metaphysical speculation.
 
• **Legacy:** The rules of interpretation developed by this school had a profound impact on the **Indian legal system** (Hindu Law) and the methodology of **Sanskrit grammar** and linguistics throughout **ancient and medieval India**.
</ul

• As per the **Hindu calendar, Vasant Ritu, **or spring, spans the months of **Chaitra and Baisakh**, which approximately align with mid-**February to mid-April **on the Gregorian calendar.

• **During Vasant Ritu**, several significant Hindu festivals are celebrated across the country.
 
• These festivals include Vasant Panchami, Ugadi, Gudi Padwa, Holi, Rama Navami, Vishu, Bihu, Baisakhi, Puthandu, and Hanuman Jayanti.

• **Vasanta Panchami, **celebrated on this day, symbolizes the conclusion of winter and the advent of spring.
 
• This auspicious occasion is dedicated to the worship of the goddess Saraswati, who embodies knowledge, wisdom, and the arts.

__
 
• The annals of **Kannada literature** are incomplete without the mention of **Adikavi Pampa**, a revered **poet of the 10th century**.
 
• Known as the first poet of the language, Pampa's works were primarily in Kannada, and he was a firm believer in **Jainism**.
 
• His two epic works, **Vikramarjuna Vijaya or Pampa Bharata and the Adi Purana**, written around **939 CE**, were composed in the champu style and served as court poems for the **Vemulavada Chalukyan king Arikesari II**.
 
• Pampa also held a position as a feudatory under the **Rashtrakuta dynasty king Krishna III**.
 
• His works set the foundation for all subsequent Kannada champu compositions and marked a significant beginning for the **10th century in Kannada literature**, alongside the works of two other **Jain authors, Sri Ponna and Ranna**, collectively known as the **“Three gems of Kannada literature”**.

• **Akka Mahadevi** (circa 1130 – 1160) emerged as a significant figure in** 12th-century Kannada literature **and played a prominent role within the **Lingayat Shaiva sect**.
 
• She is renowned as one of the **pioneering female poets of this era**.
 
 
 
• **Adikavi** (adi ‘primaeval, first’ + kavi ‘poet’) means **‘the first poet**’.

question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 in Calcutta?
solution:
The correct answer is __**William Jones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Asiatic Society of Bengal, **established on **January 15, 1784**, by **Sir William Jones**, a British lawyer and Orientalist, aimed to promote Oriental studies.
 
• Jones inaugurated the society with the first of a series of renowned discourses. A distinguished scholar from the **University of Oxford, Jones **arrived in Calcutta (now Kolkata) on** September 25, 1783, serving as a supreme court judge**.
 
• The society was formed shortly after his arrival, receiving support and encouragement from Warren Hastings, the governor-general of Bengal from 1772 to 1785, although he declined its presidency.
 
• Based in Kolkata, the Asiatic Society owns an impressive art collection featuring works by renowned artists such as Peter Paul Rubens and Joshua Reynolds.
 
• The society's library boasts around 100,000 volumes covering various subjects, while its Sanskrit section houses over 27,000 books, manuscripts, prints, coins, and engravings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Sir William Jones**, a British philologist and orientalist, served as a puisne judge on the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal.
 
• Renowned for his scholarship on ancient India, Jones is best remembered for proposing a relationship between European and Indo-Aryan languages, later recognized as the Indo-European languages.
 
• He attained Fellowship of the Royal Society on April 30, 1772, and became a member of The Club in 1773, eventually assuming the presidency in 1780.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jonathan Duncan** served as Governor of Bombay from December 27, 1795, until his passing in 1811.
 
• **Warren Hastings, **a British colonial administrator, held various significant positions, including the first Governor of the Presidency of Fort William (Bengal) and the initial Governor-General of Bengal from 1772 to 1785.
 
• **Sir Charles Eyre**, an administrator of the British East India Company, played a pivotal role as the founder of Fort William in Calcutta and served as its President.

__
 
• Nowruz is the **Iranian New Year**, which is widely known as the **Persian New Year** and is celebrated worldwide by some religious groups.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the first of **Farvardin – Zoroastrian calendar’s first month** and the onset of spring.
 
• Listed in **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity of India**, the festival is also known as **Navroj, Nowrouz, Navruz,Novruz, and Nevruz.**
 
• The festival commences at the vernal equinox stroke, the time when the sun passes through the equator. 
 
• It is celebrated in Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, India, Iran, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. 
 
• In India, it is mostly celebrated in **Gujarat and Maharashtra.**

• The tradition began long ago and is baptized after the Persian King, **Jamshed** who introduced the Parsi calendar. Thus, the name – Jamshed-i-Nowroz.
 
• **King Jamshed **was held on high for his **righteousness and truthfulness. **So, Parsis also celebrate the king during the festival signifying **walking on the virtuous path and living truthfully.**
 
• All over the world, the **Parsi community and various sects of Muslims (Sunni and Shia, both) celebrate Nowruz.**
 
• Parsis pray at **Atash Behram **(Fire of Victory- the highest fire grade of a fire that can be placed in a Zoroastrian fire temple as an eternal flame).

question: Which Indo-French structure is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Basilica of Bom Jesus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Basilica of Bom Jesus** is a renowned religious structure located in **Old Goa**, which was the former capital of **Portuguese India**.
 
• It is part of the **Churches and Convents of Goa**, which was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1986**. ***Hence, the statement regarding its UNESCO status is correct.***
 
• Construction of the basilica began in **1594** and was consecrated in **May 1605**. It stands as a landmark in the history of **Christianity** in **India**.
 
• The church is world-famous for housing the **mortal remains** of **St. Francis Xavier**, a co-founder of the **Society of Jesus** (Jesuits). The body is kept in a silver casket and is brought down for public viewing every **ten years**.
 
• Architecturally, it is one of the finest examples of **Baroque architecture** and **Manueline style** in **India**. It is the only church in **Goa** not covered with plaster on the outside, showcasing its **laterite** exterior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fort St. George:**
 
 
• Located in **Chennai** (formerly Madras), **Fort St. George** was the first **English** (British) fortress in **India**, founded in **1644**.
 
• It currently serves as the headquarters of the **Legislative Assembly** of **Tamil Nadu**. While historically significant, it is **not** a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Auroville Matrimandir:**
 
 
• The **Matrimandir** is situated in the center of **Auroville**, an experimental township in **Puducherry** (and parts of Tamil Nadu).
 
• It was designed by the **French architect Roger Anger** and is a symbol of **integral yoga** and human unity. Although **French** in its architectural origin, it does not hold the **UNESCO World Heritage** status. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Chandannagar Strand:**
 
 
• **Chandannagar** was a former **French colony** located in **West Bengal**. The **Strand** is a beautiful promenade along the **Hooghly River**, lined with **French colonial** buildings.
 
• Despite its deep **Indo-French** cultural roots and heritage value, it has not been inscribed as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**
 
 
• As of **2024**, **India** has **42** designated **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**, which include **34 cultural**, **7 natural**, and **1 mixed** site.
 
• The **Churches and Convents of Goa** (including the **Basilica of Bom Jesus** and **Se Cathedral**) are protected under the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**.
 
• The criteria for **UNESCO** inclusion for the **Goa** sites included their influence on the spread of **Manueline**, **Mannerist**, and **Baroque** art forms throughout **Asia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **"Indo-French"** in the question likely refers to the European colonial influence on Indian architecture. However, strictly speaking, the **Basilica of Bom Jesus** is of **Portuguese** origin, while **Auroville** and **Chandannagar** are the primary **French** heritage sites in **India**.
 
• The **Basilica** was elevated to the status of a **Minor Basilica** in **1946**, the first in **India** to receive such an honor.
 
• The interior of the church is highly decorated with **gilded altars** and carvings, contrasting with its simple, unplastered **red laterite** exterior.

question: Rani Karnaa was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi (1996) for her contribution to_
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rani Karnaa borne in 1939 in **Hyderabad, Sindh** (now in Pakistan).
 
• Rani Karnaa was a distinguished Indian classical dancer known for her expertise in Kathak.
 
• She trained under legendary **gurus such as Nrityacharya Narayan Prasad, Pandit Sunder Prasad, and Pandit Birju Maharaj.**
 
• Rani Karnaa was renowned for blending the **Jaipur and Lucknow gharanas**, creating a unique and aesthetically rich style.
 
• She received numerous accolades, including the **Padma Shri in 2014** and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1996.

**Kathak:**

 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of** Indian classical dance**, originating from the traveling bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• The dance form evolved during the **Bhakti movement**, incorporating stories of Hindu gods, particularly Krishna.
 
• It further developed under the patronage of **Mughal emperors, integrating Persian elements.**
 
• Kathak has **three main gharanas (schools)** - **Jaipur, Lucknow, and Banaras**.
 
• The Jaipur gharana emphasizes intricate footwork, while the Lucknow gharana focuses on facial expressions and graceful hand movements.

question:
Consider the following statements about 'Chronicle of a Corpse Bearer' by Cyrus Mistry:**
1) Won DSC Prize for depicting marginalized Parsi communities in Mumbai.

2) Received Booker Prize for narrative innovation and postcolonial themes.

3) Awarded Sahitya Akademi in 2015.

Which of the above statements is/are correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Statements 1 and 3 both are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The novel **Chronicle of a Corpse Bearer** was written by the acclaimed **Indian author** **Cyrus Mistry** and published in **2012**. It won the **DSC Prize for South Asian Literature** in **2014**. The book is noted for its deep and empathetic portrayal of the **Khandhia** community, who are the marginalized **corpse bearers** within the **Parsi community** in **Mumbai**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• While the novel received significant critical acclaim and international recognition, it did not receive the **Booker Prize**. The **Booker Prize** is a prestigious literary award for the best novel written in **English** and published in the **UK** or **Ireland**, but this specific work was not among its winners. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cyrus Mistry** was conferred with the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **2015** for this novel in the **English language** category. This award is one of the highest literary honors bestowed by the **Government of India**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The core logic of the question rests on identifying the specific literary honors received by **Cyrus Mistry** for his work that highlights the social stratification within the **Zoroastrian** faith. ***Hence, the correct answer is Statements 1 and 3 both are correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cyrus Mistry:** He is a **Mumbai-based** **playwright** and **novelist**. He is the younger brother of the famous author **Rohinton Mistry**. His writing often delves into the lives of the **Parsi** community, exploring themes of **marginalization** and **tradition**.
 
• **Book Summary:** The story is set in **pre-independence India** and follows **Phiroze Elchidana**, the son of a **Parsi priest**. Phiroze falls in love with **Sepideh**, the daughter of a **Khandhia**, and chooses to become a **corpse bearer** himself to marry her, thereby entering a life of **social exclusion** and **poverty**.
 
• **The Khandhia Community:** In the **Zoroastrian** tradition, **Khandhias** are those who carry the deceased to the **Towers of Silence** (**Doongerwadi**) for **excarnation**. Despite their vital religious role, they are often treated as **untouchables** within their own community and live in **segregated housing**.
 
• **DSC Prize for South Asian Literature:** This is an international literary prize awarded annually to writers of any **ethnicity** or **nationality**, provided the writing is about the **South Asian** region. **Cyrus Mistry** received the **$25,000** prize at the **Jaipur Literature Festival**.
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award:** Established in **1954**, it is a literary honor in **India**, which the **Sahitya Akademi** (India's National Academy of Letters) annually confers on writers of the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the **24 major Indian languages**, including **English**.
 
• **Location and Context:** The novel is primarily set in **Mumbai** (formerly **Bombay**) and provides a historical look at the **Parsi** customs and the **socio-economic** struggles of the **1940s**.

question: Which book by Anirudh Kanisetti, exploring the history of Southern India, was awarded the Yuva Puraskar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lords of the Deccan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book titled **Lords of the Deccan: Southern India from the Chalukyas to the Cholas** is authored by **Anirudh Kanisetti** and was released in the year **2022**.
 
• It was honored with the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar** in the **English** language category for the year **2023**.
 
• The book provides a vivid and comprehensive narrative of **Medieval South Indian history**, specifically focusing on the **Deccan** plateau and its powerful dynasties like the **Chalukyas**, **Rashtrakutas**, and early **Cholas**.
 
• The work covers a period of approximately **five centuries**, starting from the **6th Century CE**, and highlights how these empires shaped the cultural and political landscape of the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• It aims to challenge the **North-centric** view of **Indian history** by bringing the complex geopolitics and achievements of **Southern India** to the forefront of mainstream historical discourse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India After Gandhi:** This is a critically acclaimed historical non-fiction book written by the noted historian **Ramachandra Guha**, first published in **2007**, which details the history of **India** after it gained independence from **British rule** in **1947**. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• **The Anarchy: The Relentless Rise of the East India Company:** Authored by **William Dalrymple** and published in **2019**, this book explores the history of how the **British East India Company** seized control of vast tracts of **India** between **1756** and **1803**. *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*
 
• **Lords of the Deccan:** This work by **Anirudh Kanisetti** is the correct book that explores **Southern Indian** history and won the **Yuva Puraskar** in **2023**. *Hence, statement C is correct.*
 
• **The Argumentative Indian:** Published in **2005**, this is a collection of essays written by the **Nobel Prize** winning economist **Amartya Sen**, which focuses on **India's** intellectual history and its tradition of public debate and intellectual pluralism. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar** was instituted in the year **2011** to recognize and promote young Indian authors who are **35 years** of age or younger.
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi**, India's **National Academy of Letters**, was established on **12 March 1954** and functions as an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Culture**.
 
• The award for the **Yuva Puraskar** consists of a casket containing an engraved **copper plaque** and a cash prize of **Rs. 50,000**.
 
• **Anirudh Kanisetti** is also known for his popular history podcast, **Echoes of India**, which brings ancient **Indian history** to a modern digital audience.
 
• The book **Lords of the Deccan** was published by **Juggernaut Books** and has been praised for its cinematic storytelling style and rigorous academic research.

question: Which Indian leader received France's highest civilian award, the Legion of Honour, in 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** was conferred with the **Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour**, which is the highest civilian and military honor of **France**, in July **2023**.

• The award was presented to him by the French President **Emmanuel Macron** at the **Elysee Palace** in Paris.

• PM Modi became the **first Indian Prime Minister** to receive this prestigious award.

• The honor was bestowed during his two-day official visit to France, where he attended the **Bastille Day Parade** as the **Guest of Honour**.

• This recognition highlights the strengthening of the **strategic partnership** between India and France and acknowledges the Prime Minister's role in enhancing bilateral ties.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Legion of Honour** (Ordre national de la Légion d'honneur) was established by **Napoleon Bonaparte** in **1802**.

• It is the highest French order of merit, both military and civil, and is divided into five degrees: **Knight**, **Officer**, **Commander**, **Grand Officer**, and **Grand Cross**.

• The **Grand Cross** is the highest level within the order.

• Other notable international leaders who have received the Grand Cross include **Nelson Mandela**, **King Charles III**, and **Angela Merkel**.

• In 2023, PM Modi also received several other top international honors, including the **Order of the Nile** (Egypt) and the **Grand Companion of the Order of Logohu** (Papua New Guinea).

question: The Arjuna Award is given for excellence in which field?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sports**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arjuna Award**, officially known as the **Arjuna Awards for Outstanding Performance in Sports and Games**, is the second-highest sporting honour in **India**, after the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**.
 
• It was instituted in the year **1961** by the **Government of India** to recognize outstanding achievements in **National Sports**. The award is named after **Arjuna**, a primary protagonist from the ancient Indian epic, the **Mahabharata**, who was known for his mastery in archery and focus.
 
• As per the latest guidelines, to be eligible for the award, a sportsperson must have shown consistent outstanding performance at the **international level** for the preceding **four years**.
 
• In addition to performance, the sportsperson should have shown qualities of **leadership**, **sportsmanship**, and a sense of **discipline**.
 
• The award carries a **cash prize** of **₹15,00,000** (**15 Lakhs**), a **bronze statue** of **Arjuna** with his bow, and a **scroll of honour**. The cash prize was significantly increased from **₹5 lakh** to **₹15 lakh** in the year **2020**.
 
• The nominations for the award are received by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, and the selection is made by a committee headed by a retired **High Court** or **Supreme Court Judge** along with eminent sports personalities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**
 
 
• This is the **highest sporting honour** of **India**. It was formerly known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award**.
 
• It was instituted in **1991–1992**. The first recipient was the Chess Grandmaster **Viswanathan Anand**.
 
• The award includes a **cash prize** of **₹25,00,000** (**25 Lakhs**).
 
 
 
• **Dronacharya Award:**
 
 
• Instituted in **1985**, this award is given to **coaches** for their excellence in sports coaching.
 
• It honors those who have enabled athletes to achieve outstanding results in **international events**.
 
• The **Regular Category** award carries a prize of **₹10 lakh**, while the **Lifetime Category** carries **₹15 lakh**.
 
 
 
• **Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement:**
 
 
• Instituted in **2002**, it is awarded to individuals for their **lifetime contribution** to sports development.
 
• It is named after the legendary Indian hockey player **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• The award includes a **statue**, a **certificate**, and a cash prize of **₹10,00,000**.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Day:**
 
 
• The **National Sports Awards** are typically presented by the **President of India** at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan** on **29th August** every year.
 
• This date marks the **birth anniversary** of **Major Dhyan Chand**, known as the "**Wizard of Hockey**."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The first recipients of the **Arjuna Award** in **1961** included **Salim Durani** for **Cricket**, **Sarbit Singh** for **Basketball**, and **Manuel Aaron** for **Chess**.
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** also awards the **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy** to the overall top-performing **University** in inter-university tournaments.
