__
 
• The primary objective of the **Gaganyaan Mission** is to demonstrate **India's** indigenous capability to undertake human spaceflight to **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**. It aims to send a **3-member crew** to an altitude of **400 km** for a mission duration of **3 days**. ***Hence, option B is correct.***
 
• The mission is being spearheaded by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and was first formally announced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** during his **Independence Day speech** in **2018**.
 
• The launch vehicle identified for the **Gaganyaan** mission is the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-III)**, which was previously known as **GSLV Mk III**. This heavy-lift launcher consists of **solid, liquid, and cryogenic stages** and has been re-configured to meet **human-rating** requirements.
 
• Success in this mission will make **India** the **fourth country** in the world to launch a manned space mission, following the **Soviet Union (now Russia)**, the **United States**, and **China**.
 
• The mission also involves a safe return to **Earth**, where the **Crew Module** will splash down in **Indian sea waters** (likely the **Arabian Sea**) after re-entry into the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Crew Selection and Training:** The four designated **Gaganyatris** (astronaut-designates) are **Group Captain Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair**, **Group Captain Ajit Krishnan**, **Group Captain Angad Pratap**, and **Wing Commander Shubhanshu Shukla**, all from the **Indian Air Force (IAF)**. They underwent rigorous training at the **Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center** in **Russia** and are now training at **ISRO's Astronaut Training Facility** in **Bengaluru**.
 
• **Vyommitra (The Humanoid):** Before the actual crewed flight, **ISRO** will launch uncrewed missions carrying a **female robot humanoid** named **Vyommitra**. Her role is to simulate human functions, monitor **module parameters**, and alert about **environmental changes** within the capsule to ensure crew safety.
 
• **Human Rated LVM3 (HLVM3):** This specialized version of the **LVM3** rocket includes a **Crew Escape System (CES)** powered by high-burn rate solid motors, ensuring the **Crew Module** can be pulled away to safety in case of any **launch pad** or **ascent-phase** emergencies.
 
• **Orbital Module:** It consists of two parts: the **Crew Module (CM)**, which is the habitable space with an **Earth-like environment** for the astronauts, and the **Service Module (SM)**, which provides the necessary **propulsion** and **power** during the orbital phase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Test Vehicle Missions (TV-D1):** On **October 21, 2023**, **ISRO** successfully conducted the **Flight Test Vehicle Abort Mission-1 (TV-D1)** from **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**. This test validated the performance of the **Crew Escape System** at a **Mach number of 1.2**.
 
• **Future Space Milestones:** The **Gaganyaan** mission is a foundational step toward establishing the **Bharatiya Antariksha Station (BAS)**, a permanent Indian space station planned for **2035**, and the eventual goal of landing an **Indian on the Moon** by **2040**.
 
• **Critical Technologies:** Development involves **Thermal Protection Systems** to withstand high temperatures during re-entry, **Life Support Systems** to provide **Oxygen** and remove **Carbon Dioxide**, and **Navigation, Guidance, and Control (NGC)** systems.
 
• **Economic and Scientific Impact:** The project, with a budget of approximately **₹9,023 Crore**, encourages **industrial participation** (both **public and private**) and inspires **STEM** education among the youth in **India**.

subject: GK
question: How does India's space technology contribute to national development goals such as disaster management and agriculture?

options.text: By using satellite data for weather forecasting, crop monitoring, and resource mapping
Through manned missions to collect physical data
Via real-time social media alerts during emergencies
Through laser-based ground scanning from space stations

solution:
The correct answer is __**By using satellite data for weather forecasting, crop monitoring, and resource mapping**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's space technology, spearheaded by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, is primarily application-oriented, focusing on socio-economic development through **Remote Sensing** and **Communication** satellites.
 
• The use of satellite data for **Weather Forecasting**, **Crop Monitoring**, and **Resource Mapping** is the core mechanism through which space technology aids national goals. Satellites like **INSAT-3D** and **INSAT-3DR** provide atmospheric data every **15 minutes**, enabling precise tracking of **Cyclones** and **Monsoon** patterns. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Manned missions, such as the **Gaganyaan** project, are designed to demonstrate human spaceflight capability and conduct microgravity experiments. While scientifically significant, they are not the primary operational tool for routine **Agriculture** or **Disaster Management**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Real-time social media alerts are a communication tool used by agencies like **NDRF**, but they represent a ground-level application rather than the core space technology itself. Space technology provides the **Satellite Bandwidth** (via **GSAT** series) for internet connectivity, but social media is not the direct space-based solution for these goals. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Laser-based ground scanning (**LiDAR**) is typically performed from aerial platforms (aircraft). While **ISRO** uses **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)** from space for **Flood Mapping** and topography, routine 'laser scanning from space stations' is not the standard method for India's developmental objectives. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Agriculture Applications:** The **FASAL** (Forecasting Agricultural output using Space, Agro-meteorology and Land based observations) project uses **Resourcesat-2** data to provide production forecasts for major crops like **Rice**, **Wheat**, **Cotton**, and **Sugarcane**. Additionally, the **CHAMAN** project focuses on the **Horticulture** sector using **Geoinformatics**.
 
• **Disaster Management Support (DMS):** **ISRO**'s **DMS Programme** provides timely space-based inputs during **Floods**, **Cyclones**, **Drought**, **Forest Fires**, and **Landslides**. The **Bhuvan** geo-portal, launched in **2009**, allows users to visualize and analyze multi-sensor satellite imagery for disaster impact assessment.
 
• **NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation):** This independent regional navigation satellite system provides accurate position information service to users in **India** and the region extending up to **1500 km** from its boundary. It is used for sending **Emergency Alert Messages** to fishermen regarding high wave alerts and **Cyclone** warnings.
 
• **Resource Mapping:** **Remote Sensing** satellites are used for **Groundwater** prospecting, **Forest Cover** monitoring, and **Watershed** development. The **National Agricultural Drought Assessment and Monitoring System (NADAMS)** provides near real-time information on prevalence and severity of **Drought** at district and sub-district levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NRSC (National Remote Sensing Centre):** Located in **Hyderabad**, this center is responsible for satellite data acquisition, processing, and dissemination. It plays a vital role in **Disaster Management** by providing high-resolution maps to state and central agencies.
 
• **Satellite Constellation:** India operates one of the largest constellations of **Remote Sensing** satellites in the world, including the **IRS (Indian Remote Sensing)** series, **Cartosat**, and **Risat**. **Risat-1** and **Risat-2** are particularly useful for **Flood** monitoring as they can see through clouds using **Radar Imaging**.
 
• **Impact Data:** Precise **Cyclone** track predictions using space-based inputs have helped reduce the mortality rate during extreme weather events by over **90%** in the last two decades, as seen during **Cyclone Phailin (2013)** and **Cyclone Amphan (2020)**.
 
• **ISRO Foundation:** Established on **15 August 1969**, with headquarters in **Bengaluru**, **ISRO** has evolved from a scientific research body to a critical pillar of **India's** national security and developmental infrastructure.

question: What is the primary role of the INSAT-3DS satellite launched under the GSLV-F14 mission?

options.text: To monitor India's defense satellite communication network.
To provide direct-to-home broadcasting services across rural India.
To enhance meteorological observations and aid in weather forecasting.
To serve as a backup for interplanetary deep-space communications.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To enhance meteorological observations and aid in weather forecasting.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **INSAT-3DS** satellite is a follow-on mission of the third-generation meteorological satellite series from India, specifically designed to enhance **meteorological observations** and monitor land and ocean surfaces.

• Launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on February 17, 2024, using the **GSLV-F14** launch vehicle, its primary objective is to provide continuity of services to existing operational satellites like **INSAT-3D** and **INSAT-3DR**.

• The satellite is equipped with advanced payloads, including a **6-channel Imager** and a **19-channel Sounder**, which are crucial for capturing high-resolution images and vertical profiles of the atmosphere (temperature and humidity).

• It plays a vital role in **weather forecasting**, providing data for **disaster warning**, and monitoring environmental changes across the Indian subcontinent and surrounding oceanic regions.

• The mission is fully funded by the **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)** to improve the accuracy of weather predictions and climate research.

**Additional Information__**

question:
Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): The Reusable Launch Vehicle - Technology Demonstrator (RLV-TD) program by ISRO is a cornerstone for India's future reusable space access capabilities.
Reason (R): RLV-TD missions are specifically designed to test crucial technologies like hypersonic flight, autonomous landing systems, and the structural resilience of a winged re-entry vehicle.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Assertion (A)** is true because the **Reusable Launch Vehicle - Technology Demonstrator (RLV-TD)** is a series of technology demonstration missions that serve as the first step towards realizing a **Two-Stage-to-Orbit (TSTO)** fully reusable vehicle. It is considered a cornerstone because it aims to drastically reduce the cost of access to space by recycling the launch vehicle.

• **Reason (R)** is true because the primary objective of the **RLV-TD** program is to evaluate and validate various technologies. These include **hypersonic flight**, **autonomous landing**, **powered cruise flight**, and the use of **air-breathing propulsion**. The vehicle is designed to survive the high temperatures of **re-entry** using advanced thermal protection systems.

• **R is the correct explanation of A** because the successful testing and validation of these specific technologies (hypersonic flight, autonomous landing, and structural resilience) are exactly what make the **RLV-TD** program the foundational 'cornerstone' for India's future reusable space capabilities. Without mastering these technical aspects, a reusable system cannot be built.

**Additional Information__**

• The first experimental flight of **RLV-TD**, known as the **HEX-01 (Hypersonic Flight Experiment)**, was successfully conducted by **ISRO** on **May 23, 2016**, from Sriharikota.

• In **April 2023**, ISRO successfully conducted the **RLV LEX (Landing Experiment)** at the Aeronautical Test Range in **Chitradurga, Karnataka**, where the vehicle performed an autonomous landing under conditions similar to a space re-entry.

• The ultimate goal of the **RLV** program is to bring down the cost of launching payloads into **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** to about 1/10th of the current cost, which is approximately **$20,000 per kg**.

• The configuration of **RLV-TD** resembles an aircraft, combining the complexity of both a **launch vehicle** and an **aircraft**.
</ul

question: Which of these missions will put India among the select few nations having technology for reusable launch vehicles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**RLV-LEX**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **RLV-LEX** stands for **Reusable Launch Vehicle Autonomous Landing Mission**. It is a landmark mission by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** designed to develop technologies for a fully reusable rocket. **Hence, this option is correct.**

• The mission was successfully conducted on **April 2, 2023**, at the **Aeronautical Test Range (ATR)** in **Chitradurga**, **Karnataka**. This feat made **India** one of the few nations, alongside the **USA**, **Russia**, and **China**, to master autonomous landing technology for space vehicles.

• **SPOT-7** is a high-resolution **Earth observation satellite** from **France**, launched by **India** in **2014** using the **PSLV-C23** rocket. It is a commercial satellite mission and does not involve reusable launch vehicle technology. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

• **PSLV-C58** is an expendable launch mission that successfully placed the **XPoSat** (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) into orbit on **January 1, 2024**. It uses traditional rocket technology where the stages are not recovered. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

• **RISAT-2** is an **Indian** radar imaging satellite launched in **2009** to provide all-weather surveillance and disaster management support. It is an orbital asset rather than a launch vehicle technology demonstrator. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **RLV-TD** (Technology Demonstrator) program is a series of experimental missions by **ISRO** aimed at developing a **Two-Stage-to-Orbit (TSTO)** fully reusable launch vehicle.

• The primary objective of developing **RLV** technology is to achieve **low-cost access to space**. By reusing the launch vehicle multiple times, the cost of space missions can be reduced by nearly **80%**.

• During the **RLV-LEX** experiment, a prototype named **Pushpak** was carried to an altitude of **4.5 km** by an **Indian Air Force Chinook helicopter** and released mid-air to simulate a vehicle returning from space.

• The vehicle utilized advanced indigenous technologies, including a **Radar Altimeter**, **Pseudolite** navigation system, and **Integrated Navigation, Guidance, and Control** systems to land autonomously on a runway.

• The landing occurred at a high speed of approximately **350 km/h**, demonstrating the precision of **India's** aerospace engineering and autonomous control software.

**Important Points__**

• On **March 22, 2024**, **ISRO** successfully completed the **RLV-LEX-02** mission, which was the second autonomous landing test. This mission tested the vehicle's ability to correct its flight path and land under more challenging initial conditions.

• The **Pushpak** vehicle is equipped with **Thermal Protection Systems (TPS)** to protect its structure from the intense heat generated during atmospheric re-entry from orbit.

• The success of these missions is a critical stepping stone toward the **Orbital Re-entry Experiment (ORE)**, where a vehicle will be launched into orbit and then brought back to land on a designated runway.

• Developing reusable rockets is a global trend, with organizations like **SpaceX** already utilizing reusability to dominate the commercial launch market. **India's** progress ensures it remains competitive in the global space economy.
</ul

subject: GK
question: What is the primary objective of India's Aditya-L1 mission?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Observe solar activity**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The primary objective of the **Aditya-L1** mission is to **observe solar activity** and provide a comprehensive study of the **Sun's atmosphere**. This includes investigating the **photosphere**, **chromosphere**, and the **outermost layers (corona)**. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*

• It is **India's first dedicated space mission** for **solar observations**, launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**. The mission is designed to solve mysteries related to **coronal heating**, **coronal mass ejections (CME)**, **pre-flare**, and **flare activities**.

• The spacecraft is positioned in a **halo orbit** around the **Lagrange Point 1 (L1)** of the **Sun-Earth system**. This point is located approximately **1.5 million kilometers** away from **Earth**, which is about **1%** of the total **Sun-Earth distance**.

• Placing the satellite at the **L1 point** provides the major advantage of viewing the **Sun** continuously without any **occultation** or **eclipses**. This allows for uninterrupted monitoring of **solar flares** and their impact on **space weather**.

• The mission carries **seven scientific payloads**. Four of these are for **remote sensing** of the **Sun** (observing light), and three are for **in-situ** studies (measuring particles and fields) at the **L1 point**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Launch Details:** The **Aditya-L1** spacecraft was launched on **September 2, 2023**, from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota**. It was carried by the **PSLV-C57** rocket, which is the **XL version** of the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle**.

• **Payload Functions:** The **Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC)** is the most crucial instrument, designed to study the **solar corona**. The **Solar Ultra-violet Imaging Telescope (SUIT)** observes the **photosphere** and **chromosphere** in the **200-400 nm** wavelength range.

• **Particle Studies:** The **Aditya Solar wind Particle Experiment (ASPEX)** and **Plasma Analyser Package For Aditya (PAPA)** are designed to study the **solar wind** and **energetic ions**, providing data on their **energy distribution**.

• **Magnetometer:** The mission also includes an **Advanced Tri-axial High Resolution Digital Magnetometer** to measure the low-intensity **interplanetary magnetic fields** at the **L1 point**.

• **Space Weather Impact:** Understanding **solar activity** is vital because **solar storms** can damage **satellites**, disrupt **GPS navigation**, and affect **power grids** on **Earth**.

**Important Points__**

• **Lagrange Points:** These are specific locations in space where the **gravitational pull** of two large masses (like the **Sun** and **Earth**) precisely equals the **centripetal force** required for a small object to move with them. There are **five Lagrange points** (**L1 to L5**).

• **Mission Duration:** The **Aditya-L1** mission has an intended operational life of **five years**, though many **ISRO** missions often exceed their planned lifespan due to efficient fuel management.

• **Global Context:** With this mission, **India** joins an elite group of space agencies, including **NASA** (USA) and **ESA** (Europe), that have successfully sent probes to study the **Sun** from the **L1 point**.

• **Comparison with Other Options:** Studying **Earth's atmosphere** is usually the role of **Earth Observation Satellites (EOS)**. Exploring the **Moon's surface** was the objective of the **Chandrayaan** missions, and mapping **Mars** was the goal of the **Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)**.
</ul

question: In 1887, whose experiment was an attempt to find the velocity of the Earth with respect to the hypothetical luminiferous ether?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Michelson and Morley**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Albert Michelson and Edward Morley** conducted the **Michelson–Morley experiment** in **1887** with the aim of measuring the **Earth's velocity relative to the luminiferous ether**.
 
• This experiment had its roots in an earlier study conducted by A.A. Michelson in Germany during 1880–81.
 
• The luminiferous ether was a theoretical concept hypothesized as the medium through which light waves propagate.
 
• In the 19th century, it was widely believed that just as water waves require a medium to travel through, light waves also required such a medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **James Clerk Maxwell, **a Scottish physicist, formulated the classical theory of electromagnetic radiation, which unified electricity, magnetism, and light as different manifestations of the same phenomenon.
 
• **Pieter Zeeman, **a Dutch physicist, shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Hendrik Lorentz for discovering the Zeeman effect, which describes the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field.
 
• **Hendrik Antoon Lorentz,** also a Dutch physicist, shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pieter Zeeman for their joint discovery and theoretical explanation of the Zeeman effect, and made significant contributions to the theory of electromagnetism and the electron theory of matter.

question: Which of the following does NOT belong to class Insects?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Scorpion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Scorpion **does NOT belong to class Insects.
 
• **Scorpions **are **arachnids characterized **by **their eight legs** and **nocturnal carnivorous habits**.
 
• They **inhabit diverse environments, **ranging from deserts and plains to savannas, forests, rainforests, and even caves.
 
• One unique feature of scorpions among arachnids is their method of reproduction. Unlike most other arachnids, which lay eggs, scorpions give birth to live young.
 
• This reproductive strategy is known as ovoviviparity, where the eggs develop and hatch inside the female's body, and the young are then born live.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Insects,** derived from the Latin term "insectum," are hexapod invertebrates of the** class Insecta**.
 
• They have a chitinous exoskeleton, a three-part body (head, thorax, and abdomen), three pairs of jointed legs, compound eyes, and a pair of antennae.
 
• They are the largest group within the arthropod phylum and the most diverse group of animals, with more than a million described species, representing more than half of all animal species.
 
• Most insects reproduce by laying eggs. The insect nervous system consists of a brain and a ventral nerve cord.

• **Viniculture** refers to the process of **creating wine from grapes.**
 
• **China **was the world's top grape producer, accounting for **16.9% of global production.**
 
 
 
• **Floriculture:**
 
 
• The study of** growing and marketing flowers** and** foliage plants** is known as floriculture or flower farming.
 
• Floriculture is the cultivation of flowering and attractive plants for direct sale or as raw materials in the **cosmetics and perfume industries**, as well as in the** pharmaceutical industry.**

question: Spongilla is an example of ______ water sponge.
solution:
The correct answer is **__fresh.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Spongilla is a freshwater sponge.
 
• It is a member of the family Spongillidae.
 
• It is generally found in lakes, ponds, and slow streams.
 
• Sponges belong to the phylum Porifera. They are generally marine and mostly asymmetrical animals.
 
• These are primitive multicellular animals and have a cellular level of organization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sponges have a water transport or canal system. Water enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into a central cavity, spongocoel, from where it goes out through the osculum.
 
• This pathway of water transport is helpful in food gathering, respiratory exchange, and removal of waste. Choanocytes or collar cells line the spongocoel and the canals.
 
• Digestion is intracellular. The body is supported by a skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibres.
 
• Sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite), i.e., eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual.
 
• Sponges reproduce asexually by fragmentation and sexually by the formation of gametes.
 
• Fertilization is internal and development is indirect having a larval stage that is morphologically distinct from the adult.

question: Which of the following was discovered by GN Ramachandran?

options.text: Fluid mosaic model of a cell

solution:
The correct answer is __**Triple helical structure of collagen.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **G.N. Ramachandran** is renowned for his significant contributions to biochemistry, particularly for elucidating the triple helical structure of collagen.
 
• His work established that collagen, a key structural protein in connective tissues, consists of** three polypeptide chain**s that form a right-handed triple helix.
 
• The discovery of collagen's structure has** implications for medicine**, particularly in understanding diseases related to connective tissues.
 
• Ramachandran's work has earned him recognition as a **pioneer in structural biology,** influencing subsequent research in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluid Mosaic Model of a Cell:**

 
 
• Proposed by **Singer and Nicolson in 1972**, this model describes the cell membrane as a dynamic and flexible structure with a mosaic of various proteins floating in or on the fluid lipid bilayer.
 
• It highlights the importance of membrane proteins in functions such as signaling, transport, and maintaining cell shape.
 
 
 
• **Plasma Membrane:**
 
 
• The plasma membrane is the** outer boundary of the cell **that separates its interior from the external environment.
 
• Composed of a lipid bilayer with embedded proteins, it regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell, playing a crucial role in cell communication and homeostasis.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Bodies:**
 
 
• Also known as the **Golgi apparatus**, these organelles are involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• **Discovered by Camillo Golgi in 1898**, the Golgi apparatus is essential for processing molecules synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum.

question: Which of the following statements about nucleases and DNA polymerase I is INCORRECT?

options.text: Exonucleases remove the nucleotides from the ends
DNA Pol I does not have a 5'-to-3' exonuclease activity
First polymerase isolated in E. coli was DNA Pol I

solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA Pol I does not have a 5'-to-3' exonuclease activity**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **DNA Polymerase I (Pol I)** is a multifunctional enzyme that possesses three distinct activities: 5'-to-3' polymerase activity, 3'-to-5' exonuclease activity (for **proofreading**), and **5'-to-3' exonuclease activity**.

• The **5'-to-3' exonuclease activity** is a unique feature of DNA Pol I among the major E. coli polymerases, allowing it to remove **RNA primers** and replace them with DNA during replication and repair. Therefore, the statement that it lacks this activity is **incorrect**.

• **Exonucleases** are enzymes that catalyze the removal of nucleotides one by one from the **termini (ends)** of a DNA or RNA molecule.

• **Endonucleases** are enzymes that make cuts at specific or non-specific positions **internally** within the DNA strand, rather than at the ends.

• **DNA Polymerase I** was the **first DNA polymerase** to be isolated and characterized from **Escherichia coli** by **Arthur Kornberg** in 1956, for which he received the Nobel Prize.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Klenow fragment** is a large protein fragment produced when DNA Pol I is enzymatically cleaved by proteases like subtilisin; it retains the 5'-to-3' polymerase and 3'-to-5' exonuclease activities but **loses the 5'-to-3' exonuclease activity**.

• While DNA Pol I is essential for **DNA repair** and processing **Okazaki fragments**, **DNA Polymerase III** is the primary enzyme responsible for the bulk of **DNA replication** in E. coli.

• The 3'-to-5' exonuclease activity is critical for **high-fidelity** replication as it allows the enzyme to remove mismatched bases immediately after they are incorporated.
</ul

question: Which chromosome is involved in the production of ‘masked’ mRNAs for early development?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lampbrush chromosome**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lampbrush chromosomes** are involved in the production of 'masked' mRNAs for early development.
 
• These chromosomes are a special form of chromosome found in the growing oocytes (immature egg cells) of most animals, except mammals.
 
• The lampbrush chromosomes are characterized by their large size and distinctive appearance, which is due to the extensive looping of chromatin.
 
• They play a crucial role in gene transcription during early development, producing mRNAs that are stored and later used during embryogenesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Masked mRNAs** are mRNA molecules that are transcribed but not immediately translated into proteins; they are stored in the cytoplasm and translated at a later stage.
 
• The structure of lampbrush chromosomes allows for high levels of transcriptional activity, which is necessary for the rapid cell divisions and developmental processes in early embryogenesis.
 
• Lampbrush chromosomes were first observed by Walther Flemming in 1882, and their detailed structure was later described by Ruckert in 1892.
 
• The study of lampbrush chromosomes has provided significant insights into the organization and function of chromatin and the regulation of gene expression.

question: What is the main objective of the 'Genome India Project'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Map genetic diversity of Indians**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• The **Genome India Project (GIP)** is a national mission launched by the **Department of Biotechnology (DBT)**, Ministry of Science and Technology, to sequence the whole genomes of the Indian population.

• The primary objective is to create a **comprehensive database** of genetic variations by mapping the **genetic diversity** of India's vast and diverse population, which consists of over **4,600 distinct groups**.

• By sequencing **10,000 genetic samples** from citizens across the country, the project aims to build a **'reference genome'** specific to Indians, which will help in understanding the nature of diseases at a genetic level.

• This project is crucial because most existing global genetic databases are based on **Caucasian populations**, which do not accurately represent the unique genetic makeup of the Indian subcontinent.

• The mapping helps in identifying **genetic predispositions** to various diseases like diabetes, cardiovascular disorders, and rare genetic conditions, enabling the development of **Precision Medicine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The project involves a collaboration of **20 premier institutions** across India, led by the **Centre for Brain Research** at the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)**, Bengaluru.

• In **March 2024**, the Government of India announced the successful **completion** of sequencing 10,000 genomes under this project.

• The initiative is inspired by the **Human Genome Project (HGP)**, an international scientific research project that mapped the entire human genome between 1990 and 2003.

• India is often referred to as the **world's largest genetic laboratory** due to its history of **endogamy** (marrying within the same community), which has preserved specific genetic traits and mutations within different groups.
</ul

question: What happens during the process of transcription in cells?

options.text: DNA is replicated into identical copies
Proteins are folded into functional shapes

solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA is converted into RNA**__.

• **Transcription** is the biological process where the **DNA sequence of a gene is copied into RNA**. It is the first step in gene expression.
 
• The enzyme **RNA polymerase** plays a central role in this process by binding to the DNA at the promoter region and synthesizing a complementary strand of RNA.
 
• In transcription, the DNA strand used as a template is called the **template strand**, while the complementary strand is referred to as the **coding strand**.
 
• The result of transcription is a single-stranded RNA molecule that is complementary to the DNA template strand. This RNA can be **messenger RNA (mRNA)**, **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)**, or **transfer RNA (tRNA)**, depending on the gene being transcribed.
 
• Transcription occurs in the nucleus

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• **Sclerenchyma** is the permanent plant tissue that makes the plant hard and stiff. The **husk of a coconut** is made of sclerenchymatous tissue.

• The cells of **Sclerenchyma** tissue are **dead**, long, and narrow. They lack a nucleus and cytoplasm at maturity.

• The cell walls are greatly thickened with **lignin**, a chemical substance that acts as cement and hardens them, providing structural rigidity.

• **Parenchyma** consists of living cells with thin cell walls and is primarily responsible for **food storage** and photosynthesis. It is the most common simple permanent tissue.

• **Collenchyma** provides **flexibility** and mechanical support to plant parts like the petiole and young stems, allowing them to bend without breaking.

• **Xylem** is a complex permanent tissue responsible for the **conduction of water** and minerals from the roots to the leaves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sclerenchyma** tissue is found in stems, around vascular bundles, in the veins of leaves, and in the hard covering of **seeds and nuts**.

• There are two main types of sclerenchyma cells: **Fibers** (elongated cells often used commercially in making ropes and mats) and **Sclereids** (short, thick cells that give the gritty texture to fruits like pears).

• **Lignin** deposition is so thick in some sclerenchyma cells that there is no internal space (lumen) left inside the cell.

• Plant tissues are broadly classified into **Meristematic tissues** (capable of cell division) and **Permanent tissues** (mature cells that have lost the ability to divide).
</ul

subject: GK
question: Which of the following statements correctly describes how unicellular organisms obtain their food?

options.text: All unicellular organisms use a mouth-like structure for food intake
Unicellular organisms like Amoeba use pseudopodia, while Paramecium uses cilia to direct food into a fixed spot
Unicellular organisms such as Amoeba and Paramecium absorb food randomly from all over the cell surface.
Unicellular organisms digest food externally before taking it into their bodies.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Unicellular organisms like Amoeba use pseudopodia, while Paramecium uses cilia to direct food into a fixed spot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amoeba** is a **unicellular organism** that does not have a fixed shape or a dedicated mouth. It obtains food by extending its **cell membrane** into temporary **finger-like projections** called **pseudopodia** (false feet). These **pseudopodia** surround the **food particle** and fuse to form a **food vacuole**. *Hence, the statement regarding Amoeba in the correct option is accurate.*
 
• **Paramecium**, another **unicellular organism**, has a more **complex structure** with a **definite shape** (often described as **slipper-shaped**). Unlike Amoeba, it takes in food at a **specific spot** called the **oral groove** or **cytostome**. It uses **cilia**, which are **thousands of tiny hair-like structures** covering its **entire surface**, to create a current that sweeps **food particles** toward this fixed spot. *Hence, the statement regarding Paramecium in the correct option is accurate.*
 
• The statement claiming that all **unicellular organisms** use a **mouth-like structure** for food intake is **incorrect**. Organisms like **Amoeba** can ingest food from **any part** of their surface by forming **pseudopodia**, proving that a **permanent mouth** is not a universal feature of all single-celled life. *Hence, the first statement in the options is incorrect.*
 
• The suggestion that **unicellular organisms** like **Amoeba** and **Paramecium** absorb food **randomly** from the **cell surface** is **incorrect**. While Amoeba is **flexible**, it actively **engulfs** prey rather than just **absorbing** it across the membrane, and Paramecium is **restricted** to taking food at a **specific location**. *Hence, the third statement in the options is incorrect.*
 
• The claim that these organisms **digest food externally** before ingestion is **incorrect**. Both Amoeba and Paramecium follow a **holozoic mode of nutrition**, where **digestion** occurs **intracellularly** (inside the cell) within a **food vacuole** using **hydrolytic enzymes**. *Hence, the fourth statement in the options is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Holozoic Nutrition**: This process involves five main stages: **Ingestion** (taking in food), **Digestion** (breaking down complex food), **Absorption** (taking in nutrients), **Assimilation** (using nutrients for energy/growth), and **Egestion** (expelling waste). Both **Amoeba** and **Paramecium** exhibit this **heterotrophic** lifestyle.
 
• **Intracellular Digestion**: Once the **food vacuole** is formed, **digestive enzymes** are secreted into it from the **cytoplasm**. These enzymes break down **carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids** into **simpler molecules**. These **soluble nutrients** then **diffuse** directly into the **cytoplasm** of the cell.
 
• **Contractile Vacuoles**: In addition to **food vacuoles**, these organisms possess **contractile vacuoles**. These structures are vital for **osmoregulation**, as they **collect** and **expel excess water** from the cell to prevent it from **bursting** in their **freshwater habitats**.
 
• **Waste Removal**: In **Amoeba**, the **undigested food** is moved to the **surface** and **discharged** at any point by the **rupturing** of the **cell membrane**. In **Paramecium**, **waste** is expelled through a **fixed point** on the **pellicle** known as the **anal pore** or **cytoproct**.
 
• **Structural Differences**: **Amoeba** belongs to the **Sarcodina** group and moves using **cytoplasmic streaming**. **Paramecium** belongs to the **Ciliata** group and is much **faster** due to the **coordinated beating** of its **cilia**, which also aids in **locomotion** through **aquatic environments**.
</ul

question: What is the role of the ribosome in a cell?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Protein synthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary role of the **ribosome** in a cell is **protein synthesis**. Ribosomes act as the cellular machinery that translates genetic code into functional proteins, which are essential for all life processes. ***Hence, the correct option is Protein synthesis.***
 
• Ribosomes are composed of two major components: **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and **proteins**. They consist of a **large subunit** and a **small subunit** that come together during the process of translation.
 
• In a cell, ribosomes can be found in two locations: either floating freely in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the surface of the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**. Proteins synthesized on the **RER** are typically destined for secretion or membrane insertion, while free ribosomes synthesize proteins for use within the **cytoplasm**.
 
• The process conducted by ribosomes is known as **Translation**. During this phase, the ribosome reads the sequence of the **messenger RNA (mRNA)** and, with the help of **transfer RNA (tRNA)**, assembles **amino acids** in the correct order to form a **polypeptide chain**.
 
• Ribosomes are universal organelles, meaning they are found in both **prokaryotic** (e.g., bacteria) and **eukaryotic** (e.g., plants and animals) cells, highlighting their fundamental importance in biology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Discovery and Characteristics:**
 
 
• Ribosomes were first observed in the mid-**1950s** by the Romanian-American cell biologist **George Palade** using an electron microscope. He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** in **1974** for this discovery.
 
• In **prokaryotes**, the ribosomes are smaller, known as **70S** ribosomes (consisting of **30S** and **50S** subunits). In **eukaryotes**, they are larger, known as **80S** ribosomes (consisting of **40S** and **60S** subunits). The **"S"** stands for the **Svedberg unit**, a measure of sedimentation rate.
 
 
 
• **Energy Production (Option A):**
 
 
• **Energy production** is the primary function of the **Mitochondria**, often called the "Powerhouse of the cell." This organelle generates **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)** through the process of **cellular respiration**. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 
 
• **Cell Division (Option C):**
 
 
• The process of **cell division** is facilitated by organelles like **centrioles** and **centrosomes** in animal cells, which help in the formation of **spindle fibers**. The **nucleus** plays the leading role by managing **DNA replication**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 
 
• **Transport of Substances (Option D):**
 
 
• The **transport of substances** within and out of the cell is handled by the **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** and the **Golgi Apparatus** (or Golgi Complex). The Golgi apparatus acts as a "post office," packaging and labeling proteins for their specific **locations**. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ribozymes:** While most enzymes are proteins, some **RNA** molecules in the ribosome possess catalytic activity. These are called **ribozymes**, and they are responsible for forming the **peptide bonds** between amino acids.
 
• **Antibiotic Target:** Because **bacterial (70S)** ribosomes differ in structure from **human (80S)** ribosomes, many **antibiotics** (such as **Tetracycline** and **Erythromycin**) work by specifically targeting and inhibiting bacterial ribosomes without harming the host's cells.
 
• **Polysomes:** Often, multiple ribosomes attach to a single **mRNA** strand simultaneously to produce multiple copies of a protein quickly; this complex is known as a **polyribosome** or **polysome**.
</ul

question: What is the function of the lysosomes in animal cells?

options.text: Break down waste materials and cellular debris

solution:
The correct answer is __**Break down waste materials and cellular debris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound organelles found in **animal cells**. They are often referred to as the "suicide bags" of the cell due to their ability to break down cellular components.
 
• The primary function of lysosomes is to break down **waste materials** and cellular debris. They contain hydrolytic enzymes that are capable of digesting proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids.
 
• Lysosomes play a critical role in **autophagy**, a process where damaged organelles and unnecessary cellular components are digested and recycled to maintain cellular health.
 
• They are also involved in the **immune response** by destroying pathogens and microorganisms that enter the cell through processes like phagocytosis.
 
• Lysosomes contribute to cellular homeostasis by removing potentially harmful substances and preventing the accumulation of toxic materials. *Hence, the correct answer is to break down waste materials and cellular debris.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Lysosomes:**

 
 
• Lysosomes are surrounded by a single phospholipid bilayer membrane and contain a variety of **acid hydrolases** that function optimally at a low pH (around 4.5-5).
 
• The acidic environment is maintained by proton pumps located on the lysosomal membrane.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Lysosomes:**
 
 
• Lysosomes are involved in processes like **autophagy**, where cellular components are recycled to maintain cell health.
 
• They also play a role in **endocytosis** and **phagocytosis**, where they digest substances that enter the cell.
 
• **Example:** Lysosomes in macrophages help break down pathogens during an immune response.
 
 
 
• **Differences in Plant and Animal Cells:**
 
 
• Plant cells generally lack lysosomes, but similar functions are performed by vacuoles.
 
• Animal cells rely on lysosomes for efficient waste management and recycling.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Functions of Lysosomes:**

 
 
• Lysosomes play a role in **apoptosis**, or programmed cell death, ensuring the removal of damaged or diseased cells.
 
• They are involved in the storage and release of enzymes required for breaking down extracellular materials.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Lysosomal Disorders:**
 
 
• **Tay-Sachs disease:** A genetic disorder caused by lysosomal enzyme deficiency leading to accumulation of harmful substances in neurons.
 
• **Pompe disease:** Caused by a deficiency in the enzyme required for glycogen breakdown within lysosomes.

question: Peeling, cutting or crushing onion tissue releases which enzyme that makes our eyes water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Allinases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **an onion's tissue is peeled, cut, or crushed,** it releases enzymes known as **allinases**. These enzymes facilitate the **conversion of certain molecules** into sulfenic acids.
 
• These sulfenic acids then undergo spontaneous rearrangement to form **syn-propanethial-S-oxide**, the chemical compound responsible for triggering tears. This process involves the conversion of the onion's sulfoxides into sulfenic acid by the allinase enzyme.
 
• The resulting sulfenic acid subsequently rearranges itself into syn-propanethial-S-oxide, which irritates the lachrymal glands in the eyes, leading to the release of tears.
 
• Moreover, the allinase enzyme also plays a role in the creation of another volatile compound called **lachrymatory factor (LF)**.
 
• This LF compound, generated by the action of allinase, diffuses into the air and interacts with the nerves of the cornea, inducing an involuntary tearing response.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Xylanases **constitute a category of enzymes responsible for the degradation of xylan, a complex polysaccharide abundant in plant cell walls.
 
• **Pectinases **are enzymes specialized in breaking down pectin, another polysaccharide component prevalent in the cell walls of plants.

question: In the context of movement of cells, exocytosis is the process by which:

options.text: cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane
cell death is brought about through a heavily regulated sequence of events
cells move waste materials from within the cell into the extracellular fluid
a cell takes in the fluids along with dissolved small molecules

solution:
The correct answer is __**cells move waste materials from within the cell into the extracellular fluid**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exocytosis** is a process used by cells to move materials from within the cell into the extracellular fluid.
 
• This process involves vesicles containing waste materials or other substances fusing with the cell membrane and releasing their contents outside the cell.
 
• Exocytosis is essential for various cellular functions, including neurotransmitter release, hormone secretion, and the removal of cellular waste.
 
• It is a form of active transport, requiring energy in the form of ATP to proceed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endocytosis** is the reverse process of exocytosis, where cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane.
 
• There are different types of endocytosis, including phagocytosis (ingestion of large particles) and pinocytosis (ingestion of fluids and dissolved small molecules).
 
• **Apoptosis** refers to programmed cell death, a regulated sequence of events that leads to the elimination of cells without releasing harmful substances into the surrounding area.
 
• Both exocytosis and endocytosis are critical for maintaining cellular homeostasis and communication.

subject: GK
question: The first peptide to be produced after wounding in the tomato plant is _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Systemin**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Systemin** is a small signaling peptide consisting of **18 amino acids** that mediates the systemic defense response in plants belonging to the **Solanaceae** family, particularly the **tomato** (Solanum lycopersicum).

• It was the first **polypeptide hormone** to be identified in plants, discovered in **1991** by **Clarence A. Ryan** and his research team.

• The peptide is synthesized from a larger precursor protein called **prosystemin**, which contains approximately **200 amino acids** and is located in the **cytosol** of vascular parenchyma cells.

• Upon **mechanical wounding** or **herbivore attack**, prosystemin is proteolytically cleaved by specific enzymes to release the active systemin peptide into the **apoplast** and **phloem**.

• Systemin travels through the **vascular system** to distal tissues, where it binds to a cell-surface receptor called **SR160** (a leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinase).

• This binding initiates the **octadecanoid pathway**, leading to the rapid production of **Jasmonic Acid (JA)**, which subsequently induces the expression of **protease inhibitor** genes to deter pests.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Jasmonic acid (JA)**:

• A **lipid-derived** phytohormone synthesized from **linolenic acid**.

• While central to wound signaling, it is a **cyclopentanone** derivative and not a peptide.

• **Salicylic acid (SA)**:

• A **phenolic** hormone primarily involved in defense against **biotrophic pathogens**.

• It plays a key role in **Systemic Acquired Resistance (SAR)**, often acting antagonistically to the jasmonic acid pathway.

• **Ricin**:

• A highly toxic **Type II ribosome-inactivating protein (RIP)** extracted from **castor beans** (Ricinus communis).

• It functions as a **cytotoxin** rather than a signaling peptide for wound response in tomato plants.

</ul

question: Which of the following cell organelles is involved in apoptosis?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apoptosis**, or programmed cell death, is a controlled process by which cells undergo self-destruction.
 
• This is crucial for maintaining health by eliminating damaged or unnecessary cells.
 
• The **mitochondria** play a central role in the **intrinsic pathway of apoptosis**.
 
• They release **cytochrome c** into the cytosol, which then triggers the activation of caspases (proteins that execute apoptosis).
 
• Once **cytochrome c** is released, it forms a complex with other proteins to activate **caspase-9**, which initiates a cascade that leads to cell death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Golgi Apparatus**

 
 
• The **Golgi apparatus is involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids **for secretion or delivery to other parts of the cell.
 
• While the Golgi is not directly involved in apoptosis initiation, it can be affected during cell death, leading to fragmentation.
 
• **Some proteins from the Golgi may also play a role in regulating apoptosis indirectly.**
 
• It is **central to processes like the production of lysosomes **and glycosylation of proteins.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**
 
 
• The **ER is responsible for the synthesis of proteins (rough ER) and lipids (smooth ER), as well as detoxification processes.**
 
• The** ER plays a crucial role in the unfolded protein respons**e (UPR) and ER stress-induced apoptosis.
 
• When misfolded proteins accumulate, the ER stress can trigger apoptosis via signalling pathways involving proteins like CHOP and caspase-12.
 
• It** also stores calcium, and calcium release from the ER can amplify apoptotic signals.**
 
 
 
• **Lysosome**
 
 
• **​** **Lysosomes are responsible for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris using digestive enzymes.**
 
• While not directly initiating apoptosis, lysosomal enzymes like cathepsins can be released during apoptosis, contributing to the degradation of cellular components.
 
• **Lysosomes are involved in autophagy,** a process that can promote cell survival or death, depending on the context.

subject: GK
question: What is the primary function of the xylem tissue in plants?

options.text: To transport products of photosynthesis from leaves to other parts of the plant
To transport water and minerals obtained from the soil
To provide energy to the plant

solution:
The correct answer is __**To transport water and minerals obtained from the soil**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a specialized type of **vascular tissue** in plants primarily responsible for the **upward conduction** of **water** and **dissolved minerals** from the roots to the leaves and stems.
 
• The transport in xylem is **unidirectional**, meaning it only moves from the soil/roots upwards to the aerial parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of four main components: **Tracheids**, **Vessels** (tracheary elements), **Xylem Parenchyma**, and **Xylem Fibers**.
 
• The transport of **photosynthetic products** (like sucrose) is the primary function of **Phloem**, not xylem.
 
• **Glucose synthesis** occurs in the **chloroplasts** of leaf cells through the process of **photosynthesis**, while energy is provided through **cellular respiration** in the mitochondria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Xylem also provides **mechanical strength** and structural support to the plant body due to the presence of **lignified** cell walls.
 
• Except for **xylem parenchyma**, all other xylem elements (tracheids, vessels, and fibers) are **dead cells** at maturity.
 
• The movement of water through the xylem is driven by physical forces such as **transpiration pull** (suction created by evaporation from leaves) and **root pressure**.
 
• In **Angiosperms**, vessels are the main water-conducting elements, whereas in **Gymnosperms**, tracheids are the primary conductors as they lack true vessels.

When a blood vessel is injured, platelets adhere to the site of injury and release clotting factors to form a blood clot, which helps prevent excessive bleeding. question: Rickets is caused by deficiency of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**vitamin D**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rickets** is a condition that affects bone development in children. It causes the bones to become soft and weak, which can lead to bone deformities.
 
• The primary cause of rickets is a **deficiency of vitamin D**.
 
• Vitamin D is essential for the absorption of calcium and phosphate from the diet, which are critical for healthy bone formation.
 
• Without sufficient vitamin D, the body cannot properly regulate calcium and phosphate levels, leading to the symptoms of rickets.
 
• Common sources of vitamin D include exposure to sunlight, which triggers vitamin D production in the skin, and dietary sources such as fatty fish, liver, and fortified foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rickets can also be caused by genetic factors, certain medical conditions, or malabsorption disorders that affect the body's ability to process vitamin D.
 
• Preventing rickets involves ensuring adequate intake of vitamin D through diet and supplementation, as well as sensible sun exposure.
 
• Treatment for rickets typically includes vitamin D and calcium supplements, and in severe cases, corrective surgery may be required to address bone deformities.
 
• Public health measures, such as fortifying foods with vitamin D, have been effective in reducing the incidence of rickets in many parts of the world.

question: Soybean products contain ________, which are similar to one of the human hormones.
solution:
The correct answer is __**phytoestrogen**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Soybean products** are a rich source of **phytoestrogens**, which are naturally occurring plant-derived compounds.

• Phytoestrogens have a chemical structure very similar to the human hormone **estrogen**, allowing them to bind to **estrogen receptors** in the body.

• The primary type of phytoestrogens found in soy are **isoflavones**, specifically **genistein** and **daidzein**.

• **Manihotoxin** is a cyanogenic glycoside found in **cassava** (Manihot esculenta) and is not related to soy or human hormones.

• **Taxol** (paclitaxel) is a **chemotherapy medication** used to treat various types of cancer, originally derived from the **Pacific yew tree**.

• **Morphine** is a potent **opiate analgesic** drug used for pain relief, extracted from the **opium poppy** plant.

**Additional Information__**

• Soy is unique among plant foods because it is a **complete protein**, meaning it contains all the **essential amino acids** that the human body cannot produce on its own.

• Because of their estrogen-like activity, soy isoflavones are often studied for their potential role in managing **menopause symptoms**, such as **hot flashes**.

• Regular consumption of soy has been linked to a reduced risk of **cardiovascular disease** by helping to lower **LDL (bad) cholesterol** levels.

• Other dietary sources of phytoestrogens include **flaxseeds**, **tofu**, **tempeh**, and various **legumes**.

question:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:**
Statement 1:** Poor nutrition among adolescents can result in stunted growth and deficiency diseases.**
Statement 2:** Proper diet plays a critical role in the healthy development of adolescents.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2 are correct**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adolescence** is a period of rapid **physical growth** and **biological changes**. During this stage, the body requires a high intake of nutrients to support the development of bones, muscles, and organs.
 
• **Statement 1** is correct because **poor nutrition** or **malnutrition** during these formative years prevents the body from reaching its full genetic potential. This leads to **stunted growth** (low height for age) and **deficiency diseases** such as **Anemia** (iron deficiency), **Night Blindness** (Vitamin A deficiency), or **Rickets** (Vitamin D deficiency).
 
• **Statement 2** is correct because a **balanced diet** provides the necessary energy and building blocks (proteins, vitamins, and minerals) required for the **healthy development** of the brain and body. Proper nutrition ensures that **puberty-related changes** occur normally and strengthens the **immune system**.
 
• Since both statements accurately describe the relationship between nutrition and adolescent health, the correct choice is that **both 1 and 2 are correct**.

question: Which of the following is the correct formula for calculating Body Mass Index (BMI)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**BMI = kg/m²**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BMI = kg/m²** is the correct formula for calculating Body Mass Index.
 
• BMI is a measure of body fat based on height and weight that applies to adult men and women.
 
• The formula divides an individual's weight in kilograms by their height in meters squared.
 
• This measurement is used to categorize individuals into various weight categories such as underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obesity.
 
• BMI is widely used by healthcare professionals to assess the risk of diseases associated with excess body fat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) provides BMI cut-off points for categorizing individuals.
 
• A BMI of less than 18.5 is considered underweight, 18.5-24.9 is normal weight, 25-29.9 is overweight, and 30 or greater is obese.
 
• BMI does not directly measure body fat but correlates well with more direct measures of body fat.
 
• It is important to consider other factors such as muscle mass, bone density, and overall body composition when interpreting BMI results.
 
• BMI may not be accurate for all populations, including athletes and older adults, due to differences in muscle and fat distribution.

question: Which foods is a good source of vitamin B12?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Meats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meats **is a good source of **vitamin B12**.
 
• This essential vitamin is primarily found in **animal-derived foods**, making meat an important dietary source for individuals following a non-vegetarian diet.
 
• Vitamin B12 plays a crucial role in various bodily functions, including the** formation of red blood cells, DNA synthesis, and nerve function.**
 
• However, for individuals following a vegetarian or vegan diet, other sources of vitamin B12, such as fortified foods or supplements, may be necessary to ensure adequate intake.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vitamin B12,** scientifically known as cobalamin, is a **water-soluble vitamin** that belongs to the group of B vitamins.
 
• It plays a crucial role in metabolism and is essential for various bodily functions.
 
• Animals require vitamin B12 as a **cofactor in DNA synthesis**, as well as in the metabolism of fatty acids and amino acids.
 
• In humans, vitamin B12 is vital for the normal functioning of the nervous system, primarily due to its involvement in the synthesis of myelin. It also contributes to the maturation of red blood cells in the bone marrow, thereby supporting the circulatory system.
 
• Unlike animals, plants do not require cobalamin for their metabolic processes and utilize enzymes that do not rely on it.
 
• Vitamin B12 is distinguished as the most chemically complex among all vitamins. Notably, for humans, it is the only vitamin that must be obtained from animal-derived foods or supplements.

question: Which of the following proteins is found in plasma?

The correct answer is __**Albumin.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasma's function** is to** transport nutrients, hormones, and proteins** throughout the body.
 
• It also transports **waste products of cell metabolism **from different tissues to the organs that detoxify and/or excrete them.
 
• Plasma is** 90% water,** with the remaining** 10% **consisting of ions, proteins, dissolved gases, nutritional molecules, and wastes.
 
• Plasma proteins are of **three different types**: **albumin, globulins, and fibrinogen.**
 
• **Albumin__:**
 __
 
• Albumin aids in the maintenance of the **blood's colloid osmotic pressure.**
 
• It is the **smallest **of the plasma proteins, but it accounts for the **majority of the total.**
 
• The blood's colloid osmotic pressure is critical for maintaining a** balance between the water inside the blood and the water** in the tissue fluid surrounding the cells.
 
• When **plasma proteins are lacking,** the water in the plasma leaks into the area around the blood vessels, causing **interstitial edema,** which is a symptom of liver illness, kidney disease, and malnutrition, among other things.
 
• Albumin also aids in the** transfer of a variety of molecules**, including **medicines, hormones, and fatty acids.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Leptin__:**

 __
 
• Leptin is a hormone released by** adipose tissue** (body fat) that helps your body maintain a healthy weight over time.
 
• This is accomplished by providing the **sensation of satiety**, which regulates appetite (feeling full).
 
• **Insulin stimulates** leptin secretion via a **posttranscriptional process** including the PI3K-PKBmTOR pathway, as well as other unidentified mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Keratin__:**
 __
 
• It is a** protein** that can be found in your** hair, skin, and nails.**
 
• Keratin is also found in the **organs and glands of the body**.
 
• Keratin protects **epithelial cells, strengthens the skin, strengthens internal organs, controls the growth of epithelial cells**, and maintains **elasticity** in the skin. It also holds + cells together and helps them combat mechanical stress.
 
 
 
• **Insulin__:**
 
 
• Insulin is a hormone created by your** pancreas** that controls the** amount of glucose** in your bloodstream at any given moment.
 
• It also helps **store glucose** in your liver, fat, and muscles.
 
• It regulates your** body's metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.**

question: What is the function of cytochrome P450?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Detoxification of xenobiotics**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytochrome P450 enzymes** play a crucial role in the **detoxification of xenobiotics**, which include drugs, pollutants, and other foreign substances.
 
• These enzymes are primarily found in the liver and are involved in the metabolism and elimination of various compounds from the body.
 
• The detoxification process often involves oxidation, which makes the xenobiotics more water-soluble and easier to excrete.
 
• In addition to detoxification, cytochrome P450 enzymes are also involved in the metabolism of endogenous substrates such as steroids and fatty acids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The cytochrome P450 superfamily includes a large number of enzymes that are classified based on their sequence similarities.
 
• These enzymes are named with the prefix "CYP" followed by a number indicating the gene family, a letter indicating the subfamily, and another number indicating the individual gene (e.g., CYP3A4).
 
• Inhibition or induction of cytochrome P450 enzymes can lead to significant drug interactions, affecting the efficacy and toxicity of medications.
 
• Understanding the function and regulation of cytochrome P450 enzymes is crucial for the development of new drugs and for predicting drug interactions.

question: What is the site of transmission of electric nerve impulses between two nerve cells (neurons) or between a neuron and a gland or muscle cell (effector)?
solution:
The Correct Answer is **"**__**Synapse**__**"**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**

__**Synapse**__** :**

__
 
• The site of transmission of electric nerve impulses between two nerve cells (neurons) or between a neuron and a gland or muscle cell (effector). 
 
• In the **central nervous system,** a synapse is a **small gap** at the end of a neuron that allows a signal to pass from one neuron to the next.
 
• Synapses are found where nerve cells **connect** with other nerve cells.
 
• Synapses are **vital to the transmission **of worried impulses from one neuron to some other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**__Dendrite__ :**

__
 
• **Dendrites** are **projections of a neuron** (nerve cell) that receive signals (information) from other neurons.
 
• The transfer of information from one neuron to another is achieved through chemical **signals and electric impulses**, that is, electrochemical signals.
 
• The information transfer is usually received at the dendrites through chemical signals, then it travels to the cell body (soma), continues along the neuronal **axon as electric** **impulses**, and it is finally transferred onto the next neuron at the synapse, which is the place where the two neurons exchange information through chemical signals.

**Axon__ :**

__
 
• **Axon**, also called **nerve fiber,** a portion of a nerve cell (neuron) that carries nerve impulses away from the cell body.
 
• A neuron typically has one axon that connects it with other neurons or with muscle or gland cells.
 
• Some axons may be quite long, reaching, for example, from the **spinal cord down to a toe.**
 
• Most axons of vertebrates are enclosed in a myelin sheath, which increases the speed of impulse transmission; some large axons may transmit impulses at speeds up to **90 meters (300 feet) per second.**

**Myelin sheath__ :**

 
• **Myelin** is an insulating layer or sheath that forms around nerves, including those in the** brain and spinal cord.**
 
• It is made up of protein and fatty substances.
 
• This** myelin sheath **allows electrical impulses to transmit quickly and efficiently along with the nerve cells.
 
• If myelin is damaged, these impulses slow down.
 
• This can cause diseases such as **multiple sclerosis.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8576078b4f34b84fee3bd1ea63d14cd935dcaf6140e60bad1dde13b723e33bce.png]

**Ileum**__** :**

• It is specifically responsible for the absorption of **vitamin B12** and the reabsorption of conjugated bile salts.
 
• The **ileum** is about **3.5 meters** (11.5 feet) long (or about three-fifths the length of the small intestine) and extends from the middle section of the small intestine to the ileocecal valve, which empties into the colon (large intestine). 

**Duodenum__ :**

• It is directly attached to the** pylorus of the stomach.**
 
• It has a** C-shape, **which is closely related to the head of the pancreas and consists of four sections: **superior**, **descending**, **horizontal**, and **ascending** parts.

solution:
The correct answer is** **__**oxygen; carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Respiratory failure **

 
 
• **Respiratory failure is a condition in which your blood doesn't have enough oxygen or has too much carbon dioxide.**
 
• Sometimes you can have both problems.
 
• When you breathe, your lungs take in oxygen. The oxygen passes into your blood, which carries it to your organs.
 
• Your organs, such as your heart and brain, need this oxygen-rich blood to work well.
 
• Another part of breathing is removing the carbon dioxide from the blood and breathing it out.
 
• Having too much carbon dioxide in your blood can harm your organs.
 
 
 
• **Causes of Respiratory Failure**
 
• Conditions that affect your breathing can cause respiratory failure.
 
• These conditions may affect the muscles, nerves, bones, or tissues that support breathing. The conditions are:
 
 
• Diseases that affect the lungs, such as COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), cystic fibrosis, pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, and COVID-19
 
• Conditions that affect the nerves and muscles that control breathing, such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), muscular dystrophy, spinal cord injuries, and stroke
 
• Problems with the spine, such as scoliosis (a curve in the spine). They can affect the bones and muscles used for breathing.
 
• Damage to the tissues and ribs around the lungs.
 
• An injury to the chest can cause this damage.
 
• Drug or alcohol overdose
 
• Inhalation injuries, such as from inhaling the smoke (from fires) or harmful fumes
 
 
 
• **Treatments for respiratory failure**
 
 
• Oxygen therapy
 
• Tracheostomy
 
• Ventilator
 
• Other breathing treatments, such as noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (NPPV),
 
• Fluids
 
• Medicines

• **Elephantiasis, or lymphatic filariasis, **is a painful and disfiguring condition. Infection with parasitic nematodes (roundworms) of the family Filariodidea is transmitted through **mosquito bites**.

An entire arm or leg may swell to several times its normal size resembling the thick, round appearance of an elephant's leg.
