subject: GK
question: What is the asteroid belt primarily composed of?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rocks and metals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **asteroid belt** is a vast, **torus-shaped** region in the solar system located between the orbits of the planets **Mars** and **Jupiter**.
 
• It is primarily composed of **rocks and metals**, which are remnants from the early **Solar System** formation approximately **4.6 billion years** ago. ***Hence, the option stating rocks and metals is correct.***
 
• The composition of these asteroids is mainly **silicate minerals** (rock) and **metals** such as **iron** and **nickel**.
 
• Unlike **comets**, which are composed significantly of **gases and ice**, asteroids in the main belt are mostly **volatile-poor** due to their proximity to the **Sun** during formation.
 
• The **gravitational pull** of **Jupiter** prevented these fragments from accreting into a full-sized planet, leaving them as **planetesimals** or fragments of shattered bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Asteroids**:
 
 
• **C-type (Carbonaceous)**: These are the most common, making up about **75%** of known asteroids. They consist of **clay** and **silicate rocks** and are dark in appearance.
 
• **S-type (Silicaceous)**: These account for about **17%** of the belt and are composed of **nickel-iron** mixed with **magnesium-silicates**.
 
• **M-type (Metallic)**: These are composed of nearly pure **nickel-iron** and are often considered the exposed **cores** of ancient, differentiated planetary bodies.
 
 
 
• **Major Bodies in the Belt**:
 
 
• **Ceres**: Discovered in **1801** by **Giuseppe Piazzi**, it is the largest object in the belt and is classified as a **dwarf planet**. It contains about **one-third** of the belt's total mass.
 
• **Vesta**: It is the second-most massive body and the brightest asteroid visible from **Earth**. It has a **differentiated** structure like **terrestrial planets**.
 
• **Pallas and Hygiea**: These are the third and fourth largest objects respectively, contributing significantly to the **mass distribution** within the region.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Density**:
 
 
• The **total mass** of the entire asteroid belt is estimated to be around **3% to 3.5%** of the mass of the **Moon**.
 
• Despite containing millions of asteroids, the region is mostly **empty space**. Spacecraft like **Pioneer 10**, **Voyager**, and **New Horizons** have passed through it without any collisions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location**: The belt resides between **2.2** and **3.2 astronomical units (AU)** from the **Sun**.
 
• **Kirkwood Gaps**: These are specific areas in the belt that are relatively empty due to **orbital resonance** with **Jupiter**, which clears out asteroids from certain distances.
 
• **Formation Theory**: The **Planetesimal Hypothesis** suggests that these bodies are leftovers that never merged into a planet due to **orbital perturbations** caused by **Jupiter's** massive **gravity**.
 
• **Scientific Missions**: **NASA's Dawn Mission** (launched in **2007**) provided the most detailed data on **Vesta** and **Ceres**, revolutionizing our understanding of **protoplanetary** evolution.
 
• **Meteorites**: Most **meteorites** that fall to **Earth** originate from collisions within the asteroid belt, providing direct **geological samples** of the early **Solar System**.
</ul

question: Which of the following celestial bodies is classified as a dwarf planet?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pluto**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Pluto** was officially reclassified from a major planet to a **dwarf planet** by the **International Astronomical Union (IAU)** in **August 2006**.

• The IAU defines a planet based on three criteria: it must **orbit the Sun**, it must have **sufficient mass** to assume a nearly round shape (hydrostatic equilibrium), and it must have **cleared the neighborhood** around its orbit.

• While Pluto orbits the Sun and is spherical, it has not cleared its orbital path of other debris, as it resides in the **Kuiper Belt** alongside many other icy objects.

• **Jupiter**, **Earth**, and **Venus** are all classified as **major planets** because they satisfy all three criteria, including clearing their respective orbital neighborhoods.

**Additional Information__**

• There are currently five recognized dwarf planets in our solar system: **Pluto**, **Eris**, **Haumea**, **Makemake**, and **Ceres**.

• **Ceres** is the smallest of the dwarf planets and the only one located in the **asteroid belt** between **Mars** and **Jupiter**.

• **Eris**, discovered in **2005**, is more massive than Pluto, which triggered the debate leading to the new definition of a planet.

• Dwarf planets are distinct from **natural satellites** (moons) because they orbit the Sun directly rather than orbiting another planet.

question:
Consider these facts about prominent solar system bodies:
1. Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a persistent anticyclonic storm.
2. Mars has two small, irregularly shaped moons.
Which of the above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jupiter** is the largest planet in our solar system and is famous for the **Great Red Spot**. This feature is a massive **anticyclonic storm**, meaning it rotates around a center of high atmospheric pressure.
 
• The storm is so large that it is wider than **Earth** and has been observed by astronomers for over **350 years**. It is located in **Jupiter's** southern hemisphere. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Mars**, the fourth planet from the **Sun**, has two natural satellites named **Phobos** and **Deimos**.
 
• These moons are significantly smaller than **Earth's Moon** and are **irregularly shaped** rather than spherical. Scientists believe they might be **asteroids** captured by **Mars's** gravity. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both 1 and 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jupiter and its Atmospheric Features:**
 
 
• **Jupiter** is a **Gas Giant** primarily composed of **Hydrogen** and **Helium**. It lacks a solid surface.
 
• The **Great Red Spot** exhibits wind speeds exceeding **400 km/h**. Recent data from **NASA's Juno mission** indicates that the storm's roots extend about **300 to 500 kilometers** deep into the planet's atmosphere.
 
• The planet has a very strong **magnetic field** and a total of **95 confirmed moons** as of **2023**, including the four large **Galilean moons**: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.
 
 
 
• **Mars and its Moons:**
 
 
• **Mars** is often called the **Red Planet** due to the prevalence of **Iron oxide** on its surface.
 
• **Phobos** is the larger and closer of the two moons, orbiting **Mars** three times a day. It is slowly spiraling toward the planet at a rate of **1.8 meters** every hundred years.
 
• **Deimos** is the smaller moon and orbits much further away. Both moons were discovered in **August 1877** by the American astronomer **Asaph Hall**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Physical Characteristics:**
 
 
• The **Great Red Spot** has been shrinking in size since the **19th century**. When **Voyager 1** and **Voyager 2** flew by in **1979**, it was much larger than it is today.
 
• While **Earth's Moon** is roughly **3,474 km** in diameter, **Phobos** is only about **22 km** across and **Deimos** is just **12 km** across.
 
 
 
• **Astronomical Significance:**
 
 
• The study of **Jupiter's** storms helps scientists understand **fluid dynamics** and atmospheric patterns on a massive scale.
 
• The **Mars Sample Return** and other future missions aim to study **Phobos** and **Deimos** to determine whether they are indeed captured **carbonaceous asteroids**.
 
 
</ul

question: What is the purpose of the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) mission?

options.text: To study the cosmic microwave background radiation
To provide insights into the sun
To monitor the Earth's magnetic field

solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide insights into the sun**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)** is a joint international project between the **European Space Agency (ESA)** and **NASA**.

• Launched on **December 2, 1995**, its primary objective is to investigate the **Sun** from its deep core to the outer **corona** and the **solar wind**.

• The observatory is stationed at the **First Lagrangian Point (L1)**, which is a gravitationally stable point located about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth toward the Sun. This position allows SOHO to maintain a **constant, uninterrupted view** of the Sun.

• The mission aims to solve three fundamental questions in solar physics: the **internal structure** of the Sun, the mechanism behind the **heating of the solar corona**, and where the **solar wind** is produced and how it is accelerated.

• SOHO provides real-time data that is essential for **space weather forecasting**, helping to predict solar storms that can affect satellites, telecommunications, and power grids on Earth.

**Additional Information__**

• SOHO is the most successful **comet hunter** in history, having discovered over **4,000 comets** (mostly 'sungrazing' comets) during its mission.

• The spacecraft is equipped with **12 scientific instruments**, including the **LASCO (Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph)**, which blocks the Sun's direct light to observe the much fainter corona.

• While originally designed for a **two-year mission**, SOHO has been operational for nearly **three decades**, allowing scientists to observe more than two full **11-year solar cycles**.

• The study of the **cosmic microwave background (CMB)** radiation mentioned in other options is the domain of missions like **COBE**, **WMAP**, and **Planck**, not SOHO.
</ul

question: Which of the following is classified as a galaxy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Andromeda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Andromeda** is a spiral galaxy located approximately **2.537 million light-years** from Earth. It is the closest large galaxy to the Milky Way.
 
• It is also known as **M31**, Messier 31, or NGC 224, and is part of the Local Group of galaxies, which includes the Milky Way, Triangulum, and around 54 other smaller galaxies.
 
• The Andromeda Galaxy is massive, containing approximately **one trillion stars**, which is more than twice the number of stars in the Milky Way.
 
• It is visible to the naked eye from Earth in areas with dark skies and is often studied to understand galaxy formation, structure, and dynamics.
 
• Unlike stars, constellations, or star systems, galaxies like Andromeda are vast collections of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sirius:**

 
 
• Sirius, also known as the **Dog Star**, is the brightest star in the night sky. It is located in the constellation Canis Major.
 
• Sirius is a binary star system consisting of Sirius A and its faint companion, Sirius B.
 
• It is approximately **8.6 light-years** away from Earth, making it one of the closest stars to our planet.
 
• Sirius is not a galaxy but a star system.
 
 
 
• **Orion:**
 
 
• Orion is a prominent constellation visible from Earth, famous for the **Orion Belt**, which consists of three aligned stars.
 
• It contains notable stars like **Betelgeuse** and **Rigel**, and features the Orion Nebula, which is a stellar nursery.
 
• Orion is not a galaxy but a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern.
 
 
 
• **Ursa Minor:**
 
 
• Ursa Minor, or the **Little Bear**, is a constellation known for containing the **North Star** (Polaris), which is a key navigational star.
 
• It is located near the celestial north pole and is used to find direction in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• Ursa Minor is not a galaxy but a constellation.
 
 
 
• **Galaxies:**
 
 
• A galaxy is a massive system consisting of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.
 
• The Milky Way (our galaxy), Andromeda, and Triangulum are part of the Local Group of galaxies.
 
• Galaxies come in different types, such as **spiral, elliptical, and irregular**, each with unique characteristics and structures.
 
• Galaxies are studied to understand cosmic phenomena like star formation, black holes, and dark matter.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Andromeda-Milky Way Collision:**

 
 
• The Andromeda Galaxy is on a collision course with the Milky Way, predicted to occur in approximately **4.5 billion years**.
 
• This event will result in the formation of a new galaxy, sometimes referred to as **Milkomeda**.
 
 
 
• **Galactic Research:**
 
 
• Studying galaxies like Andromeda helps scientists understand cosmic evolution, including the formation and lifecycle of stars.
 
• Research on galaxies contributes to insights into phenomena such as **supermassive black holes** and the distribution of **dark matter**.
 
 
 
• **Messier Objects:**
 
 
• Andromeda is part of the **Messier catalog**, which lists astronomical objects like galaxies, nebulae, and star clusters.
 
• These objects are frequently studied by astronomers due to their accessibility and scientific importance.

question: Which planet in our solar system is known as the "Morning Star" and the "Evening Star"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venus** is the **second planet** from the **Sun** and is the brightest natural object in Earth's night sky after the **Moon**.
 
• It is famously known as the **"Morning Star"** and the **"Evening Star"** because it is often visible shortly before **sunrise** or shortly after **sunset**. ***Hence, the statement regarding its nomenclature is correct.***
 
• **Venus** is frequently referred to as **"Earth's Twin"** due to its similar **size**, **mass**, **density**, and **bulk composition**. Its diameter is about **12,104 kilometers**, which is roughly **95%** of Earth's diameter.
 
• The planet possesses an incredibly dense atmosphere consisting of more than **96% Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**. This thick layer of gas traps heat in a runaway **greenhouse effect**, making it the **hottest planet** in the solar system with surface temperatures reaching approximately **462°C (864°F)**. ***Hence, the physical characteristics support its unique status among planets.***
 
• Unlike most other planets, **Venus** exhibits **retrograde rotation**, meaning it rotates on its axis from **east to west** (clockwise). Consequently, on **Venus**, the **Sun** would appear to rise in the west and set in the east.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mars**: Known as the **"Red Planet"** because of the **iron oxide** (rust) prevalent on its surface. It has two small moons, **Phobos** and **Deimos**, and is home to **Olympus Mons**, the largest volcano in the entire solar system. It is the **fourth planet** from the **Sun**.
 
• **Mercury**: The **closest planet** to the **Sun** and the **smallest** in the solar system. It has the shortest orbital period, taking only **88 Earth days** to revolve around the **Sun**. It lacks a significant atmosphere, causing extreme temperature variations between day and night.
 
• **Jupiter**: The **fifth planet** from the **Sun** and the **largest** in the solar system. It is a **gas giant** primarily composed of **Hydrogen** and **Helium**. It is famous for its **Great Red Spot**, a giant storm, and has at least **95 moons**, including **Ganymede**, the largest moon in the solar system.
 
• **Planetary Classification**: The first four planets (**Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars**) are **Terrestrial Planets** or **Inner Planets**, characterized by solid, rocky surfaces. The outer four (**Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune**) are **Jovian Planets** or **Gas/Ice Giants**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Albedo**: **Venus** has a very high **albedo** of approximately **0.7**. This high reflectivity is due to its permanent cover of highly reflective clouds composed of **sulfuric acid**, which prevents **70%** of sunlight from reaching the surface but makes it shine brilliantly.
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure**: The surface pressure on **Venus** is about **92 times** that of **Earth**, which is equivalent to the pressure at a depth of nearly **1 kilometer** under **Earth's** oceans.
 
• **Orbital Characteristics**: A **sidereal day** on **Venus** (one full rotation) takes about **243 Earth days**, while its **orbital period** (one year) takes about **225 Earth days**. This means a day on **Venus** is actually longer than its year.
 
• **Exploration**: The **Venera program** by the **Soviet Union** was the first to send probes that successfully landed on the surface of **Venus** in the **1970s** and **1980s**, providing the first images of its harsh, rocky terrain.
</ul

The correct answer is __**AstroSat**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **AstroSat** is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory, launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **September 28, 2015**.

• The satellite is designed to study celestial sources in **X-ray**, **optical**, and **UV spectral bands** simultaneously, which provides a unique capability to observe high-energy processes in **black holes**, **neutron stars**, and **binary star systems**.

• **Mangalyaan**, also known as the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)**, was India's first interplanetary mission aimed at studying the **Martian surface** and atmosphere.

• **Chandrayaan-2** was India's second lunar exploration mission, which included an **Orbiter**, **Lander (Vikram)**, and **Rover (Pragyan)** to explore the Moon's south polar region.

• **RISAT-1** (Radar Imaging Satellite-1) is an indigenous **Earth observation satellite** that uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) for applications in agriculture, forestry, and disaster management.

**Additional Information__**

• **AstroSat** was launched into a 650 km orbit with an inclination of 6 degrees by the **PSLV-C30** rocket from **Sriharikota**.

• It carries five major scientific payloads: **UVIT** (Ultra Violet Imaging Telescope), **SXT** (Soft X-ray Telescope), **LAXPC** (Large Area X-ray Proportional Counter), **CZTI** (Cadmium Zinc Telluride Imager), and **SSM** (Scanning Sky Monitor).

• India is the **fifth country/agency** in the world to launch a full-fledged space observatory, following the **USA (NASA)**, **Russia**, **Japan**, and the **European Space Agency (ESA)**.

• In 2024, ISRO also launched **XPoSat** (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) to further study the polarization of cosmic X-rays from sources like **black holes**.
</ul

question: Which device is commonly used to measure temperature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thermometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thermometer:** A thermometer is a scientific instrument used to measure temperature. It provides readings in units such as Celsius, Fahrenheit, or Kelvin.
 
• Thermometers work based on the principle of thermal expansion or the change in physical properties of materials (e.g., mercury or alcohol) when heated or cooled.
 
• They are widely used in various fields, including **medical, industrial, meteorological, and research applications**. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• **Barometer:** This device measures atmospheric pressure and is not designed to measure temperature. It is primarily used in meteorology. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• **Speedometer:** A speedometer measures the speed of a vehicle. It has no relation to temperature measurement. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• **Altimeter:** An altimeter measures altitude or the height above sea level. It is used in aviation and mountaineering, not for temperature measurement. *Hence, this is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thermometer Types:**

 
 
• **Mercury Thermometers:** These thermometers use mercury in a glass tube. They are highly accurate and used in laboratories and medical settings.
 
• **Digital Thermometers:** These devices provide temperature readings in a digital format and are commonly used in homes and hospitals due to their ease of use.
 
• **Infrared Thermometers:** These thermometers measure temperature from a distance by detecting infrared radiation emitted by an object. They are widely used in industrial and medical fields.
 
• **Alcohol Thermometers:** These use alcohol dyed for visibility and are suitable for measuring lower temperatures, as alcohol has a lower freezing point than mercury.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Thermometers:**
 
 
• **Medical Use:** Thermometers are essential in healthcare to monitor body temperature and diagnose fever or hypothermia.
 
• **Weather Monitoring:** Meteorologists use thermometers to measure ambient air temperature for weather forecasts.
 
• **Industrial Use:** Thermometers are crucial in industries such as manufacturing, food processing, and chemical production to ensure proper temperature control.
 
• **Scientific Research:** Precise temperature measurement is essential in experiments related to physics, chemistry, and biology.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History of Thermometers:**

 
 
• **Gabriel Fahrenheit:** Invented the mercury thermometer in **1714**, introducing the Fahrenheit scale.
 
• **Anders Celsius:** Developed the Celsius scale in **1742**, widely used in scientific and daily temperature measurements.
 
 
 
• **Key Scientific Principles:**
 
 
• **Thermal Expansion:** Materials expand or contract with temperature changes, a principle used in traditional thermometers.
 
• **Infrared Radiation:** Infrared thermometers detect heat radiation, enabling non-contact temperature measurement.
 
 
 
• **Global Standards:**
 
 
• Temperature measurements follow internationally recognized units like **Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin**, standardized for consistency.

subject: GK
question: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between velocity and acceleration in different dimensions?

options.text: In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration are always perpendicular to each other.
In two-dimensional motion, acceleration must always act opposite to velocity.
In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration lie along the same line, either in the same or opposite direction.
In three-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration must always act in the same direction.

solution:
The correct answer is __**In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration lie along the same line, either in the same or opposite direction.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• **One-dimensional motion**, also known as **rectilinear motion**, refers to movement along a straight line. In this case, the position of the object can be described using a single coordinate (e.g., x).

• The **velocity** vector always points in the direction of motion along that straight line.

• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of velocity. For the motion to remain strictly one-dimensional, any change in the velocity must occur along the same axis. Therefore, acceleration must act along the same line as velocity.

• If **velocity and acceleration** are in the **same direction**, the object is **speeding up**.

• If **velocity and acceleration** are in **opposite directions**, the object is **slowing down** (also known as **deceleration** or **retardation**).

• In **two-dimensional** or **three-dimensional** motion, acceleration can be at any angle to the velocity vector, which allows the object to change its **direction** of motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In **Uniform Circular Motion**, the acceleration (centripetal acceleration) is always **perpendicular** to the velocity vector. This changes the direction of the object but not its speed.

• In **Projectile Motion** (a type of 2D motion), the acceleration due to gravity is constant and acts vertically downwards, while the velocity has both horizontal and vertical components.

• **Instantaneous velocity** is the derivative of position with respect to time, and **instantaneous acceleration** is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.

• If acceleration is **zero**, the velocity remains **constant** in both magnitude and direction.
</ul

subject: GK
question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to dimensional analysis?

options.text: An equation that is dimensionally consistent is always physically correct.
Dimensional analysis can verify both the magnitude and the physical validity of an equation.
Trigonometric and logarithmic functions are valid only when applied to quantities that are dimensionless.
Refractive index has dimensions because it involves the speed of light.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Trigonometric and logarithmic functions are valid only when applied to quantities that are dimensionless.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential functions** are mathematical operations that must take **dimensionless arguments**. For example, in the expression sin(theta) , the angle theta must be dimensionless. Similarly, in log(x) or e^x , x must be a pure number.

• An equation that is **dimensionally consistent** is not necessarily **physically correct**. For instance, the equation s = ut + at² is dimensionally consistent (all terms have dimensions of length), but it is physically incorrect because the correct kinematic formula is s = ut + (1)/(2)at² .

• **Dimensional analysis** cannot verify the **magnitude** or **dimensionless constants** in an equation. It only checks if the units on both sides of the equation are compatible.

• The **Refractive Index** is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in a medium ( n = c/v ). Since it is a ratio of two similar physical quantities (speeds), it is a **dimensionless quantity**.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Principle of Homogeneity of Dimensions** states that the dimensions of all the terms in a physical expression must be the same.

• Other common **dimensionless quantities** include **strain**, **relative density**, **solid angle**, and **plane angle**.

• While dimensional analysis is a powerful tool for checking the consistency of equations and deriving relations, its main limitation is its inability to determine **proportionality constants** or handle **summation/difference** of terms that are not of the same dimension.
</ul

subject: GK
question:
A car accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 20 m/s in 5 seconds.

What is the magnitude of its acceleration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4 m/s²**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of **velocity** of an object with respect to **time**.
 
• The formula to calculate **uniform acceleration** is derived from the **first equation of motion**: v = u + at, which can be rearranged as a = (v - u) / t.
 
• In this scenario, the car starts from **rest**, which means the **initial velocity (u)** is 0 m/s.
 
• The **final velocity (v)** reached by the car is 20 m/s, and the **time (t)** taken to reach this speed is 5 seconds.
 
• Plugging these values into the formula: a = (20 - 0) / 5.
 
• The calculation results in an acceleration of **4 m/s²**.
 
• Option (1) is incorrect as 20 / 5 is not 2. Option (3) and (4) are incorrect as they represent values derived from incorrect mathematical operations (like 20 / 2 or 5 squared).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **SI unit** of acceleration is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• Acceleration is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• If an object is slowing down, the acceleration is opposite to the direction of motion, often referred to as **retardation** or **deceleration**.
 
• **Uniform acceleration** implies that the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, which is represented by a straight line on a **velocity-time graph**.
 
• The **slope** of a velocity-time graph gives the **magnitude of acceleration**.

question: What is the difference between displacement and distance?

options.text: Distance includes direction; displacement does not
Displacement includes direction; distance does not

solution:
The correct answer is __**Displacement includes direction; distance does not**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
__ 

• **Displacement** is a vector quantity that specifies the shortest straight-line distance between the initial and final positions of an object, along with the direction of movement. 

• **Distance**, on the other hand, is a scalar quantity that measures the total length of the path traveled by an object, irrespective of the direction. 

• Displacement can have a positive, negative, or zero value depending on the direction of motion, while distance is always positive and cannot be negative. 

• For example, if an object moves 10 meters forward and then 10 meters backward to its starting point, the displacement is 0 meters (due to no net change in position), while the distance is 20 meters. 

• Displacement considers direction and magnitude, making it more specific for indicating the change in position, whereas distance only measures magnitude, making it less specific. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Vector Quantity:** 

• A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. Examples include displacement, velocity, acceleration, and force. 

• Displacement is a vector quantity because it specifies both the magnitude (shortest distance) and direction. 
 
 

• **Scalar Quantity:** 

• A scalar quantity has only magnitude and no direction. Examples include distance, speed, mass, and temperature. 

• Distance is a scalar quantity because it measures only the magnitude of the path traveled. 
 
 

• **Applications:** 

• Displacement is used in physics for calculations involving motion, such as determining velocity and acceleration. 

• Distance is commonly used for practical purposes like measuring travel lengths or determining road routes. 
 
 

• **Example:** 

• If a person walks 3 km north and then 4 km east, the distance traveled is 7 km, while the displacement (using Pythagoras theorem) is 5 km northeast. 

• This highlights the difference between the total path traveled (distance) and the shortest path between two points (displacement). 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Directional Significance:** Displacement’s inclusion of direction makes it crucial for vector-based calculations in physics, while distance is used for scalar measurements. 

• **Zero Displacement:** If an object returns to its starting point after movement, displacement is zero, but distance measures the total path traveled. 

• **Real-Life Scenarios:** Distance is practical for everyday usage (e.g., driving or running), while displacement is essential for scientific experiments and modeling motion. 

• **Geographical Representation:** In maps, displacement is represented as straight-line distance between two points, while distance considers the curved or actual traveled path.

• Mutual Inductance is the interaction of one coil's magnetic field on another coil as it induces a voltage in the adjacent coil.
 
• It is the basic operating principle of the transformer, motors, generators, and many other electrical components that interact with another magnetic field. 
 
• The mutual inductance between the two coils can be greatly increased by **positioning them on a common soft iron core** or by **increasing the number of turns**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weber **is the SI unit of m**agnetic flux.**
 
• **Farad **is the SI unit of **electrical capacitance.**
 
• Tesla (T) is SI unit of magnetic flux density or magnetic field strength.

question: Which of the following is dimensionless?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Longitudinal strain.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• The powers to which fundamental quantities must be raised in order to express the given physical quantity are called its dimensions.
 
• A quantity without dimension will usually be a ratio of two quantities with similar dimensions and, hence, cancel out.
 
• Thus, they will have no units.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• **Longitudinal stress:**

 
 
• Longitudinal stress is the stress which acts along the length and its unit is **N/m² or Pascal.**
 
 
 
• **Shear stress: **
 
 
• **​**If the deforming force acts tangentially to the surface of the body, It produces a change in the shape of the body.
 
• This tangential force applied per unit area is called shear stress.
 
• Its unit is ** N/mm2 or MPa. **
 
 
 
• **Deforming force: **
 
 
• **​**Deforming Force An external force applied to a body that changes its size or shape or both is called deforming force.
 
• its unit is** N or kg-m/s².**
 
 
 
• **Longitudinal strain: **
 
 
• **​**The change in the length (ΔL) to the original length (L) of the body is known as longitudinal strain.
 
 

i.e., Longitudinal strain = frac{{{{Delta }}L}}{L}

 
• And since it is a ratio of two lengths, hence it is a **dimensionless **quantity.

question: -40 degrees Fahrenheit is equal to how many degrees on the Celsius scale?
solution:
The correct answer is __**– 40.**__

__
 
• **-40 degrees**__ is the temperature that shows the **same measurement **in Celsius and Fahrenheit scales.
 
• On a Fahrenheit scale, the intervals between the ice point and the steam point are divided into **180 equal parts.**
 
• The following mathematical equation is used to convert the Fahrenheit scale(F) to Celsius scale(C):
 __
 
• C=(F -32)times {5over9}
 
 
 
• Given that;
 
 
• F= -40.
 
• Substitute the value of F in the above equation:
 
• C=(-40 -32)times {5over9}
 
• C=(-72)times {5over9}
 
• C= -40.
 
 
 
• -40 degrees Fahrenheit is equal to** -40 degrees Celsius.**__
 
• **-574.25 degrees** is the temperature that shows the same measurement in Kelvin and Fahrenheit scales.

question: Which of the following is the SI unit of luminous intensity?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Candela.__**

__
 
• Candela is the unit of **luminous intensity** in the **International System** of **Units.**
 
• It is defined as the **luminous intensity** in a given **direction** of a **source** that emits **monochromatic** **radiation** of frequency **540 × 1012 hertz.**
 
• It has a **radiant intensity** in that same direction of **1/683 watt** per **steradian.**
 
• The **candela** has replaced the standard** candle** or **lamp** as a unit of **luminous intensity** in calculations involving **artificial lighting** and is sometimes called the **new candle**.
 
• It is the unit of** Luminous intensity. **The symbol of Candela is **Cd.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Lambert**
 
 
The lambert is a **non-SI metric** unit of luminance.

 
It is named after **Johann Heinrich Lambert**, a Swiss **mathematician**, **physicist,** and **astronomer.**

 
A related unit of **luminance**, the **foot-lambert**, is used in the **lighting**, **cinema,** and **flight** simulation **industries.**

 
 
 

 **Joule**
 
 
A joule is a derived unit of** energy** in the **International System of Units**.

 
It is equal to the** work **done by a** force** of **one newton** acting through **one meter**.

 
It is named in honor of the English physicist **James Prescott Joule.**

 
It equals **107 ergs** or approximately 0.7377-foot-**pounds**.

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd57ca557e9e3184ff39514b5e6bdcfe11dcb2bc5c261b25a40fcfedaf1bf4ae.png] 

 
 
 

 **Ampere**
 
 
**Ampere** is the unit of **electric current **in the International System of Units. 

 
The **ampere** would henceforth be defined such that the **elementary charge** would be **equal** to **1.602176634 × 10−19 coulomb**.

 
Unit of ** Electric current.**

 
Named after** Andre-Marie Ampere.**

question: What is the eligibility criteria for artisans under the PM Vishwakarma Yojana?

options.text: Must be engaged in traditional crafts
Must have a minimum income of ₹5 lakh
Must be employed in government services

solution:
The correct answer is __**Must be engaged in traditional crafts**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **PM Vishwakarma Yojana** is a central sector scheme launched to provide comprehensive support to **artisans and craftspeople** who work with their hands and tools.

• The primary eligibility criterion is that the applicant must be engaged in one of the **18 identified traditional trades**, which include occupations like **Carpenter, Boat Maker, Blacksmith, Potter, Sculptor, and Cobbler**, among others.

• The scheme is inclusive and covers artisans from both **rural and urban areas** across India; therefore, being restricted to urban areas is not a requirement.

• Individuals employed in **government services** and their family members are specifically **excluded** from the eligibility list.

• There is no requirement for a **minimum income of ₹5 lakh**; in fact, the scheme aims to uplift those at the grassroots level who often lack financial resources.

• The minimum age for registration under the scheme is **18 years**, and the benefit is restricted to **one member per family**.

• Applicants must not have taken loans under similar credit-based self-employment schemes like **PMEGP, PM SVANidhi, or Mudra** in the last five years.

**Additional Information__**

• The scheme was officially launched on **September 17, 2023**, coinciding with **Vishwakarma Jayanti**.

• It has a total financial outlay of **₹13,000 crore** for a period of five years (FY 2023-24 to FY 2027-28).

• Beneficiaries are provided with a **PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID card**, which grants them formal recognition.

• The scheme offers **skill upgradation** through basic and advanced training, along with a **stipend of ₹500 per day** during the training period.

• A **toolkit incentive** of up to **₹15,000** is provided to help artisans purchase modern equipment.

• Artisans can access **collateral-free credit** of up to **₹3 lakh** (in two tranches of ₹1 lakh and ₹2 lakh) at a highly subsidized interest rate of **5%**.

• The **Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)** is the nodal ministry for the implementation of this scheme.

question: What is the primary goal of the Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP) under NRLM?

options.text: To provide free seeds to farmers

solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote women in agriculture**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP)** is a sub-component of the **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)**. Its primary objective is to empower women in agriculture by making systematic investments to enhance their participation and productivity. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• The scheme seeks to improve the socio-economic status of rural women and recognize the identity of women as **'Kisan'** (farmers), ensuring they have better access to resources and technology.

• It aims to build the capacity of women in the agriculture sector through systematic investments and handholding by community-based institutions.

• Providing free seeds is not the primary goal of this specific mission, although agricultural inputs may be part of broader support provided by other government schemes. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• Building irrigation facilities is primarily handled under dedicated infrastructure schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• While MKSP promotes **Sustainable Agriculture** and non-chemical farming, its core mission is the holistic empowerment of the woman farmer herself. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Launch and Ministry**: MKSP was launched in **2011** by the **Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)** as a specialized program for women farmers.

• **Implementation Strategy**: The scheme is implemented through **State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs)** which act as Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) at the state level.

• **Funding Pattern**: It is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme**. The funding pattern is **60:40** between the Centre and the States, while for North Eastern and Himalayan states, the ratio is **90:10**.

• **Focus Areas**: The program focuses on **Sustainable Agriculture**, **Community Managed Sustainable Agriculture (CMSA)**, and **Non-Timber Forest Produce (NTFP)** to ensure diverse livelihood options.

• **Target Group**: The program prioritizes **small and marginal farmers**, with a specific focus on women from **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** communities.

**Important Points__**

• **Drudgery Reduction**: A key objective of MKSP is to introduce **women-friendly tools** and technologies to reduce the physical labor and drudgery associated with traditional farming activities.

• **Krishi Sakhis**: The scheme creates a cadre of **Community Resource Persons (CRPs)** known as **Krishi Sakhis** who provide training, handholding, and support to other women farmers at the grassroots level.

• **Food and Nutritional Security**: By increasing the productivity and income of women-led farms, the scheme directly contributes to the **food and nutritional security** of rural households.

• **Market Linkages**: MKSP also works towards providing better **market linkages** and value chain development to ensure that women farmers receive fair prices for their produce.

question: What is the key focus of NRLM (National Rural Livelihood Mission)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Formation of Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)** was launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development**, **Government of India**, in **June 2011**. It was later renamed **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana (DAY-NRLM)** in **November 2015**.

• The key focus and core strategy of the mission is the **Formation of Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**. The mission aims to organize the rural poor, especially women, into SHGs and their federations to provide them with a platform for financial services and sustainable livelihoods. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***

• The scheme does not focus on **Providing free food grains**. This is the primary objective of the **National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013**, and the **Public Distribution System (PDS)**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***

• **Building rural roads** is the specific mandate of the **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)**, which was launched in **December 2000** to provide all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

• **Promoting urban employment** is the goal of the **National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM)**. **NRLM** is strictly dedicated to the **rural** population and poverty alleviation in villages. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

• The mission follows a **demand-driven strategy**, where states have the flexibility to develop their own **poverty reduction action plans** based on local needs.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Universal Social Mobilization**: The mission seeks to bring at least **one woman member** from each identified rural poor household into the **Self-Help Group (SHG)** network in a time-bound manner.

• **Financial Inclusion**: **DAY-NRLM** works on both the demand and supply sides of financial inclusion. It provides **Revolving Funds (RF)** and **Community Investment Funds (CIF)** to SHGs to strengthen their financial base and encourage internal lending.

• **Interest Subvention**: The mission provides interest subvention to SHGs to ensure they can access bank credit at an effective interest rate of **7% per annum**. In **250 identified backward districts**, an additional subvention of **3%** is provided for prompt repayment, reducing the effective rate to **4%**.

• **Livelihood Enhancement**: It focuses on stabilizing and promoting existing livelihoods of the poor through **agriculture**, **non-farm sectors**, and **skill development**.

• **Funding Pattern**: It is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** where the funding is shared between the **Centre** and the **States** in the ratio of **60:40** (for general states) and **90:10** (for North-Eastern and Himalayan states).

**Important Points__**

• **Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP)**: A sub-component of **NRLM**, it aims to empower women in agriculture by making systematic investments to enhance their participation and productivity.

• **DDU-GKY**: The **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana** is the placement-linked skill development program under the mission, targeting rural youth in the age group of **15 to 35 years**.

• **Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP)**: This component supports the rural poor to set up **small enterprises** at the village level, providing them with business management training and capital.

• **Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana (AGEY)**: Launched in **2017**, it provides alternative livelihood options to SHG members by allowing them to operate **public transport services** in backward rural areas.

• **World Bank Support**: The mission is partially funded through a credit from the **World Bank** under the **National Rural Livelihoods Project (NRLP)**.
</ul

__
 
• **Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana** (VKY) was launched by the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** in **2014** as a comprehensive scheme to improve the quality of life of tribal people, especially focusing on **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)**.
 
• The scheme aims at **holistic development** by addressing critical areas such as education, health, nutrition, livelihood, housing, and infrastructure for tribal communities.
 
• VKY focuses on **converging resources** from existing government schemes and programs to ensure that tribal development is inclusive and targeted. *Hence, it is the correct option.*
 
• The scheme emphasizes on **area-specific interventions** based on the needs of tribal groups, ensuring that no tribal community is left behind in development initiatives.
 
• Under VKY, special attention is paid to **education and skill development** to empower tribal youth and improve their employability. This is crucial for improving socio-economic conditions. *Hence, this scheme is highly effective for PVTGs.*
 
• The scheme also ensures that tribal communities have access to **basic services** such as drinking water, sanitation, electricity, and healthcare facilities, thereby improving their standard of living.
 
• It seeks to **protect tribal culture** while ensuring socio-economic development, thus maintaining the unique identity of tribal groups. *Hence, VKY aligns well with the question’s focus.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

question: Which organization supports meal distribution under the scheme in some areas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Akshaya Patra Foundation**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Akshaya Patra Foundation** is a **not-for-profit organization** based in **Bengaluru**, India, that operates on a **Public-Private Partnership (PPP)** model with the **Government of India** and various **State Governments**.

• It is the primary organization that supports the **distribution of meals** under the **PM POSHAN** (formerly **Mid-Day Meal**) scheme in several states across India, serving millions of children every day to eliminate classroom hunger.

• The foundation was established in the year **2000** and started by serving **1,500 children** in **5 schools**; today, it has scaled up to reach over **2 million children** across multiple states and union territories.

• **UNICEF** (United Nations Children's Fund) and **WHO** (World Health Organization) are international bodies that provide **technical expertise**, **policy guidelines**, and **funding for health initiatives**, but they do not typically manage the daily logistics of meal distribution in Indian schools. ***Hence, options 1 and 3 are incorrect.***

• **NITI Aayog** is the premier **policy think tank** of the **Government of India**, providing directional and policy inputs; it monitors and evaluates the performance of the **PM POSHAN** scheme but does not act as an implementing agency for food distribution. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

• The **Akshaya Patra Foundation** utilizes **centralized kitchens** in urban areas, which are highly automated facilities capable of preparing up to **100,000 meals** in a few hours, ensuring high standards of **hygiene** and **nutrition**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Akshaya Patra Foundation.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **PM POSHAN Scheme** (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** that provides one hot cooked meal in **Government** and **Government-aided schools**.

• The scheme was renamed from the **National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education** (Mid-Day Meal Scheme) in **September 2021** and has been extended to include children in **Balvatikas** (pre-primary classes).

• The **Ministry of Education** is the nodal ministry responsible for the implementation of this scheme at the national level, covering approximately **11.80 crore children** in **11.20 lakh schools**.

• The nutritional norms for the **Primary level** (Classes 1-5) are **450 calories** and **12 grams of protein**, while for the **Upper Primary level** (Classes 6-8), the norms are **700 calories** and **20 grams of protein**.

• The scheme aims to address two major issues: **malnutrition** among children and the **socio-economic gap** in education by incentivizing parents to send their children to school.

**Important Points__**

• **Historical Context**: **Tamil Nadu** was the first state in **India** to introduce the **Mid-Day Meal Scheme** in the **1960s** under the leadership of Chief Minister **K. Kamaraj**.

• **Legal Mandate**: In **November 2001**, the **Supreme Court of India** passed a landmark judgment in the **PUCL vs Union of India** case, making it mandatory for all **State Governments** to provide cooked mid-day meals.

• **Funding Pattern**: The cost of the scheme is shared between the **Centre** and the **States** in a **60:40** ratio for general category states, **90:10** for **North-Eastern** and **Himalayan States**, and **100%** for **Union Territories** without a legislature.

• **Tithi Bhojan**: This is a community participation program under **PM POSHAN** where people provide special food to children on occasions like **festivals**, **birthdays**, or **anniversaries**.

• **Social Integration**: The scheme plays a vital role in **socialization** as children from different **castes** and **religions** sit together and eat the same meal, helping to break down **social barriers**.
</ul

question: The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) aims to provide pension benefits to which segment of the population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Unorganized sector workers**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Atal Pension Yojana (APY)** was officially launched on **9th May 2015** by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** in **Kolkata**, **West Bengal**. The scheme is specifically designed to provide **social security** and **old-age protection** to the **unorganized sector workers**, such as **domestic helps**, **gardeners**, **delivery boys**, and **street vendors**, who do not have any formal pension coverage. ***Hence, the correct answer is Unorganized sector workers.***

• The scheme is open to all **citizens of India** who fall within the **age group** of **18 to 40 years**. This entry age ensures that the subscriber contributes for at least **20 years** before reaching the **maturity age** of **60 years**.

• Under **APY**, a subscriber is guaranteed a **minimum monthly pension** of **Rs. 1,000**, **Rs. 2,000**, **Rs. 3,000**, **Rs. 4,000**, or **Rs. 5,000** after they reach the **age of 60**. The exact amount of pension depends on the **contribution amount** and the **age** at which the individual joins the scheme.

• The **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** is the **statutory body** responsible for the **administration** and **regulation** of the **Atal Pension Yojana** under the **National Pension System (NPS)** framework.

• **Government employees** (Option 1) are typically covered under the **National Pension System (NPS)** or other statutory pension schemes, and **students** (Option 4) are generally not earning members, making them ineligible for this contribution-linked scheme. ***Hence, these options are incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Successor Scheme:** The **Atal Pension Yojana** replaced the earlier **Swavalamban Yojana**, which was launched in **2010-11**. The **APY** was introduced to address the shortcomings of **Swavalamban**, particularly the lack of a **guaranteed pension amount**.

• **Recent Amendment (2022):** As per the **Ministry of Finance** notification, effective from **1st October 2022**, any citizen who is or has been an **income taxpayer** is not eligible to join the **Atal Pension Yojana**. This change was implemented to ensure that the **government subsidies** are targeted towards the **economically weaker sections**.

• **Contribution Mechanism:** The **contribution** is **automatically debited** from the subscriber's **savings bank account** or **post office account**. Subscribers can choose to contribute on a **monthly**, **quarterly**, or **half-yearly** basis to suit their income patterns.

• **Tax Benefits:** Contributions made to the **APY** are eligible for **tax deductions** under **Section 80CCD (1)** of the **Income Tax Act, 1961**, providing an additional incentive for **long-term savings**.

• **Death Benefits:** If the **subscriber dies** before the age of **60**, the **spouse** has the option to continue the account until the original subscriber would have reached **60 years**. If the **subscriber dies** after **60**, the **spouse** receives the same **pension amount** for life.

**Important Points__**

• **Nominee Rights:** In the event of the **death of both** the subscriber and the spouse, the **entire accumulated pension corpus** (the sum of contributions and returns) is handed over to the **nominee** designated by the subscriber.

• **Penalty for Default:** If a subscriber fails to maintain the required balance for **auto-debit**, banks may charge a **nominal penalty** ranging from **Rs. 1 to Rs. 10 per month**, depending on the contribution slab. The account is only **closed** if the **contributions stop** completely for a prolonged period (usually **24 months**).

• **Jan Suraksha Trinity:** The **APY** is one of the three **social security schemes** launched together in **2015**, the other two being **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)** and **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)**, collectively aimed at providing **comprehensive insurance and pension** coverage to all Indians.

• **Voluntary Exit:** **Voluntary exit** from **APY** before the **age of 60** is generally not permitted, except in **exceptional circumstances** such as the **death** of the beneficiary or the onset of a **terminal illness**.
</ul

• **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)** is a **food security welfare scheme **announced by the Government of India on **March 26, 2020,** during the COVID-19 pandemic in India.
 
• The program is operated by the **Department of Food and Public Distribution **under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
 
• The initiative intends to** feed India's poorest citizens** by distributing grain to all priority families through the **Public Distribution System **(ration cardholders and those identified by the **Antyodaya Anna Yojana scheme**).

• Phase III of the scheme was operational from **May to June 2021.**
 
• Phase IV of the scheme during** July-November, 2021**.

 __

• The scheme was approved in **March 2006.**
 
 
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana:**__

• The government plans to** invest ₹756 billion** for rural electrification under this scheme.
 
• The scheme replaced the existing** Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana.**
 
• The scheme is one of the** flagship programmes** of the **Power Ministry (MoP) **and will facilitate 24x7 supply of electricity.
 
• The scheme was launched under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in** November 2014.**​

question: In 2023, Government of India has proposed to launch the ‘Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana’ ___________ to skill lakhs of youth within the next three years covering new age courses like coding, AI, robotics, mechatronics, IOT, 3D printing, drones and soft skills.
solution:
The correct answer is __**4.0.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2023, the Government of India launched ‘Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana** 4.0** (PMKVY 4.0)’, as part of its continued effort to upskill India's youth in emerging technologies.
 
• The aim is to train over** 4.2 lakh youth **over the next three years, covering modern areas like artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, coding, drones, 3D printing, mechatronics, Internet of Things (IoT), and soft skills.
 
• The scheme also focuses on industry-based learning to ensure that participants acquire skills that align with market demands.
 
• The **key objectives** include:
 
 
• Enhancing employability by providing vocational training and certification in new-age technologies.
 
• Incorporating international standards into the curriculum for globally recognized certifications.
 
• Promoting self-employment and entrepreneurship alongside providing placements in relevant industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) has been implemented in phases since its inception, each aiming to build on the last in terms of training India’s workforce for new and emerging industries.

 
• **PMKVY 1.0 (2015-2016):**

 
 
• Launch Date: 15 July **2015**
 
• Goal: To provide skill training to around 24 lakh youth across the country in various sectors.
 
• Focused on short-term training programs through training centers accredited by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).
 
• Outcome: More than 19 lakh candidates were trained, but the placement rate was a key challenge, as the training did not always align with industry demand.
 
 
 
• **PMKVY 2.0 (2016-2020):**
 
 
• Launch Date: 2 October **2016**
 
• Goal: Upskilling of over 1 crore people by 2020.
 
• Expanded to cover more sectors and introduced Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) for workers who already possess certain skills.
 
• Focus on placements with the introduction of mandatory placement tracking and support.
 
• Increased participation of state governments in the scheme for local adaptability.
 
• Special Projects were introduced to cater to the specific needs of certain industries, job roles, or regions.
 
• Outcome: It significantly increased reach but faced criticism for not achieving a high placement rate despite the broader scope.
 
 
 
• **PMKVY 3.0 (2020-2021):**
 
• Launch Date: January 15, **2021**
 
 
• Goal: To skill over 8 lakh people in emerging areas over one year.
 
• Shifted focus towards local demand-based skill training.
 
• Emphasized digital learning to adapt to the post-pandemic world, incorporating online and blended training modes.
 
• Introduction of district skill committees to identify demand-driven skills specific to local areas.
 
• Strengthened the focus on apprenticeship training and linking skilling with employment.
 
• Outcome: PMKVY 3.0 aimed to refine earlier challenges by localizing skill development and incorporating emerging technologies like AI, cybersecurity, and cloud computing.
 
 

Each version of the PMKVY scheme aimed to improve India’s skill ecosystem by adapting to the evolving needs of the labor market and technological advancements. PMKVY 4.0 continues this effort by focusing on futuristic technologies and aligning the training program with global standards.

question: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (2005) provides work for how many days?
solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• MGNREGA is a landmark social welfare scheme enacted by the Government of India in **2005**.
 
• Its primary objective is to enhance the **livelihood security **of rural households by providing at least **100 days of guaranteed wage employment **each financial year.
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• **Right to Work: **MGNREGA provides rural households the legal right to employment. Any** adult member** of the household willing to do **unskilled **manual labor can apply for work.
 
• **Timely Wages:** Wages are to be paid within **15 days** of the work being completed. The wage rate is determined by the state government in accordance with the Minimum Wage Act.
 
• **Work Availability: **Work must be provided within **15 days** of the demand. If not, the applicant is entitled to an unemployment allowance.
 
• **Decentralized Implementation:** The scheme is implemented through** Gram Panchayats** (local self-government bodies), allowing for local-level decision-making regarding the projects and their implementation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• MGNREGA is a** centrally sponsored scheme**, where the central government provides a significant portion of the funding, especially for wages and material costs, while the state government also contributes.
 
• In some states, the number of guaranteed workdays under MGNREGA has been extended beyond 100 days to counter the impact of economic slowdowns, droughts, or the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• In the **2024 Union Budget**, the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) was allocated** ₹86,000 crore,** the same as the previous year.

The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)** is the correct answer because it was specifically launched to provide **clean cooking fuel** like **LPG** to women from **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** households. This scheme aims to replace unhealthy traditional fuels such as **firewood**, **coal**, and **cow-dung cakes**. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
 
• The scheme was launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** on **May 1, 2016**, in **Ballia, Uttar Pradesh**. It is implemented by the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**.
 
• Under this scheme, the **Central Government** provides a financial assistance of **Rs. 1600** for each **LPG connection** to the **BPL** households. This covers the security deposit of the cylinder and administrative charges.
 
• The primary objective of **PMUY** is to empower women and protect their health by reducing **indoor air pollution**, which is a major cause of respiratory diseases in **rural India**.
 
• The scheme has been highly successful, reaching its initial target of **5 crore** connections well ahead of schedule and subsequently expanding to cover over **9 crore** beneficiaries across the **country**.

__
 
• **PMUY 2.0 (Ujjwala 2.0)**: Launched in **August 2021** from **Mahoba, Uttar Pradesh**, this phase aimed to provide an additional **1 crore** connections to low-income families who were not covered under the first phase. In this version, beneficiaries receive the first **refill** and a **hotplate (stove)** free of cost.
 
• **Eligibility Criteria**: The applicant must be a **woman** above **18 years** of age belonging to **SC/ST**, **Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY)**, **Most Backward Classes (MBC)**, or other identified categories. She should not have any other **LPG connection** in her household.
 
• **Health and Environmental Impact**: According to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**, smoke from traditional fuels is equivalent to burning **400 cigarettes** per hour. **PMUY** helps mitigate **deforestation** and reduces the time spent by women on collecting firewood.
 
• **Ujjwala Diwas**: The government celebrates **May 1st** as **Ujjwala Diwas** to mark the anniversary of the scheme and promote the usage of **LPG** as a safe and sustainable fuel.

question: Who launched the National Digital Library of India in 2018?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakash Javadekar**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **National Digital Library of India (NDLI)** was officially dedicated to the nation on **June 19, 2018**, which coincides with **National Reading Day** in **India**.

• The launch was performed by **Prakash Javadekar**, who was serving as the **Union Minister for Human Resource Development** (now renamed the **Ministry of Education**) at that time. The event was held in **New Delhi**.

• The **NDLI** is a flagship project under the **National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT)**, an initiative funded by the **Ministry of Education**.

• The platform was developed, and is currently managed and maintained, by the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur** to provide a **single-window search** facility for all digital educational assets.

• While other ministers like **Smriti Irani**, **Ramesh Pokhriyal**, and **Dharmendra Pradhan** have held the **Education** portfolio at different times, it was specifically **Prakash Javadekar** who inaugurated this digital repository in **2018**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **NDLI** repository is an extensive virtual library that hosts over **60 million** digital resources, including **e-books**, **scholarly articles**, **thesis**, **manuscripts**, **audio lectures**, and **video lectures**.

• It is designed to be **multilingual**, providing interface support and content in more than **10 major Indian languages** to ensure that language is not a barrier to learning.

• The library caters to a wide spectrum of users, including **school students**, **undergraduates**, **post-graduates**, **researchers**, and **lifelong learners** across various academic disciplines.

• Users can access the library through the official **NDLI portal** or via a **mobile application**, which has also been integrated with the **UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance)** platform for wider reach.

• The project aims to bridge the **digital divide** by providing **inclusive and open access** to high-quality learning materials to all citizens of **India**, regardless of their location.

**Important Points__**

• **National Reading Day** (June 19) is celebrated to honor the legacy of **P.N. Panicker**, who is known as the **Father of the Library Movement** in **Kerala**.

• The **Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD)** was officially renamed the **Ministry of Education** in **August 2020** following the cabinet approval of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**.

• **Prakash Javadekar** served as the **Union HRD Minister** from **July 2016** to **May 2019**, a period during which several digital initiatives like **SWAYAM** and **NDL** were significantly scaled up.

• **IIT Kharagpur** was chosen as the lead institution for this project due to its technical expertise in handling large-scale **data management** and **digital archiving**.

• The **NDLI** also features specialized collections for **competitive exam preparation**, helping students prepare for exams like **JEE**, **NEET**, **GATE**, and **UPSC** by providing previous year papers and study guides.
</ul

question: Which government scheme aims to provide a social safety net by guaranteeing wage employment to rural households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** was enacted in **September 2005** and is one of the largest work guarantee programs in the world. It provides a **legal guarantee** for at least **100 days** of wage employment in every **financial year** to every **rural household** whose adult members volunteer to do **unskilled manual work**.

• The core objective of the scheme is to enhance **livelihood security** in rural areas by providing a safety net for the poor, while simultaneously creating **durable assets** such as roads, ponds, and irrigation canals to improve rural infrastructure.

• The act establishes a **demand-driven** model where the government is legally obligated to provide work within **15 days** of a demand being made. If the government fails to provide employment within this period, the applicant is entitled to a daily **unemployment allowance**.

• To promote **social inclusion** and **gender equality**, the act mandates that at least **one-third** of the total beneficiaries must be **women** who have registered and requested work under the scheme.

• Employment is provided locally, typically within a **5 km radius** of the applicant’s residence. If work is provided beyond this distance, an additional **10% wage** is paid to the worker to meet extra transportation and living expenses.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)**: Launched on **25 December 2000**, this is a nationwide plan in **India** to provide **all-weather road connectivity** to unconnected rural habitations. Unlike **MGNREGA**, it is an infrastructure project and not a wage employment guarantee scheme.

• **National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM)**: Launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development** in **June 2011**, it aims to create efficient and effective institutional platforms for the rural poor, enabling them to increase household income through sustainable **livelihood enhancements** and improved access to **financial services**.

• **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)**: This is a restructured version of the **NRLM** that focuses on organizing the poor into **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** and fostering **self-employment**. It emphasizes **skill development** and **entrepreneurship** rather than manual labor.

• **Social Audit**: A unique feature of **MGNREGA** is the mandatory **Social Audit**, which is conducted by the **Gram Sabha**. This process ensures **transparency** and **accountability** by allowing the community to monitor and verify the implementation of projects and expenditure.

• **Funding Mechanism**: The **Central Government** of **India** bears **100%** of the cost of wages for **unskilled manual labor** and **75%** of the material cost and wages for skilled or semi-skilled workers, while the remaining **25%** of material costs is borne by the **State Governments**.

**Important Points__**

• The scheme was originally launched as **NREGA** but was renamed the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act** on **2 October 2009**, marking the birth anniversary of **Mahatma Gandhi**.

• The **Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)** is the nodal agency at the **Central** level that oversees the policy framework and funding, while the **Gram Panchayats** are responsible for the actual implementation at the village level.

• Workers are issued a **Job Card**, which is a key document that records their rights and the amount of work they have completed. This card must be issued within **15 days** of application.

• Wages under **MGNREGA** are revised annually by the government and are linked to the **Consumer Price Index-Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL)** to ensure that the purchasing power of rural workers is maintained against **inflation**.

• The program has played a significant role in reducing **rural-to-urban migration** by providing viable employment opportunities within the villages during lean agricultural seasons.

question: Which government scheme aims to provide affordable and quality healthcare through a network of primary health centers and other facilities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Rural Health Mission (NHM)**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **National Health Mission (NHM)** is the primary government initiative aimed at providing affordable, accessible, and quality healthcare through a vast network of facilities. It was launched by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** to address the healthcare needs of both rural and urban populations. ***Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.***

• The mission is divided into two sub-missions: the **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)**, launched on **12th April 2005**, and the **National Urban Health Mission (NUHM)**, launched in **2013**.

• The core strategy of **NHM** involves strengthening the public health delivery system by improving the infrastructure of **Sub-Centres (SCs)**, **Primary Health Centres (PHCs)**, and **Community Health Centres (CHCs)**. It ensures that these facilities meet the **Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS)**.

• A key feature of the **NRHM** is the introduction of the **Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA)**, a trained female community health volunteer who acts as the first point of contact for any health-related demands of the rural population, particularly women and children.

• The mission focuses on achieving major health indicators such as reducing the **Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)** to **1 per 1000 live births**, the **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)** to **25 per 1000 live births**, and the **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)** to **2.1**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM)**: Launched in **October 2021**, this scheme is one of the largest pan-India schemes for strengthening healthcare infrastructure. Its primary goal is to fill critical gaps in public health infrastructure, surveillance, and health research. It aims to establish **Integrated Public Health Labs** in all **730 districts** and set up **Critical Care Hospital Blocks** in over **600 districts**.

• **Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY)**: This scheme was announced in **2003** with the objective of correcting regional imbalances in the availability of affordable and reliable **tertiary healthcare services**. It involves the setting up of **AIIMS-like institutions** (such as **AIIMS Rishikesh**, **AIIMS Bhopal**, etc.) and the upgradation of existing **Government Medical Colleges (GMCs)** by adding super-specialty blocks.

• **Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)**: Launched on **1st June 2011**, this initiative aims to eliminate out-of-pocket expenses for **pregnant women** and **sick newborns**. It entitles all pregnant women delivering in public health institutions to **free delivery**, including **Caesarean sections**, free drugs, diagnostics, diet, and free transport from home to the facility.

• **Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)**: Launched in **September 2018**, it is the world’s largest health insurance scheme fully financed by the government. It provides a cover of **Rs. 5 lakhs** per family per year for **secondary and tertiary care** hospitalization to over **12 crore** poor and vulnerable families (approximately **55 crore beneficiaries**).

• **National Health Policy (NHP) 2017**: This policy serves as the guiding framework for these schemes, aiming to increase government health expenditure to **2.5% of GDP** by **2025** and ensuring **Universal Health Coverage (UHC)** for all citizens.
