question: Which constitutional authority decides on the disqualification of a Member of State Legislature under the Anti-Defection Law?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker of the Legislative Assembly**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The decision on the disqualification of a member of the State Legislature under the **Anti-Defection Law** is made by the **Presiding Officer** of the House. For the Legislative Assembly, this authority is the **Speaker**, and for the Legislative Council, it is the **Chairperson**. ***Hence, the option involving the Speaker is correct.***
 
• The **Anti-Defection Law** was added to the Constitution of India via the **10th Schedule** through the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in the year **1985**. It was designed to prevent political defections prompted by the lure of office or similar considerations.
 
• According to the **10th Schedule**, any question regarding whether a member of a House has become subject to disqualification shall be referred to the **Speaker** or the **Chairperson** of such House, and their decision shall be final.
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India, in the landmark **Kihoto Hollohan vs Zachillhu case (1992)**, ruled that the decision of the **Speaker** or **Chairperson** is subject to **judicial review** on grounds of malafides or perversity. This means that while the Speaker decides, the **High Court** or **Supreme Court** can later examine the legality of that decision. ***Hence, the statement regarding the Chief Justice deciding initially is incorrect.***
 
• The **Election Commission** of India does not have the primary authority to decide on disqualification under the **10th Schedule**, although it advises the **Governor** on disqualifications arising under **Article 191(1)** (like office of profit or unsound mind). ***Hence, the statement involving the Election Commission in the context of defection is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Grounds for Disqualification:** Under the **10th Schedule**, a member can be disqualified if they **voluntarily give up** the membership of their political party or if they vote (or abstain from voting) in the House contrary to any direction issued by the political party (the **Whip**) without obtaining prior permission or if such act is not condoned within **15 days**.
 
• **Independent and Nominated Members:** An **independent member** becomes disqualified if they join any political party after the election. A **nominated member** is disqualified if they join any political party after the expiry of **6 months** from the date on which they take their seat in the House.
 
• **The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:** This amendment strengthened the law by deleting the provision that protected a "split" (where 1/3rd members defect). Now, at least **two-thirds** of the members of a party must in favour of a **merger** with another party to avoid disqualification.
 
• **Article 191 and 192:** **Article 191(2)** specifically mentions disqualification on the grounds of the **Tenth Schedule**. **Article 192** states that for other disqualifications (like holding an **Office of Profit**), the **Governor** decides after obtaining the opinion of the **Election Commission**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **No Time Limit for Decision:** Originally, the **Constitution** did not specify a **time limit** within which the **Speaker** must decide on a disqualification plea. This often led to political delays. However, in the **Keisham Meghachandra Singh case (2020)**, the **Supreme Court** recommended that the **Speaker** should decide such cases within a reasonable period, typically **3 months**.
 
• **Exceptions to the Law:** Disqualification does not apply in the case of a **merger** where **two-thirds** of the members of the legislative party agree to the merger. Also, a person elected as **Speaker** or **Deputy Speaker** can resign from their party and rejoin it after they cease to hold that office without being disqualified.
 
• **Impact on Stability:** The law aims to bring **political stability** to the **government** by ensuring that legislators do not change parties frequently, a practice colloquially known as **"Aaya Ram Gaya Ram"** in the Indian political context which was prevalent before **1985**.

question: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National human rights commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Human Rights Commission** is **NOT **a **constitutional body **in India.
 
• Established in 1993, the **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** is an autonomous statutory body mandated by the Protection of Human Rights Act of 1993, which was subsequently amended in 2006.
 
• Human rights are an integral component of society, and NHRC plays a pivotal role in safeguarding human rights in India.
 
• Serving as a vigilant guardian, NHRC oversees rights pertaining to life, dignity, liberty, and equality as outlined in Section 2(1) of the PHR Act.
 
• These rights, enshrined in the Constitution of India and upheld by international treaties, are enforceable by Indian courts. The establishment of NHRC aligns with the Paris Principles of Human Rights, 1991, which were adopted to promote and protect human rights.
 
• These principles, endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1993, serve as a guiding framework for NHRC's endeavours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Finance Commissions are periodically** constituted by the President of India under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution to delineate the financial interactions between the central government of India and the respective state governments.
 
• **The State Public Service Commission (SPSC)** is a constitutional entity responsible for administering examinations for state service appointments. Additionally, the SPSC offers guidance to the government on matters related to disciplinary actions and promotions.
 
• **The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)** is a constitutional body tasked with safeguarding the interests of scheduled castes in India.

question: What is the tenure of the Chairperson of National Human Rights Commission?
solution:
Tenure: The chairman and members hold office for a term of 3 years or until they attain the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India ​

 
• It is a statutory body constituted under the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993 on 12 October 1993. 
 
• It is in conformity with the Paris Principles, adopted at the first international workshop on national institutions for the promotion and protection of human rights held in Paris in October 1991, and endorsed by the General Assembly of the United Nations by its Regulations 48/134 of 20 December 1993.
 
• The NHRC is an embodiment of India’s concern for the promotion and protection of human rights.
 
• The Commission is responsible for spreading human rights awareness amongst the masses and encouraging the efforts of all stakeholders in the field of human rights literacy not only at the national level but at the international level too.
 
• The NHRC, India plays an active role in coordinating with other NHRIs of the world to enhance awareness from the perspective of human rights.
 
• The commission has no power to punish the violators of human rights, nor to award any relief including monetary relief to the victim.
 
• The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Bill, 2019 amended the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993. Some of the amendments were - 
 
 
• Tenure: Earlier the chairman and members hold office for a term of Five years or until they attain the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier. The Bill reduces the term of office to three years or till the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier. Further, the Act allows for the reappointment of members of the NHRC and SHRCs for a period of five years. The Bill removes the five-year limit for reappointment. 
 
• Composition of NHRC: Under the Act, the chairperson of the NHRC is a person who has been a Chief Justice of the Supreme Court. The Bill amends this to provide that a person who has been Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or a Judge of the Supreme Court will be the chairperson of the NHRC. 
 
• The Act provides for two persons having knowledge of human rights to be appointed as members of the NHRC. The Bill amends this to allow three members to be appointed, of which at least one will be a woman. 
 
• Under the Act, chairpersons of various commissions such as the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, and National Commission for Women are members of the NHRC. The Bill provides for including the chairpersons of the National Commission for Backward Classes, the National Commission for the Protection of Child Rights, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities as members of the NHRC.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 148**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 148** of the Constitution of India deals with the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
 
• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is an authority, established by the Constitution of India under Chapter V, who audits all receipts and expenditure of the Government of India and the state governments, including those of bodies and authorities substantially financed by the government.

question: Which of the following laws governs criminal offenses in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita** is a proposed legislation that will replace the existing Indian Penal Code (IPC), which governs criminal offenses in India. It aims to modernize the criminal justice system and introduce significant reforms.
 
• The existing **Indian Penal Code (IPC)**, enacted in **1860** during British rule, has been the primary law for criminal offenses in India. However, the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita is designed to address contemporary needs and align with the principles of justice in a democratic society.
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita** focuses on simplifying legal terminology, reducing delays in criminal trials, and enhancing the efficiency of the judicial process. It incorporates suggestions from legal experts, judiciary members, and stakeholders. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• It aims to replace archaic provisions of the IPC while ensuring that laws are consistent with India's changing socio-political framework and constitutional values.
 
• Key features of the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita include provisions for stricter punishment, streamlined definitions of offenses, and an emphasis on victim rights. It also aims to reduce misuse of certain provisions and enhance transparency. *Hence, this aligns with the current needs of India's legal framework.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita**:

 
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita** is part of a series of new legislative reforms proposed by the Indian government to replace colonial-era laws like the IPC, Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), and the Indian Evidence Act.
 
• It aims to bring more comprehensive and inclusive legislation that is aligned with India's present-day needs and aspirations. The legislation also seeks to eliminate redundancies and outdated provisions in the IPC.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Legislations:**
 
 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Samhita**: This legislation is designed to replace the **Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC)**, focusing on enhancing the procedural aspects of criminal law and ensuring speedy trials.
 
• **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam**: This is intended to replace the **Indian Evidence Act**. It aims to modernize the rules of evidence in criminal cases and ensure they are in line with technological advancements.
 
• **Civil Procedure Code:** This governs the procedural aspects of civil cases in India and is unrelated to criminal offenses. It is not being replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Replacing Colonial Laws:**
 
 
• Colonial laws like the IPC were framed to serve the interests of the British Empire. Replacing them with laws like the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita ensures that the legal framework aligns with the principles of democracy, justice, and equality enshrined in the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The new laws emphasize safeguarding the rights of victims, ensuring fair trials, and eliminating procedural delays in the justice system.
 
• For example, provisions related to sedition under Section 124A of the IPC have faced criticism for being misused. The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita seeks to address such issues comprehensively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita:**

 
 
• It introduces provisions to prevent the misuse of laws, particularly in cases of sedition and terrorism-related offenses.
 
• It simplifies the process of filing complaints and ensures that victims receive justice without unnecessary delays.
 
• The legislation focuses on improving transparency and accountability in the criminal justice system.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Reforms:**
 
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita reflects India's commitment to a fair and efficient legal system that prioritizes the rights of individuals and the needs of society.
 
• These reforms are expected to strengthen India's position as a modern democracy with robust legal and judicial frameworks.

question: Under the BSA, what is the value of expert opinion in a trial?

options.text: Advisory in nature, but holds persuasive value

solution:
The correct answer is __**Advisory in nature, but holds persuasive value**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• Under the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023**, specifically **Section 39** (which corresponds to Section 45 of the erstwhile Indian Evidence Act), the opinion of an **expert** is considered a relevant fact. However, it is fundamentally **advisory in nature** and does not bind the court.

• The primary role of an expert is to provide the judge with the necessary **scientific or technical criteria** for testing the accuracy of their conclusions, so as to enable the judge to form their own independent judgment by the application of these criteria to the facts proved in the case.

• Expert evidence is **persuasive** because it is based on specialized knowledge in fields like **foreign law, science, art, handwriting, or finger impressions**. While the court gives due weight to such opinions, it is not **conclusive proof**, meaning the court can reject the opinion if it finds it inconsistent with other evidence or if the reasons provided are not convincing. ***Hence, the correct answer is advisory in nature, but holds persuasive value.***

• The court is often described as the **'expert of experts'**. This means the final decision rests with the **Judiciary**, and the expert's testimony is treated as **corroborative evidence** rather than substantive evidence. It cannot be **ignored by the court** if it is relevant, but it also cannot be the sole basis for a conviction or decree without further scrutiny. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

• The value of expert opinion is the same in both **civil and criminal trials**. In criminal cases, expert opinions from **forensic scientists** or **medical examiners** are crucial but must still be weighed against other direct or circumstantial evidence. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**

• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023** replaced the **Indian Evidence Act of 1872** to modernize the rules of evidence in India. It was passed by the **Parliament of India** and came into force on **July 1, 2024**.

• **Section 39** of the **BSA** defines an **expert** as a person who is especially skilled in a particular field. The scope of expert opinion under the **BSA** has been maintained to ensure continuity in legal interpretation while aligning with modern technological advancements.

• **Section 40** of the **BSA** mentions that facts which support or are inconsistent with the opinions of experts are also relevant. This allows the court to test the **credibility** and **consistency** of the expert's opinion against the broader context of the case.

• The **Supreme Court of India** has consistently held that expert opinion is a **'weak'** form of evidence. In the landmark case of **State of Himachal Pradesh v. Jai Lal**, it was emphasized that the expert must provide reasons for their opinion, and a mere assertion without supporting data is of little value to the **trial**.

• Common examples of expert evidence include **DNA profiling**, **ballistics reports**, **handwriting analysis**, and **digital forensic reports**. Under the **BSA**, there is an increased emphasis on **electronic and digital records**, making the role of **cyber experts** and **IT professionals** even more significant in modern judicial proceedings.
</ul

subject: GK
question: What is the significance of confessions made to police officers under the BSA 2023?

options.text: Inadmissible unless made in the presence of a magistrate

solution:
The correct answer is __**Inadmissible unless made in the presence of a magistrate**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023**, which replaced the **Indian Evidence Act, 1872**, governs the admissibility of evidence in **Indian courts**. Under **Section 23(1)** of the **BSA 2023**, it is clearly stated that no confession made to a **police officer** shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence.

• **Section 23(2)** of the **BSA 2023** further clarifies that no confession made by any person while they are in the **custody** of a **police officer** shall be proved against them, unless it is made in the immediate presence of a **Magistrate**. This provision acts as a safeguard against **custodial torture** and ensures that confessions are voluntary. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*

• The logic behind this rule is to prevent the **police** from using **coercion**, **threats**, or **physical violence** to extract statements from an **accused person**. Since the **police** have significant power over a person in **custody**, the law presumes that such confessions might not be **voluntary**.

• Option 1 suggests that such confessions are admissible only in **traffic cases**; however, the **BSA 2023** applies to all criminal trials, and the bar on **police confessions** is universal regardless of the nature of the crime. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

• Option 2 claims that confessions are automatically used as **judgment**; this is false because a confession is merely a piece of **evidence** that the **court** must evaluate for **truthfulness** and **reliability** before reaching a verdict. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

• Option 3 states that confessions to police are **fully admissible**; this contradicts the core **legal principles** of the **Indian justice system** which seeks to protect the **fundamental rights** of the accused. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023** received the **Presidential assent** on **December 25, 2023**, and officially came into force on **July 1, 2024**, marking a significant shift from **colonial-era laws**.

• While confessions to **police** are generally **inadmissible**, there is a vital exception under the **proviso** to **Section 23(2)** of the **BSA 2023** (formerly **Section 27** of the **IEA**). If a **fact** is discovered based on information provided by the **accused** in **custody**, that specific part of the information which relates distinctly to the **discovery** (such as the location of a **murder weapon**) is **admissible** in **court**.

• The protection against **self-incrimination** is a **fundamental right** guaranteed under **Article 20(3)** of the **Constitution of India**, which states that no person accused of an offence shall be compelled to be a **witness** against himself.

• The **BSA 2023** also modernizes **evidence law** by giving **electronic and digital records** the same legal standing as **paper documents**, acknowledging the role of **technology** in modern **criminal investigations**.

• A **confession** made to a **Magistrate** must follow the procedural requirements set out in the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023**, where the **Magistrate** must ensure the **accused** understands that the statement can be used against them in **trial**.

**Important Points__**

• **Judicial Confession**: These are confessions made before a **Magistrate** or in a **court** during the due course of **legal proceedings**. These carry high **evidentiary value** as they are presumed to be **voluntary**.

• **Extra-Judicial Confession**: These are confessions made to anyone other than a **Magistrate** or a **court**, such as a **friend**, **neighbor**, or **doctor**. While **admissible**, the **court** treats them with **caution** and usually requires **corroboration** from other **evidence**.

• **Retracted Confession**: If an **accused** person makes a **confession** but later denies it during the **trial**, it is called a **retracted confession**. The **court** can still convict based on it if it is satisfied that the **confession** was **true** and **voluntary** at the time it was made, though **corroboration** is typically sought.

• **Distinction from Admission**: While all **confessions** are **admissions**, not all **admissions** are **confessions**. An **admission** is a statement regarding a **fact in issue**, whereas a **confession** is a direct **acknowledgment of guilt** for the **crime** charged.
</ul

• A fundamental feature of the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam** is its explicit recognition of **electronic and digital records** as valid legal evidence. This modernization ensures that digital trails are treated with the same legal sanctity as physical documents. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• The Act expands the definition of a **document** to include any information generated, transmitted, or stored in any **electronic or digital form**, such as **emails**, **server logs**, and **smartphone messages**.

• Option 1 is incorrect because the Act specifically **includes** electronic records to keep pace with the digital age, rather than excluding them. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• Option 2 is incorrect because while the Act requires **certification** for the admissibility of digital records under **Section 63**, it does not mandate **notarization** as the standard procedure for all digital documents. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• Option 4 is incorrect because the Act **broadens** the scope and utility of electronic records, allowing them to be presented as **primary evidence** in most legal scenarios, rather than limiting their use. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**

__

• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam** was passed by the **Parliament of India** in **December 2023** and officially came into effect on **July 1, 2024**, marking a significant shift in the **criminal justice system**.

• Under **Section 2(1)(i)**, the term **document** now encompasses **digital records**, **locational data**, **voice mails**, and **cloud-stored information**, reflecting the reality of modern communication.

• The Act aligns the rules of evidence with the **Information Technology Act, 2000**, ensuring consistency across different legal frameworks regarding **cybercrimes** and **digital transactions**.

• It introduces provisions for **oral evidence** to be delivered through **electronic means**, which allows **witnesses**, **accused persons**, and **victims** to appear via **video conferencing**, thereby reducing delays in trials.

• The Act also clarifies the distinction between **primary** and **secondary evidence**, stating that **electronic records** produced from a computer resource are considered **primary evidence** if they meet specific criteria.

**Important Points__**

• **Section 63** of the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam** is a crucial provision that details the **admissibility of electronic records**. It mandates a **certificate** to be submitted to verify the authenticity of the digital data.

• This **certificate** must be signed by a person in a **responsible official position** or someone who manages the relevant **computer resource** or device from which the data originated.

• The Act recognizes a wide array of digital evidence, including **WhatsApp chats**, **call recordings**, **GPS data**, and **website logs**, which are vital for investigating **modern crimes**.

• By allowing **digital signatures** and **electronic logs** as evidence, the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam** facilitates a more **technology-driven** and efficient **judiciary** in **India**.

• The transition from the **1872 Act** to the **2023 Adhiniyam** is intended to remove **colonial-era** terminology and adapt the law to contemporary **socio-technological** conditions.
</ul

question: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains the distribution of powers between Union and States?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the allocation of powers and functions between the **Union** and the **States**. It contains three lists: **Union List**, **State List**, and **Concurrent List**.
 
• **Article 246** of the Indian Constitution provides the constitutional framework for this distribution, specifying that the **Parliament** has exclusive power to make laws on matters in the **Union List**, and **State Legislatures** have power over the **State List**.
 
• This schedule is a crucial feature of **Indian Federalism**, ensuring a clear demarcation of legislative jurisdiction to prevent administrative and legal conflicts between different levels of government.
 
• The **Union List** originally had **97 subjects** but currently contains **100 subjects**. The **State List** originally had **66 subjects** but now has **61 subjects**, and the **Concurrent List** originally had **47 subjects** but now consists of **52 subjects**.
 
• Any subject not mentioned in any of the three lists is considered a **Residuary Power**, which, according to **Article 248**, vests exclusively with the **Union Parliament**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union List (List I):**
 
 
• This list includes subjects of **national importance** where a uniform law is required across the **country**.
 
• Major subjects include **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, **Banking**, **Atomic Energy**, **Railways**, **Post and Telegraph**, **Census**, and **Insurance**.
 
• Only the **Central Government** has the authority to legislate on these matters.
 
 
 
• **State List (List II):**
 
 
• This list contains subjects of **regional and local importance**.
 
• Key subjects include **Police**, **Public Order**, **Public Health**, **Sanitation**, **Agriculture**, **Local Government**, and **Fisheries**.
 
• Under normal circumstances, only **State Governments** can pass laws on these subjects.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List (List III):**
 
 
• This list includes subjects where both the **Union** and the **States** have the power to legislate.
 
• Subjects include **Education**, **Forests**, **Marriage and Divorce**, **Trade Unions**, **Adoption**, and **Succession**.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** transferred five subjects from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**: **Education**, **Forests**, **Weights and Measures**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Administration of Justice**.
 
• In case of a conflict between a **Central law** and a **State law** on a concurrent subject, the **Central law** prevails.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sixth Schedule:** It contains provisions related to the administration of **Tribal Areas** in the **states** of **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Seventh Schedule:** It contains the three lists that distribute legislative power between the **Union** and the **States**. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Eighth Schedule:** It lists the **22 official languages** recognized by the **Constitution of India**, including **Assamese**, **Bengali**, **Hindi**, **Sanskrit**, **Tamil**, **Telugu**, etc. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Tenth Schedule:** Known as the **Anti-Defection Law**, it was added by the **52nd Amendment Act** in **1985** to prevent political defections. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• The distribution of powers is inspired by the **Government of India Act, 1935**, which also provided for a threefold enumeration of legislative subjects.
</ul

subject: GK
question: How many schedules are there in the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution of India** currently consists of **12 schedules**. These schedules are essentially supplementary tables that provide detailed information regarding various articles of the **Constitution**.
 
• At the time of its **adoption** on **26 November 1949** and its **commencement** on **26 January 1950**, the **Indian Constitution** contained only **8 schedules**.
 
• The increase from **8 to 12 schedules** occurred over time through various **Constitutional Amendment Acts** passed by the **Parliament of India** to address evolving administrative and political needs.
 
• The **9th Schedule** was added by the **1st Constitutional Amendment Act** in **1951**.
 
• The **10th Schedule**, known as the **Anti-Defection Law**, was added by the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in **1985**.
 
• The **11th Schedule** and **12th Schedule** were added by the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts** respectively in **1992**, focusing on **Panchayati Raj** and **Municipalities**.

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First to Fourth Schedules:**
 
 
• **First Schedule**: Lists the **States and Union Territories** of India and their **territorial jurisdictions**.
 
• **Second Schedule**: Contains provisions relating to the **emoluments, allowances, and privileges** of the **President**, **Governors**, **Speaker of Lok Sabha**, **Judges of Supreme Court**, and **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**.
 
• **Third Schedule**: Specifies the forms of **Oaths and Affirmations** for **Union Ministers**, **Members of Parliament**, and **Judges**.
 
• **Fourth Schedule**: Details the **allocation of seats** in the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States) to each **State and Union Territory**.
 
 
 
• **Fifth to Eighth Schedules:**
 
 
• **Fifth Schedule**: Deals with the **administration and control** of **Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• **Sixth Schedule**: Contains special provisions for the **administration of tribal areas** in the states of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• **Seventh Schedule**: Defines the **division of powers** between the Union and States through three lists: **Union List** (currently 100 subjects), **State List** (61 subjects), and **Concurrent List** (52 subjects).
 
• **Eighth Schedule**: Lists the **22 official languages** recognized by the **Indian Constitution**, including **Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, and Sanskrit**.
 
 
 
• **Ninth to Twelfth Schedules:**
 
 
• **Ninth Schedule**: Contains acts and regulations (originally **land reforms**) that are protected from **judicial review**. It was added in **1951**.
 
• **Tenth Schedule**: Contains provisions regarding **disqualification** of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of **defection**, introduced in **1985**.
 
• **Eleventh Schedule**: Specifies the **29 functional items** or powers of the **Panchayats**, added in **1992**.
 
• **Twelfth Schedule**: Specifies the **18 functional items** or powers of the **Municipalities**, added in **1992**.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The **Indian Constitution** is the **world longest written constitution**. As of **2024**, it has approximately **448 articles** grouped into **25 parts** and **12 schedules**.
 
• The **Drafting Committee**, headed by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, took **2 years, 11 months, and 18 days** to complete the **Constitution**.
 
• The **7th Schedule** is a critical feature of **Indian Federalism**, ensuring a clear **separation of powers** between the **Central Government** and **State Governments**.
 
• The **8th Schedule** originally had **14 languages**; others like **Sindhi, Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali** were added later through **amendments**.
</ul

question: In which year did the Indian Constitution come into effect?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1950**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution of India** officially came into effect on **January 26, 1950**. This date was specifically chosen to commemorate the declaration of **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence) by the **Indian National Congress** in **1930**.
 
• While the Constitution was **adopted** by the **Constituent Assembly** on **November 26, 1949**, it was legally enforced two months later to mark the historical significance of **Republic Day**. ***Hence, the option 1950 is correct.***
 
• With the enforcement of the Constitution, the **Government of India Act 1935** was repealed, and India transitioned from a **British Dominion** to a **Sovereign Democratic Republic**.
 
• The **Constituent Assembly** took precisely **2 years, 11 months, and 18 days** to complete the drafting of the world's lengthiest written constitution.
 
• At the time of its commencement in **1950**, the Constitution consisted of a **Preamble**, **395 Articles** (divided into **22 Parts**), and **8 Schedules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of other years mentioned in the options:**
 
 
• **1947:** This year marks the **Indian Independence Act**, through which India gained freedom from British rule on **August 15, 1947**. However, the country continued to be governed by modified colonial laws until the Constitution was enacted.
 
• **1949:** On **November 26, 1949**, the drafting process was finalized, and the document was signed by the members of the **Constituent Assembly**. This day is now celebrated annually as **Constitution Day** (Samvidhan Divas).
 
• **1952:** This year is significant as it saw the conclusion of India's **first General Elections** (held between October 1951 and February 1952) and the formation of the first democratically elected **Parliament** of India.
 
 
 
• **The Drafting Committee:**
 
 
• The **Drafting Committee**, which was responsible for preparing the final text, was chaired by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, who is recognized as the **Father of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• Other prominent members included **Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer**, **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar**, and **K.M. Munshi**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Original Manuscript:** The original Constitution of India was not printed but **handwritten** (calligraphed) in both **Hindi and English** by **Prem Behari Narain Raizada**.
 
• **Artistic Decoration:** Each page of the original document was uniquely decorated by artists from **Shantiniketan**, including **Nandalal Bose** and **Beohar Rammanohar Sinha**.
 
• **Universal Adult Franchise:** One of the most revolutionary features of the 1950 Constitution was the introduction of **Universal Adult Suffrage**, granting every citizen above a certain age (originally **21 years**, later reduced to **18 years** by the **61st Amendment**) the right to vote regardless of gender, caste, or education.
 
• **Borrowed Features:** The Indian Constitution is often described as a "bag of borrowings" because it incorporated best practices from various countries, such as **Parliamentary Democracy** from the **UK**, **Fundamental Rights** from the **USA**, and **Directive Principles** from **Ireland**.
</ul

subject: GK
question: The Constitution of India deals with the citizenship rights from Articles 5 to 11 under part ______.
solution:
The correct answer is__** II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 5-11**:

 
 
• **Part II** of the Constitution of India **(Articles 5-11)** deals with the **Citizenship of India**.
 
• **Article 5 **speaks about the** citizenship of India** at the commencement of the Constitution on** November 26, 1949**.
 
 
 
• **Article 5**:
 
 
• At the commencement of this Constitution, every person who has his **domicile **in the** territory of India** and –

 **(a)** who was **born in the territory of India**; or

 **(b)** either of **whose parents were born in the territory of India**; or

 **(c)** who has been **ordinarily resident in the territory of India for not less than five years** immediately preceding such commencement, shall be a citizen of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 6: RIGHTS OF CITIZENSHIP OF CERTAIN PERSONS WHO HAVE MIGRATED TO INDIA FROM PAKISTAN**
 
 
• a person who has** migrated **to the territory of India **from the territory now included in Pakistan** shall be **deemed to be a citizen of India** at the commencement of this Constitution if –

 **(a)** he or **either of his parents or any of his grand-parents was born in India** as defined in the** Government of India Act, 1935 **(as originally enacted); and

 **(b)(i)** in the case where such person has so** migrated before the nineteenth day of July 1948**, he has been ordinarily resident in the territory of India since the date of his migration, or

 **(ii)** in the case where such person has so migrated on or after the nineteenth day of July 1948, he has been registered as a citizen of India by an officer **appointed on that behalf by the Government of the Dominion of India **on an application made by him therefor to such officer before the commencement of this Constitution in the form and manner prescribed by that Government:

 Provided that no person shall be so registered unless he has been resident in the territory of India for** at least six months** immediately preceding the date of his application.
 
 
 
• **Article 7**: **RIGHTS OF CITIZENSHIP OF CERTAIN MIGRANTS TO PAKISTAN**
 
 
• a person who has **after the first day of March 1947**, **migrated from the territory of India to the territory now included in Pakistan shall not be deemed to be a citizen of India**:

 (a)Provided that nothing in this article shall apply to a person who, after having so migrated to the territory now included in Pakistan, has returned to the territory of India under a** permit for resettlement or permanent return **issued by or under the authority of any law and every such person shall for the purposes of clause.
 
• (b) of Article 6 be deemed to have migrated to the territory of India after the nineteenth day of July, 1948.
 
 
 
• **Article 8**:**RIGHTS OF CITIZENSHIP OF CERTAIN PERSONS OF INDIAN ORIGIN RESIDING OUTSIDE INDIA**
 
 
• any person who or either of whose** parents or any of whose grandparents** was **born in India** as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935 (as originally enacted), and who is **ordinarily residing in any country outside India** as so defined shall be **deemed to be a citizen** of India if he has been registered as a citizen of India by the **diplomatic or consular representative** of India in the country where he is for the time being residing on an application made by him therefor to such diplomatic or consular representative, whether before or after the commencement of this Constitution, in the form and manner prescribed by the Government of the Dominion of India or the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 9**:** PERSONS VOLUNTARILY ACQUIRING CITIZENSHIP OF A FOREIGN STATE NOT TO BE CITIZENS**
 
 
• No person shall be a citizen of India by article 5 or be deemed to be a citizen of India by article 6 or article 8 if **he has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of any foreign State**.
 
 
 
• **Article 10**:**CONTINUANCE OF THE RIGHTS OF CITIZENSHIP**
 
 
• Every person who is or is deemed to be a citizen of India under any of the foregoing provisions of this Part shall, subject to the provisions of any law that may be made by Parliament, continue to be such a citizen.
 
 
 
• **Article 11**:**PARLIAMENT TO REGULATE THE RIGHT OF CITIZENSHIP BY LAW**
 
 
• Nothing in the foregoing provisions of this Part shall derogate from the **power of Parliament to make any provision** concerning the **acquisition and termination of citizenship **and all other matters relating to citizenship.

question: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)** is a regional intergovernmental organization and geopolitical union of states in **South Asia**. It was established with the signing of the **SAARC Charter** in **Dhaka** on **8 December 1985**.
 
• The organization currently has **8 member countries**: **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• **Afghanistan** became the **8th member** of **SAARC** during the **14th SAARC Summit** held in **New Delhi** in **April 2007**. Prior to this, there were only seven founding members. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• **Bhutan** is one of the founding members of the association and has been an active participant since its inception in **1985**. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• **China** holds the status of an **Observer Country** in **SAARC**, but it is not a formal member of the association. The association currently has **9 observers**, including **Australia**, **China**, the **European Union**, **Iran**, **Japan**, **Mauritius**, **Myanmar**, **South Korea**, and the **United States**. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• **Nepal** is a founding member and currently hosts the **SAARC Secretariat**, which was established in **Kathmandu** on **16 January 1987**. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of SAARC:**
 
 
• The primary objective of **SAARC** is to promote the **welfare of the peoples of South Asia** and to improve their quality of life through **accelerated economic growth**, **social progress**, and **cultural development** in the region.
 
• It aims to provide all individuals the opportunity to live in dignity and to realize their full potentials by strengthening **collective self-reliance** among the countries of **South Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Secretariat and Administration:**
 
 
• The **SAARC Secretariat** is headed by a **Secretary-General**, who is appointed by the **Council of Ministers** from Member States in alphabetical order for a **three-year term**.
 
• The first **Secretary-General** was **Abul Ahsan** from **Bangladesh**. The current **Secretariat** is located in **Kathmandu**, **Nepal**.
 
 
 
• **Specialized Bodies of SAARC:**
 
 
• **South Asian University (SAU)**: An international university established by the eight member nations of **SAARC**, located in **India** (**New Delhi**).
 
• **SAARC Development Fund (SDF)**: Its primary objective is to promote the welfare of the people of the **SAARC region**, with its secretariat located in **Thimphu**, **Bhutan**.
 
• **SAARC Arbitration Council (SARCO)**: An inter-governmental body located in **Islamabad**, **Pakistan**, to provide a legal framework for the settlement of commercial and trade disputes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Principles of SAARC:**
 
 
• Cooperation within the framework of the association is based on respect for the principles of **sovereign equality**, **territorial integrity**, **political independence**, and **non-interference** in the internal affairs of other states.
 
• Decisions at all levels in **SAARC** are taken on the basis of **unanimity**, and **bilateral and contentious issues** are excluded from the deliberations of the association.
 
 
 
• **SAARC Charter Day:**
 
 
• Every **year**, **8 December** is observed as **SAARC Charter Day** to mark the adoption of the **SAARC Charter** in **1985**.
 
 
 
• **South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA):**
 
 
• **SAFTA** was reached at the **12th SAARC Summit** at **Islamabad**, **Pakistan** on **6 January 2004**. It aims to reduce **customs duties** of all traded goods to **zero percent** by the **year 2016**.
 
 
</ul

question: When was BIMSTEC established?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BIMSTEC**, which stands for the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**, was officially established on **6 June 1997**.
 
• The organization came into existence through the signing of the **Bangkok Declaration**, which served as the founding document for this regional group.
 
• Initially, the group was formed with four member states and was known as **BIST-EC** (**Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand** Economic Cooperation).
 
• Following the inclusion of **Myanmar** on **22 December 1997** during a special Ministerial Meeting in **Bangkok**, the group was renamed **BIMST-EC**.
 
• In **February 2004**, the organization expanded further as **Nepal** and **Bhutan** became full members, leading to the current name adopted during the first summit in **Bangkok**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographic Scope:** **BIMSTEC** is a unique regional organization that brings together seven countries from **South Asia** and **Southeast Asia**, creating a bridge between the two regions. Five members are from **South Asia** (**Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, and Sri Lanka**) and two are from **Southeast Asia** (**Myanmar and Thailand**).
 
• **Secretariat:** The permanent secretariat of **BIMSTEC** is located in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**. It was formally inaugurated in **2014** to coordinate the activities and implementation of various projects.
 
• **Areas of Cooperation:** Originally, the cooperation started with **six sectors** including **trade, technology, energy, transport, tourism, and fisheries**. It has since expanded to **14 sectors**, including **agriculture, public health, poverty alleviation, counter-terrorism, and climate change**.
 
• **Strategic Significance for India:** For **India**, **BIMSTEC** has become a primary platform for regional cooperation under its **Neighborhood First** and **Act East Policy**, especially as activities in **SAARC** (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) have remained stalled.
 
• **Economic Potential:** The **Bay of Bengal** region is home to approximately **1.5 billion people**, accounting for about **22% of the global population**, and has a combined **GDP** of over **USD 3.8 trillion** as of recent estimates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Institutional Reforms:** During the **5th BIMSTEC Summit** hosted virtually by **Sri Lanka** in **March 2022**, the **BIMSTEC Charter** was signed and adopted. This provided the organization with a formal legal identity and a specific flag and emblem.
 
• **Lead Countries:** Each member state leads specific pillars of cooperation. For instance, **India** leads the **Security** pillar, which includes **counter-terrorism, transnational crime, and disaster management**.
 
• **Connectivity:** A major focus of the group is the **BIMSTEC Master Plan for Transport Connectivity**, which aims to enhance physical connectivity through roads, railways, and maritime routes to boost regional trade.
 
• **Milestones:** The year **2022** marked the **25th anniversary** of the founding of **BIMSTEC**, highlighting a quarter-century of effort toward regional integration in the **Bay of Bengal** rim.
</ul

question: What is the primary focus of BIMSTEC?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Economic and technical cooperation**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BIMSTEC**, or the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**, is a regional organization comprising seven member countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand.
 
• The primary focus of BIMSTEC is on fostering **economic and technical cooperation** among member nations, with the aim of promoting shared growth and development.
 
• The organization aims to act as a bridge between South and Southeast Asia, leveraging the **Bay of Bengal region** as an area of cooperation and connectivity.
 
• BIMSTEC identifies key areas of cooperation, including **trade, investment, technology, energy, transport, and tourism**. These sectors are critical for improving economic ties and technical collaboration among member countries.
 
• The organization also focuses on enhancing **regional integration** and addressing common challenges such as **poverty, climate change, and natural disasters**.
 
• BIMSTEC is not a military or security alliance; its focus remains primarily on **economic and technical areas**, distinguishing it from other regional organizations.
 
• The organization facilitates **cooperation in science and technology**, including the exchange of expertise and resources to address technological needs in member states.

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of BIMSTEC:**

 
 
• BIMSTEC was established in **June 1997** through the **Bangkok Declaration**. Initially, it was known as the BIST-EC (Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand Economic Cooperation). Later, Myanmar joined in 1997, followed by Nepal and Bhutan in 2004, and the name was changed to BIMSTEC.
 
• The organization aims to promote **sub-regional cooperation** among countries bordering the Bay of Bengal, focusing on economic and technical collaboration.
 
 
 
• **Key Areas of Cooperation:**
 
 
• **Trade and Investment:** BIMSTEC works to enhance trade facilitation, reduce trade barriers, and promote investment opportunities among member countries.
 
• **Connectivity:** Improving transport and infrastructure networks, such as highways and maritime routes, is a crucial aspect of BIMSTEC's agenda.
 
• **Energy Cooperation:** The organization focuses on enhancing energy security, including the development of renewable energy sources like solar and wind power.
 
 
 
• **Difference from Other Organizations:**
 
 
• Unlike organizations like **SAARC**, which focus on political cooperation, BIMSTEC is primarily focused on **economic and technical collaboration**.
 
• BIMSTEC does not have a military focus, distinguishing it from organizations such as NATO or ASEAN’s security framework.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Key Facts about BIMSTEC:**

 
 
• BIMSTEC covers a population of approximately **1.7 billion people** (around 22% of the world's population) and has a combined GDP of over **US $4 trillion**.
 
• The headquarters of BIMSTEC is located in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**.
 
• BIMSTEC promotes **people-to-people contact** through cultural exchanges, tourism, and educational initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Challenges and Opportunities:**
 
 
• Challenges include **regional disparities**, political differences, and the need for stronger institutional frameworks.
 
• However, BIMSTEC offers significant opportunities for **regional integration**, sustainable development, and addressing shared challenges like **climate change** and **disaster management**.

__
 
• The **BRICS Business Council** was established in **2013** with the aim of fostering economic, trade, and investment cooperation among BRICS nations (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa).
 
• One of its primary focus areas is **infrastructure development**, which involves the construction and improvement of facilities such as transportation networks, energy projects, and urban development across member nations.
 
• The emphasis on **infrastructure** aligns with the shared goal of addressing the significant infrastructure deficit in BRICS countries, which is seen as a key barrier to sustainable economic growth.
 
• Projects supported by the BRICS Business Council often include major initiatives such as **transportation networks, renewable energy projects, and urban development**. These projects aim to improve connectivity and efficiency among member nations.
 
• The Council facilitates partnerships between governments and the private sector to fund and execute large-scale infrastructure projects, ensuring mutual benefit and sustainable development.
 
• In addition to infrastructure, the Council also focuses on other key sectors such as **manufacturing, technology, and financial services**, but infrastructure remains a primary area of concern due to its significant impact on the overall economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of the BRICS Business Council in Infrastructure:**

 
 
• The Council acts as a platform for dialogue and collaboration between the private and public sectors to promote **infrastructure development** in BRICS nations.
 
• It identifies potential projects, facilitates funding options, and ensures that projects align with the development goals of member countries.
 
• The Council also works to remove barriers to investment in infrastructure and improve the regulatory environment to attract foreign and domestic investors.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Infrastructure Development in BRICS Nations:**
 
 
• **Infrastructure development** is critical for enhancing economic growth, improving connectivity between regions, and ensuring sustainable urbanization.
 
• BRICS nations face significant challenges, such as **inadequate transportation systems, energy shortages, and urban congestion**. Addressing these issues is crucial for achieving long-term economic stability.
 
• Examples of major initiatives include China's **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**, India's **Smart Cities Mission**, and Brazil's infrastructure modernization projects.
 
 
 
• **Other Focus Areas of the BRICS Business Council:**
 
 
• Besides infrastructure, the Council promotes cooperation in sectors like **tourism, manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, and technology**.
 
• For example, the Council supports tourism initiatives to boost cultural exchange and economic growth, and technology projects to promote innovation and digital transformation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **New Development Bank (NDB):**

 
 
• The BRICS nations established the **New Development Bank** to provide financial support for infrastructure and sustainable development projects. Since its inception in **2014**, it has funded numerous projects across BRICS nations.
 
• The NDB complements the efforts of the BRICS Business Council by ensuring adequate funding for large-scale infrastructure projects.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact of BRICS Infrastructure Initiatives:**
 
 
• The infrastructure projects initiated by BRICS nations have a ripple effect on global trade and economic growth, as they improve connectivity and reduce logistical costs.
 
• For instance, China's Belt and Road Initiative, which involves several BRICS countries, has significantly enhanced global trade routes and supply chains.

question: Which modes of transport are included in the TEN-T(Trans-European Transport Network) network?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Roads, railways, airports, and waterways**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T)** is an ambitious initiative by the **European Union (EU)** designed to integrate and improve transportation infrastructure across Europe. It includes various modes of transport such as **roads, railways, airports, and waterways**.
 
• The aim of the TEN-T is to establish a unified and modern **transportation network** to enhance connectivity between regions, facilitate economic growth, and improve mobility across the EU.
 
• In addition to roads and railways, the TEN-T also incorporates the development of **airports and ports** to ensure a comprehensive, multimodal transport system. *Hence, the inclusion of all these modes of transport is correct.*
 
• The TEN-T network also includes **inland waterways**, which are essential for reducing congestion on roads and providing an environmentally sustainable mode of freight transport.
 
• The combination of roads, railways, airports, and waterways ensures a cohesive and balanced network that facilitates both passenger and freight transport. *Thus, the correct answer is option 2.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• **Objectives of the TEN-T Network:**

 
 
• The primary goal of the **TEN-T** is to enhance **transport integration** across the EU by connecting urban centers, ports, and airports and improving accessibility to remote regions.
 
• It aims to create a **multimodal transport system** that promotes economic growth, reduces environmental impact, and ensures efficient mobility for goods and passengers.
 
 
 
• **Features of the TEN-T Network:**
 
 
• The TEN-T consists of two main layers: the **Core Network** and the **Comprehensive Network**. The Core Network includes the most critical transport corridors, while the Comprehensive Network ensures connectivity to all regions.
 
• The network focuses on integrating **railways, roads, inland waterways, maritime shipping routes, and airports**.
 
• **Example:** The TEN-T includes major corridors such as the **North Sea-Baltic Corridor** and the **Scandinavian-Mediterranean Corridor**, which connect multiple regions across Europe.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Benefits:**
 
 
• The inclusion of **railways and waterways** in the network supports the EU's goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by promoting sustainable modes of transport.
 
• Efficient transport networks reduce congestion and reliance on fossil fuels, contributing to the EU’s **Green Deal objectives.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **Key Modes of Transport in the TEN-T Network:**

 
 
• **Roads:** Highways and motorways are a major component of the network, connecting urban and rural areas.
 
• **Railways:** High-speed and conventional rail networks ensure quick and efficient mobility of passengers and goods.
 
• **Airports:** The TEN-T includes airports to enhance air connectivity within Europe and to other continents.
 
• **Waterways:** Inland waterways and ports facilitate freight movement, reducing the load on road and rail networks.
 
 
 
• **Financing and Implementation:**
 
 
• The TEN-T network is supported by funding programs like the **Connecting Europe Facility (CEF)**, which provides financial assistance for infrastructure projects.
 
• **EU Member States** collaborate to implement and maintain the infrastructure projects under the network.

question: As per the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, how should every summons issued by a Court be formatted?

options.text: In duplicate, signed and sealed or sent via encrypted digital form
Only handwritten and sent via personal messenger from the Court
Verbal instructions delivered by an officer of the Court
Sealed envelope signed by any officer of the police station

solution:
The correct answer is __**In duplicate, signed and sealed or sent via encrypted digital form**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023** introduces several reforms and guidelines aimed at ensuring efficiency and transparency in legal processes in India.
 
• As per the act, every summons issued by the court must be **formatted in duplicate**, ensuring that one copy is retained for records while the other is sent to the recipient. This ensures transparency and accountability.
 
• The summons must be **signed and sealed** by the issuing authority, i.e., the court. This guarantees authenticity and prevents misuse or forgery. *Hence, this provision is mandatory.*
 
• Alternatively, summons can be sent in an **encrypted digital form**. This is in line with India’s push towards digitalization and ensures secure delivery of legal documents while maintaining authenticity.
 
• The use of **encrypted digital forms** also reduces delays caused by traditional modes of delivery, enhancing the efficiency of legal proceedings. *Hence, the correct answer aligns with modern legal and technological standards.*
 
• Options such as handwritten or verbal instructions (Option 2 and 3) are incorrect as they lack authenticity, security, and formal documentation. Similarly, Option 4 does not meet the mandated legal standards of signature and court seal. *Hence, these options are not valid as per the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.*

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Details of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023:**

 
 
• **Purpose:** The act seeks to streamline and modernize the criminal procedure code in India. It focuses on ensuring transparency, efficiency, and citizen-centric reforms in the justice delivery system.
 
• **Key Features:** The Sanhita emphasizes the use of modern technology, such as encrypted digital communication, to reduce delays and improve accuracy in legal documentation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Summons:**
 
 
• Summons is a legal document issued by a court to compel the appearance of an individual in a legal proceeding. It ensures that the person is informed of their legal obligations.
 
• **Proper Format:** A summons must be issued in a manner that ensures authenticity, security, and proper documentation, as required by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
 
 
 
• **Encrypted Digital Forms:**
 
 
• **Advantages:** Using encrypted digital forms for summons delivery ensures faster communication, reduces paperwork, and minimizes the chances of tampering.
 
• **Implementation:** Courts and legal authorities are increasingly adopting secure digital platforms to comply with modern legal standards and enhance efficiency.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Reforms:**

 
 
• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, emphasizes citizen-centric reforms, including the use of technology to simplify legal processes and reduce delays.
 
• **Digital Integration:** The act aligns with India’s Digital India initiative by promoting the use of encrypted digital communication in legal procedures.
 
 
 
• **Authenticity and Security:**
 
 
• The requirement for signed and sealed summons ensures that legal documents are authentic and cannot be misused.
 
• **Encrypted Digital Summons:** This modern approach prevents unauthorized access or tampering, ensuring secure communication between courts and individuals.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhaka, Bangladesh**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **BIMSTEC Secretariat** is located in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**. It serves as the central administrative hub for the regional organization, facilitating coordination among member states and managing the implementation of various projects. ***Hence, this option is correct.***

• The Secretariat was formally inaugurated on **13 September 2014** by the Prime Minister of **Bangladesh**, **Sheikh Hasina**. Before its establishment, the organization operated without a permanent headquarters for nearly **17 years** since its formation in **1997**.

• **New Delhi, India**: While **India** is a founding member and a major contributor to the organization, it does not host the central Secretariat. **India** leads the **Security** pillar of **BIMSTEC**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• **Bangkok, Thailand**: This city is significant as the birthplace of the organization where the **Bangkok Declaration** was signed on **6 June 1997**. However, it is not the seat of the permanent Secretariat. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• **Colombo, Sri Lanka**: **Sri Lanka** is an active member and hosted the **5th BIMSTEC Summit** in **2022**, but the permanent administrative office is not situated here. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• The **Secretary General** of **BIMSTEC** heads the Secretariat and is appointed for a tenure of **three years**. The first Secretary General was **Sumith Nakandala** from **Sri Lanka**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **BIMSTEC** stands for the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**. It is a unique regional multilateral organization that bridges **South Asia** and **Southeast Asia**.

• The organization currently comprises **seven member states**: **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Myanmar**, **Nepal**, **Sri Lanka**, and **Thailand**. It was originally established as **BIST-EC** (Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand Economic Cooperation).

• The **BIMSTEC** region is home to approximately **1.8 billion people**, which accounts for roughly **22%** of the global population. The combined **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** of the member nations is estimated at **USD 4.5 trillion**.

• The primary objectives of the group include promoting rapid economic development, accelerating social progress, and enhancing cooperation in areas of common interest such as **Trade**, **Investment**, **Technology**, and **Energy**.

• The chairmanship of **BIMSTEC** rotates among the member states in alphabetical order. **Thailand** assumed the chairmanship for the **2022-2024** cycle.

**Important Points__**

• A major milestone was the signing of the **BIMSTEC Charter** during the **5th Summit** in **Colombo** on **30 March 2022**. This charter provides the organization with a formal legal identity and a defined institutional structure.

• The current **Secretary General** is **Indra Mani Pandey**, a senior diplomat from **India**, who took charge in **January 2024**. He is the fourth person to hold this prestigious designation.

• Cooperation within **BIMSTEC** was reorganized into **seven pillars** in **2021**. Each member state leads a specific pillar; for example, **India** leads **Security**, **Thailand** leads **Connectivity**, and **Bangladesh** leads **Trade, Investment, and Development**.

• Key connectivity projects under the **BIMSTEC** framework include the **Kaladan Multi-modal Transit Transport Project** and the **Asian Trilateral Highway**, which aim to link **India** with **Southeast Asian** nations.

• The organization serves as a strategic alternative for regional cooperation, especially given the stagnation of **SAARC** (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) in recent years.
</ul

subject: GK
question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the provisions of the POSH Act, 2013?

options.text: The POSH Act, 2013 is designed to prevent child marriage in India.
The POSH Act, 2013 provides protection against sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
The POSH Act, 2013 governs the regulation of orphanages across India.
The POSH Act, 2013 focuses on the harassment of domestic workers.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The POSH Act, 2013 provides protection against sexual harassment of women at the workplace**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act**, commonly known as the **POSH Act**, was enacted by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** in **2013** to ensure a safe and secure environment for women in their professional lives.

• **Statement 1**: The **POSH Act, 2013** is designed to prevent child marriage in India. This statement is incorrect because the prevention of child marriage is governed by the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**, which sets the legal age for marriage. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 2**: The **POSH Act, 2013** provides protection against sexual harassment of women at the workplace. This is the fundamental purpose of the legislation, which seeks to uphold the **fundamental right** of women to equality and a dignified livelihood as guaranteed under **Article 14, 15, and 21** of the **Constitution of India**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

• **Statement 3**: The **POSH Act, 2013** governs the regulation of orphanages across India. This statement is incorrect as the care, protection, and regulation of orphanages and children in need are handled under the **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 4**: The **POSH Act, 2013** focuses on the harassment of domestic workers. While the act specifically includes **domestic workers** within its definition of an **aggrieved woman** and a **dwelling place** as a **workplace**, the act is a broad legislation covering all types of workplaces, not just domestic settings. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct but is a specific subset of the broader protection mentioned in statement 2.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Vishaka Guidelines**: The **POSH Act** is rooted in the **Vishaka Guidelines** formulated by the **Supreme Court of India** in **1997** following the landmark case of **Vishaka vs. State of Rajasthan**. These guidelines remained the law of the land for **16 years** until the formal act was passed in **2013**.

• **Internal Committee (IC)**: Every employer who has **10 or more employees** is legally mandated to constitute an **Internal Committee** at each branch or office to receive and redress complaints of sexual harassment.

• **Local Committee (LC)**: For establishments with fewer than **10 employees**, or if the complaint is against the employer himself, the **District Officer** (usually the **District Magistrate** or **Additional District Magistrate**) is required to constitute a **Local Committee** in every district.

• **Definition of Workplace**: The act defines **workplace** very broadly, including **private sector organizations**, **government bodies**, **hospitals**, **sports institutes**, **stadiums**, and any place visited by the employee during the course of employment, including **transportation** provided by the employer.

• **Definition of Sexual Harassment**: It includes unwelcome acts such as **physical contact**, a demand or **request for sexual favors**, **sexually colored remarks**, showing **pornography**, or any other unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.

**Important Points__**

• **Aggrieved Woman**: Under the **POSH Act**, an **aggrieved woman** is defined as a woman of **any age**, whether employed or not, who alleges to have been subjected to any act of sexual harassment by the respondent. This includes **regular**, **temporary**, **ad hoc**, or **daily wage** employees.

• **Complaint Timeline**: A written complaint must be filed with the **Internal Committee** or **Local Committee** within a period of **3 months** from the date of the incident. In the case of a series of incidents, it must be within **3 months** from the date of the last incident.

• **Redressal Process**: Before starting an inquiry, the committee can, at the request of the woman, attempt to settle the matter through **conciliation**. However, no **monetary settlement** can be made the basis of such conciliation. If conciliation is not possible, a formal inquiry is conducted within **90 days**.

• **SHe-Box Portal**: To facilitate the registration of complaints, the **Government of India** launched the **Sexual Harassment electronic Box (SHe-Box)**, an online portal that allows women in both **public and private sectors** to report incidents directly to the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**.

• **Penalties**: Non-compliance with the provisions of the act, such as failure to constitute an **Internal Committee**, can result in a fine of up to **50,000 rupees** for the employer, and repeated offenses can lead to the **cancellation of the business license**.
</ul

question: The Election Commission of India was established in ________.

The correct answer is __**1950**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Election Commission of India **was established in **1950**.
 
• **The Election Commission of India (ECI) **is a **constitutional body **established by the **Constitution of India **with the **mandate to oversee and regulate elections **throughout the country.
 
• **Article 324** of the Constitution empowers the Election Commission with the authority and responsibility for the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to various offices, including parliament, state legislatures, the presidency, and the vice presidency.
 
• As such, the Election Commission functions as a nationwide entity, serving **both the Central government and the state governments**.
 
• This esteemed body administers elections for a multitude of governmental positions, including the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, State Legislative Councils, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President of the nation.
 
• The Election Commission operates within the framework provided by the Constitution, as stipulated in Article 324, and implements relevant electoral laws such as the Representation of the People Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Established in 1950, the Election Commission initially comprised only** one Chief Election Commissioner.**
 
• However, on **October 16, 1989, ahead of the 1989 General Election,** two additional Commissioners were appointed, albeit for a brief period until January 1, 1990.
 
• Subsequently, the** Election Commissioner Amendment Act, 1989,** was enacted, transforming the commission into a multi-member body. Since then, a three-member Commission has been operational, with decisions made through majority voting.
 
• Situated in New Delhi, the commission is supported by its secretariat. Assisting the Election Commissioners are Deputy Election Commissioners, typically comprising Indian Administrative Service officers.
 
• **Rajiv Kumar**, a former Indian Administrative Service officer born on February 19, 1960, assumed office as the 25th Chief Election Commissioner of India on May 15, 2022, succeeding Sushil Chandra.
