question: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to transfer cases from one High Court to another and on what grounds?

options.text: Article 139A; for ensuring justice and expeditious trial

solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 139A; for ensuring justice and expeditious trial**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 139A** of the **Constitution of India** specifically empowers the **Supreme Court** to transfer cases from one **High Court** to another or to withdraw cases to itself.
 
• This power can be exercised if the **Supreme Court** is satisfied that cases involving the same or substantially the same **questions of law** are pending before it and one or more **High Courts**, or before two or more **High Courts**.
 
• The primary grounds for such a transfer are to ensure **justice** and the **expeditious trial** or disposal of cases, preventing conflicting judgments on identical legal issues. ***Hence, the correct answer is Article 139A; for ensuring justice and expeditious trial.***
 
• The **Supreme Court** may exercise this authority **suo motu** (on its own motion) or based on an application filed by the **Attorney-General of India** or by a party involved in any such case.
 
• This provision was inserted into the **Constitution** by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, to streamline the judicial process and maintain consistency in the interpretation of law across the **country**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 226:**
 
 
• This article empowers the **High Courts** of **India** with **Writ Jurisdiction**.
 
• It allows **High Courts** to issue directions, orders, or writs (such as **Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**, **Quo Warranto**, **Prohibition**, and **Certiorari**) for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** and for any other purpose.
 
• Unlike the **Supreme Court's** power under **Article 32**, the power under **Article 226** is broader as it covers non-fundamental legal rights as well. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect in the context of case transfer between High Courts.***
 
 
 
• **Article 142:**
 
 
• This article provides the **Supreme Court** with the power to pass such **decrees** or orders as may be necessary for doing **"complete justice"** in any cause or matter pending before it.
 
• While it is a unique and wide-ranging power, it is generally used for providing equitable relief and enforcing its own orders rather than the specific statutory mechanism for transferring cases between different **High Courts**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Article 131:**
 
 
• This article deals with the **Original Jurisdiction** of the **Supreme Court**.
 
• It covers **disputes** between the **Government of India** and one or more **States**, or between two or more **States**.
 
• It serves as a forum for resolving federal conflicts but does not relate to the procedural transfer of civil or criminal cases between **High Courts**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:** This amendment is often called the **"Mini-Constitution"** due to the vast changes it brought, including the insertion of **Article 139A**.
 
• **Role of the Attorney General:** The **Attorney-General of India** plays a crucial role in **Article 139A** by identifying cases of **national importance** or widespread legal impact that require a unified decision by the **Apex Court**.
 
• **Expeditious Disposal:** One of the key **features** of **Article 139A** is to reduce **pendency** and ensure that similar legal questions are not litigated repeatedly in different jurisdictions, thereby saving the time of the **judiciary** and the litigants.
 
• **Independence of Judiciary:** These powers ensure that the **Supreme Court** remains the final arbiter and maintains a **harmonious** legal environment across all **Indian states**.
</ul

question: In case of a conflict between Central and State law on a Concurrent List subject, the State law prevails only if:

options.text: It is passed by a two-thirds majority
It is supported by a Supreme Court ruling

solution:
The correct answer is __**It has received Presidential assent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In India, the **Concurrent List** refers to subjects on which both the **Central and State governments** can legislate, as per the **Seventh Schedule of the Constitution**.
 
• When there is a conflict between a **Central law** and a **State law** on a matter in the Concurrent List, the **Central law generally prevails** under **Article 254(1)** of the Constitution.
 
• However, if a **State law** that is inconsistent with a **Central law** has been passed and subsequently **receives Presidential assent**, it will prevail in that particular state under **Article 254(2)**. This is an exception to the general rule.
 
• The Presidential assent allows the State law to override the Central law, but the overriding effect is limited to the territory of that specific state.
 
• This provision reflects the federal nature of India's governance, allowing states some flexibility in dealing with matters where there may be unique regional requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concurrent List under the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• The **Concurrent List** is one of the three lists under the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution, alongside the Union List and the State List.
 
• Subjects in the Concurrent List include matters such as **education, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy, forests, and criminal law**, where both the Center and States can legislate.
 
• This list allows for **cooperative federalism**, ensuring both levels of government can address issues of national and regional importance.
 
 
 
• **Presidential Assent:**
 
 
• **Presidential assent** is the approval given by the President of India for a bill passed by a state legislature that conflicts with an existing Central law.
 
• Under **Article 254(2)**, once a state bill receives Presidential assent, it can prevail within that specific state even if it is inconsistent with the Central law.
 
• This mechanism ensures a balance between the **autonomy of states** and the overarching authority of the Central government.
 
 
 
• **Article 254 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• **Article 254(1):** If there is a conflict between laws made by the Center and the State on a Concurrent List subject, the Central law will prevail.
 
• **Article 254(2):** A State law that conflicts with a Central law can prevail in the state if it receives Presidential assent, but this does not affect the validity of the Central law in other parts of the country.
 
• This provision highlights India's **quasi-federal structure**, where states have limited autonomy in legislative matters.
 
 
 
• **Examples of State Override:**
 
 
• One notable example is the **Maharashtra Animal Preservation Act**, which received Presidential assent and prevails over Central laws related to animal preservation in Maharashtra.
 
• Such instances underscore the importance of Presidential assent in addressing **regional legislative priorities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the President:**

 
 
• The President's role in granting assent is crucial as it ensures the **constitutional validity** of laws enacted by state legislatures that may conflict with Central laws.
 
• By granting assent, the President upholds the principles of **federalism** while ensuring the legislative needs of individual states are met.
 
 
 
• **Union vs State Legislation:**
 
 
• The Union List contains subjects exclusively legislated by the Center, while the State List is reserved for state legislatures.
 
• The Concurrent List serves as a **shared domain**, enabling both levels of government to legislate on crucial subjects.
 
• Conflicts are resolved through mechanisms like **Presidential assent** or judicial review.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**
 
 
• The judiciary plays a significant role in interpreting **Article 254** and resolving disputes related to legislative conflicts.
 
• Several landmark cases have clarified the scope and application of state laws that override Central laws with Presidential assent.

question:
Match the following Articles with their provisions:

A. Article 50 1. Original jurisdiction of Supreme Court

B. Article 131 2. Separation of Judiciary from Executive

C. Article 312 3. Creation of All India Services

D. Article 263 4. Inter-State Council
solution:
The correct answer is __**A - 2, B - 1, C - 3, D - 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 50 - Separation of Judiciary from Executive**:

 
 
• **Article 50** is a part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** under **Part IV** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• It mandates that the **State** shall take steps to separate the **judiciary** from the **executive** in the public services of the State to ensure **judicial independence**.
 
• The separation is vital for the **Rule of Law** and to prevent the interference of the executive in the administration of justice. *Hence, the match A-2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 131 - Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court**:
 
 
• **Article 131** deals with the **Original Jurisdiction** of the **Supreme Court of India**, meaning cases that can be brought directly to the Supreme Court.
 
• This jurisdiction covers **federal disputes** such as those between the **Government of India** and one or more **States**, or between two or more **States**.
 
• It serves as the mechanism for resolving legal conflicts involving the **units of the Indian federation**. *Hence, the match B-1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 312 - All India Services**:
 
 
• **Article 312** empowers the **Parliament of India** to create **All India Services** common to both the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• A new **All India Service** can be created only if the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution supported by not less than **two-thirds** of the members present and voting.
 
• Currently, there are three All India Services: **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)**, **Indian Police Service (IPS)**, and **Indian Forest Service (IFoS)**. *Hence, the match C-3 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 263 - Inter-State Council**:
 
 
• **Article 263** provides for the establishment of an **Inter-State Council** to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• The **President of India** is authorized to establish this council by an **Executive Order** if it appears that the **public interest** would be served.
 
• The primary function of the council is to promote **cooperative federalism** and ensure better **coordination** of policy and action. *Hence, the match D-4 is correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Federalism and Article 131**:

 
 
• The **Original Jurisdiction** excludes disputes arising out of any **pre-Constitution treaty**, agreement, or covenant.
 
• In **1977**, in the case of **State of Rajasthan v. Union of India**, the scope of **Article 131** was extensively discussed regarding the **President's power** to dissolve State Assemblies.
 
 
 
• **History of All India Services (Article 312)**:
 
 
• The **Indian Forest Service** was the third service added to the list of All India Services in the year **1966** under the **All India Services Act, 1951**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** holds special power under **Article 312**, which reflects the **federal character** of the Indian Constitution as it represents the interests of the **States**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Inter-State Council (Article 263)**:
 
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission (1983-1988)** strongly recommended the establishment of a permanent **Inter-State Council**.
 
• Following these recommendations, the **Inter-State Council** was finally established by a **Presidential Order** on **28th May 1990**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** acts as the **Chairman** of the Council, while **Chief Ministers** of all States and **Union Territories** are its members.
 
 
 
• **DPSP and Judicial Independence**:
 
 
• While **Article 50** is a **Directive Principle** (and thus non-justiciable), it influenced the **Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), 1973**, which effectively separated the **judicial functions** from **executive magistrates** at the district level.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Summary of Articles**:

 
 
• **Article 50**: Promotes the **separation of powers** between the executive and judiciary.
 
• **Article 131**: Provides a legal forum for **Inter-State** and **Center-State** disputes.
 
• **Article 312**: Highlights the unique legislative power of the **Upper House (Rajya Sabha)**.
 
• **Article 263**: Acts as a bridge for **administrative and political cooperation** in a federal setup.

question: Which state has a bicameral legislature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maharashtra** has a **bicameral legislature**, which means it consists of two houses: the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** and the **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• **Tamil Nadu** currently has a **unicameral legislature**. The **Tamil Nadu Legislative Council** was abolished in **1986** via the **Tamil Nadu Legislative Council (Abolition) Act, 1986**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **West Bengal** has a **unicameral legislature**. Its **Legislative Council** was abolished in **1969**. Although the state assembly passed a resolution to create a council again in **July 2021**, it has not yet received **Parliamentary** approval. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Gujarat** has a **unicameral legislature** with only a **Legislative Assembly** consisting of **182 members**. It does not have a **Legislative Council**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• At present, only **six states** in India have a **bicameral legislature**: **Andhra Pradesh**, **Bihar**, **Karnataka**, **Maharashtra**, **Telangana**, and **Uttar Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 168** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the constitution of **Legislatures** in States, specifying which states have one house and which have two.
 
• **Article 169** grants the **Parliament** the power to **create or abolish** a **Legislative Council** in a state if the **Legislative Assembly** of that state passes a resolution by a **special majority** (a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and a majority of not less than **two-thirds** of the members present and voting).
 
• The **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)** is the **Upper House**, and the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** is the **Lower House**.
 
• The **Legislative Council** is a **permanent body** and is not subject to dissolution; however, **one-third** of its members retire every **second year**.
 
• The **maximum strength** of the **Legislative Council** is fixed at **one-third** of the total strength of the **Legislative Assembly**, and the **minimum strength** is **40 members**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The members of the **Legislative Council (MLCs)** are elected and nominated as follows: **1/3** by local bodies, **1/3** by **MLAs**, **1/12** by **graduates** of at least three years standing, **1/12** by **teachers** (secondary school or higher), and **1/6** are nominated by the **Governor**.
 
• To be eligible for membership in the **Legislative Council**, a person must be a **citizen of India**, at least **30 years of age**, and must be a registered voter in the state. The **tenure** of an **MLC** is **6 years**.
 
• The **Governor** nominates members to the **Legislative Council** from among persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as **Literature**, **Science**, **Art**, **Co-operative Movement**, and **Social Service**.
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir** also had a **bicameral legislature** until the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**, which converted the state into two **Union Territories** and abolished its **Legislative Council**.

question: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act passed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Parliament **passed the **Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014,** which was subsequently approved by the President on **March 1, 2014**.
 
• This act, commonly referred to as the **Telangana Act,** came into effect on June 2, 2014, leading to the formation of two new states:** Telangana and the remaining part of Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• The enactment of this legislation was a response to the Telangana movement, which advocated for the creation of a separate state of Telangana.
 
• As a result, the state of Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated into Telangana and the residual Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, mandates the division of assets, liabilities, employees, and contracts between the two newly formed states, ensuring a smooth transition and administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In August 2013, the **Union Cabinet** established a **Group of Ministers (GoM)** committee to assess the feasibility of dividing Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The committee was chaired by the Union Home Minister, Sushil Kumar Shinde. Other members of the committee included the Finance Minister, P. Chidambaram, the Health Minister, Ghulam Nabi Azad, the Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister, Veerappa Moily, the Union Rural Development Minister, Jairam Ramesh, and the Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Narayanaswamy.
 
• The committee's objective was to examine various aspects of the potential division, drawing insights from the findings of the Srikrishna committee on Telangana.

 __

__
 
• A state government's **advocate general** is a legal advisor. The post was formed by the Indian Constitution (see **Article 165**) and is equivalent to the position of **Attorney General for India at the federal level**.
 
• **The Advocate General **is appointed by the Governor of each state and must be eligible to serve as a High Court judge.
 
• The Attorney General of India is governed by** Article 76** of the Indian Constitution, whereas the Advocate General of India is governed by **Article 165**.
 
• Because the former is the chief law officer of the state and the latter is the highest law officer of India, the offices of Advocate General of State and Attorney General of India are interchangeable.

• **The Indian President **selects **Governors **for each state by a warrant signed and sealed by him. Each state's governor is appointed by the federal government.
 
• The Governor's post has no set term because he serves at the pleasure of the President. The President has the power to remove the Governor, and the grounds for his removal are not specified in the constitution.
 
• The President may also transfer the Governor from one state to another. He can also be reappointed.

question: Which is NOT correct about the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?

__
 
• There are three structures of jurisdiction for the Supreme Court:** Original, Appeal and Advisory.**
 
• A court has original jurisdiction if it is the **first court to hear a case.** 
 
• The SC has original jurisdiction in cases requiring foreign dignitaries, **one or more states, or cases requiring other public ministers.**
 
• The word original jurisdiction mentions to the question of which court has the authority to hear a **legal case for the first time.**

 The Supreme Court has original, appellate and advisory jurisdiction. 
 
• Its exclusive original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more States on the other or between two or more States, if and insofar as the dispute involves any question (whether of law or fact) on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends. 
 
• In addition, Article 32 of the Constitution gives an extensive original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 
 
• It is empowered to issue directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari to enforce them. 
 
• The Supreme Court has been conferred with power to direct transfer of any civil or criminal case from one High Court to another High Court or from a Court subordinate to another High Court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court** can hear any dispute between the Government of India and one or more states.**
 
• Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court **can hear any dispute between the Government of India and any state or states on one side and one or more states on the other.**
 
• ​Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court **can hear any dispute between two or more states**.

• **Article 53** of the Constitution of India states that the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President.
 
• The President can exercise these powers either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.
 
• This article is a part of the larger framework that outlines the powers and duties of the executive branch of the government.
 
• It ensures that the executive authority is centralized under the President, thereby providing a unified command structure.

• The President is elected by an electoral college comprising the elected members of both houses of Parliament and the legislative assemblies of states and union territories.
 
• The executive power extends to the matters with respect to which Parliament has the power to make laws and to the exercise of such rights, authority, and jurisdiction as are exercisable by the Government of India by virtue of any treaty or agreement.
 
• The President also has the power to appoint the Prime Minister, who acts as the head of government, and other ministers based on the Prime Minister's advice.
 
• The Constitution of India provides a detailed framework for the distribution of powers between the executive, legislative, and judiciary branches to ensure a balanced governance structure.

question: Article 171 deals with ________.

options.text: qualifications of the Chief Minister of a State
qualifications of the Governor of a State

solution:
The correct answer is __**composition of the Legislative Councils**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 171** of the Indian Constitution deals with the **composition of the Legislative Councils**.
 
• The Legislative Council is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• According to Article 171, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a state shall not exceed one-third of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that state.
 
• The members of the Legislative Council are elected by various groups including the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, and local authority members.
 
• The Governor of the state also nominates some members to the Legislative Council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 168** of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Legislative Council in states.
 
• The creation or abolition of the Legislative Council in a state can be done by Parliament on the basis of a resolution passed by the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
• Currently, six states in India have a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The Legislative Council is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.

• The Governor has both executive and legislative powers, including giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature, issuing ordinances, and making recommendations for President's Rule in the state.
 
• In addition to proroguing the House, the Governor can also dissolve the legislative assembly, usually upon the advice of the Chief Minister.
 
• The **Governor** plays a crucial role in maintaining the constitutional framework and ensuring the smooth functioning of the state government.

question: Who is considered as the ‘linchpin of the Government’?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The **Prime Minister** is considered the 'linchpin of the Government'.
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government and is responsible for running the government and implementing laws.
 
• The Prime Minister leads the executive branch of the government and is the chief advisor to the President.
 
• The Prime Minister plays a crucial role in formulating and executing government policies and decisions.
 
• As the leader of the majority party in the Parliament, the Prime Minister ensures the stability and functionality of the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In case of a coalition government, the Prime Minister is usually the leader of the largest party in the coalition.
 
• The Prime Minister plays a key role in the appointment of various constitutional and statutory bodies.

subject: GK
question: Which of the following topics falls under the State List as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Police and public order**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Article 246** of the **Constitution of India** distributes the legislative powers between the **Union** and the **States** through the **Seventh Schedule**, which contains three distinct lists.

• **Police and public order** are subjects specifically mentioned under the **State List** (List II). **Public Order** is listed as **Entry 1** and **Police** (including railway and village police) is listed as **Entry 2**. This means the **State Government** has the exclusive power to legislate on these matters. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*

• **Defense and Armed Forces** of the Union, including the preparation for defense and all such acts as may be conducive in times of war, fall under **Entry 1** of the **Union List** (List I). Only the **Parliament** can make laws regarding the **military**, **naval**, and **air forces**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

• **Foreign affairs and international treaties**, including all matters which bring the **Union** into relation with any **foreign country**, are covered under **Entries 10 to 14** of the **Union List**. This ensures a unified **foreign policy** for the **nation**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

• **Currency, coinage, and legal tender**; foreign exchange and the **Reserve Bank of India** are subjects under **Entry 36** of the **Union List**. This allows the **Central Government** to maintain a uniform **monetary system** across the **country**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Union List** (List I) consists of subjects of **national importance**. It originally contained **97 subjects**, but currently, it has **100 subjects**. Major entries include **Atomic Energy**, **Railways**, **Post and Telegraph**, **Banking**, and **Census**.

• The **State List** (List II) comprises subjects of **local or regional importance**. It originally had **66 subjects**, but after various amendments, it now contains **61 subjects**. Key entries include **Agriculture**, **Public Health**, **Sanitation**, **Local Government**, **Fisheries**, and **Markets**.

• The **Concurrent List** (List III) includes subjects where both the **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** can legislate. It has **52 subjects** (originally **47**). In case of a conflict between a **Central law** and a **State law** on a concurrent subject, the **Central law** generally prevails. Examples include **Education**, **Forests**, **Marriage and Divorce**, and **Trade Unions**.

• The **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** was a landmark legislation that transferred five subjects from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**: **Education**, **Forests**, **Weights and Measures**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Administration of Justice**.

• **Residuary Powers** refer to the power to legislate on any matter not enumerated in any of the three lists. According to **Article 248**, these powers are exclusively vested in the **Parliament of India**.

**Important Points__**

• Although **Police** is a **State subject**, the **Union Government** maintains several **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF)** such as the **Border Security Force (BSF)**, **Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)**, and **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)** to assist states in maintaining **internal security** and guarding **borders**.

• In certain **Union Territories** like **Delhi**, the legislative and executive power over **Police**, **Public Order**, and **Land** is reserved for the **Central Government** (Ministry of Home Affairs) under **Article 239AA** of the **Constitution**.

• The **Sarkaria Commission** (established in **1983**) and the **Punchhi Commission** (established in **2007**) were appointed to examine **Centre-State relations** and suggested that the **Seventh Schedule** should be periodically reviewed to ensure it reflects the changing **socio-economic** needs of the **country**.

• The **Seventh Schedule** is a key feature of **Indian Federalism**, ensuring a clear **division of powers** to prevent **administrative** overlaps and conflicts between different levels of **government**.
</ul

subject: GK
question: In India, which of the following statement is correct about the financial relation between the Center and the States?

options.text: The Union Government has exclusive control over all types of taxation, including state taxes.
The States have no role in the allocation of taxes and resources, and all funds are directly managed by the Union.
The Union Government collects taxes and distributes them between the Union and the States through the Finance Commission.
States have the authority to impose taxes on defense, currency, and foreign trade.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union Government collects taxes and distributes them between the Union and the States through the Finance Commission**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The financial relations between the **Union** and the **States** are primarily governed by **Articles 264 to 293** in **Part XII** of the **Constitution of India**. The **Constitution** provides for a clear division of taxing powers between the two levels of government to ensure fiscal federalism.

• Statement 1: The **Union Government** has exclusive control over all types of taxation, including state taxes. This is incorrect because the **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution** divides the power to levy taxes into three lists: the **Union List**, the **State List**, and the **Concurrent List**. **States** have the exclusive power to tax items like **land revenue**, **agricultural income**, and **state excise duties** on alcoholic liquors. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• Statement 2: The **States** have no role in the allocation of taxes and resources, and all funds are directly managed by the **Union**. This is incorrect because **States** manage their own **Consolidated Fund of the State** and play a vital role in the **GST Council** and the **Finance Commission** deliberations to determine resource sharing. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• Statement 3: The **Union Government** collects taxes and distributes them between the **Union** and the **States** through the **Finance Commission**. This is correct as **Article 280** mandates the **President of India** to constitute a **Finance Commission** every **five years** to recommend the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the **Center** and the **States**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• Statement 4: **States** have the authority to impose taxes on **defense**, **currency**, and **foreign trade**. This is incorrect because these subjects are part of the **Union List (List I)**, and only the **Parliament of India** has the authority to legislate and levy taxes on these national importance matters. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Finance Commission**: It is a **constitutional body** established under **Article 280**. The **15th Finance Commission**, chaired by **N.K. Singh**, recommended a **41%** share of the divisible pool of central taxes for **States** for the period **2021-2026**. The **16th Finance Commission** was recently constituted under the chairmanship of **Dr. Arvind Panagariya** in **December 2023**.

• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**: Introduced by the **101st Amendment Act, 2016**, **GST** is a comprehensive indirect tax that replaced multiple central and state taxes. The **GST Council**, established under **Article 279A**, is a joint forum of the **Center** and the **States** that makes recommendations on tax rates, exemptions, and thresholds.

• **Grants-in-Aid**: Apart from tax sharing, the **Center** provides grants to **States**. **Statutory Grants** are given under **Article 275** based on the **Finance Commission’s** recommendations, while **Discretionary Grants** are provided under **Article 282** for public purposes or specific schemes.

• **Borrowing Powers**: Under **Article 292**, the **Union Government** can borrow upon the security of the **Consolidated Fund of India**. Under **Article 293**, **States** can borrow within **India** upon the security of the **Consolidated Fund of the State**, but they require the **Center’s** consent if they have any outstanding central loans.

**Important Points__**

• **Sarkaria Commission (1983)**: This commission was set up to review the **Center-State relations** and recommended that the **residuary powers** of taxation should remain with the **Parliament**, while other residuary powers should be moved to the **Concurrent List**.

• **Vertical vs Horizontal Devolution**: **Vertical Devolution** refers to the transfer of resources from the **Union** to the **States**. **Horizontal Devolution** is the formula used to distribute the **States’** share among individual **States** based on factors like **population (2011 census)**, **area**, **forest cover**, **income distance**, and **demographic performance**.

• **Article 265**: It ensures that **no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law**, protecting citizens from arbitrary taxation by either the **Central** or **State** governments.

• **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**: Under **Article 148**, the **CAG** audits the accounts of both the **Union** and the **States**, ensuring financial accountability in the federal structure.

subject: GK
question: Under which of the following circumstances the Parliament of India can legislate on the matters listed in the State List?

options.text: If there is a need to regulate local government elections
If there is a need to impose state-level taxes
If there is a need to appoint new state ministers
If there is a need to implement an international treaty

solution:
The correct answer is __**If there is a need to implement an international treaty**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Article 253** of the **Constitution of India** explicitly empowers the **Parliament** to make any law for the whole or any part of the territory of **India** for implementing any **treaty**, **agreement**, or **convention** with any other country or countries, or any decision made at any international conference, association, or other body. This allows the **Union Government** to legislate on matters even if they are listed in the **State List**. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*

• The regulation of **local government elections** is a subject primarily under the jurisdiction of the **State Legislature**. According to **Entry 5** of the **State List** and **Articles 243K** and **243ZA**, the power to conduct and regulate these elections is vested in the **State Election Commission**. **Parliament** does not have the general authority to legislate on this under normal circumstances. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

• The power to impose **state-level taxes**, such as **land revenue**, **taxes on agricultural income**, or **taxes on mineral rights**, is an exclusive legislative power of the **State** as per the **Seventh Schedule**. **Parliament** cannot generally legislate on these taxes unless a **National Emergency** is in place or other specific constitutional exceptions apply. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

• The **appointment of state ministers** is an executive function governed by **Article 164** of the **Constitution**. The **Governor** appoints the **Chief Minister** and other ministers on the advice of the **Chief Minister**. This is a matter of state executive process and does not fall under the legislative domain of the **Parliament**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Seventh Schedule** (Article 246) of the **Indian Constitution** divides legislative powers into three lists: the **Union List** (List I), the **State List** (List II), and the **Concurrent List** (List III). While the **State List** is usually the exclusive domain of **States**, the **Constitution** provides specific scenarios where **Parliament** can intervene.

• **Article 249**: If the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution supported by not less than **two-thirds** of the members present and voting that it is necessary or expedient in the **national interest**, **Parliament** can make laws with respect to any matter in the **State List**. Such a law remains in force for **one year**.

• **Article 250**: During the operation of a **Proclamation of Emergency**, **Parliament** acquires the power to legislate on any matter enumerated in the **State List** for the whole or any part of **India**. These laws cease to have effect **six months** after the emergency ends.

• **Article 252**: If the **Legislatures** of **two or more states** pass resolutions requesting **Parliament** to enact a law on a state subject, **Parliament** can pass such an act. This act applies only to the requesting states and any other state that adopts it later by a resolution.

• **Article 248**: This article confers **residuary powers** of legislation upon the **Parliament**, meaning any matter not mentioned in any of the three lists falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of the **Union**.

**Important Points__**

• **Article 356**: When **President's Rule** is imposed in a state due to the failure of constitutional machinery, the **Parliament** is authorized to exercise the legislative powers of that **State Legislature**.

• The **Environment Protection Act, 1986** and the **Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972** are prominent examples of laws enacted by the **Parliament** under **Article 253** to fulfill **international obligations** arising from the **Stockholm Conference** of **1972**.

• The **Sarkaria Commission** (established in **1983**) and the **Punchhi Commission** (established in **2007**) both reviewed **Centre-State relations** and emphasized that while the **federal structure** is essential, the **Union's** power to implement **international treaties** is vital for **national integrity** and **foreign policy**.

• Under **Article 253**, the **Parliament** can even legislate on subjects like **agriculture** or **public health** (which are in the **State List**) if it is necessary to comply with **international agreements** like those of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**.
</ul

subject: GK
question: What is the total number of houses that make up the Indian Parliament?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Parliament of India** is the supreme legislative body of the **Republic of India**. It is **bicameral** in nature, meaning it consists of **two houses**: the **Rajya Sabha** and the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• According to **Article 79** of the **Constitution of India**, the Parliament for the Union consists of the **President** and the **two Houses**. While the **President** is an integral part of the Parliament, they are not a member of either house.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha**, also known as the **Council of States**, is the **Upper House** of the Parliament. It represents the **States** and **Union Territories** of India. It is a **permanent body** and is not subject to dissolution.
 
• The **Lok Sabha**, also known as the **House of the People**, is the **Lower House** of the Parliament. It represents the people of India as a whole, and its members are directly elected by the citizens through **universal adult suffrage**.
 
• The option **One** is incorrect because India does not follow a **unicameral** system at the federal level. The option **Three** is often a point of confusion because the Parliament has **three parts** (President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha), but it only has **two houses**. The option **Four** is incorrect as there are no other legislative chambers in the Indian federal structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rajya Sabha (Council of States):**

 
 
• The maximum strength of the **Rajya Sabha** is fixed at **250** members.
 
• Out of these, **238** members are elected by the **State Legislative Assemblies**, and **12** members are nominated by the **President** for their expertise in **Literature, Science, Art, and Social Service**.
 
• The **Vice-President of India** serves as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• Members are elected for a term of **six years**, with **one-third** of the members retiring every **two years**.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha (House of the People):**
 
 
• The maximum strength of the **Lok Sabha** as per the Constitution is **550** (after the **104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019**, which discontinued the nomination of **two Anglo-Indians**).
 
• The **Lok Sabha** has a normal term of **five years** from the date of its first meeting, after which it stands automatically dissolved.
 
• The **Speaker**, elected by the members of the **Lok Sabha**, is the presiding officer of the house.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process:**
 
 
• A **Bill** must be passed by both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** to become an **Act**.
 
• In case of a deadlock between the two houses on an ordinary bill, the **President** can summon a **Joint Sitting** under **Article 108**.
 
• **Money Bills**, defined under **Article 110**, can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha**, and the **Rajya Sabha** has limited powers regarding them.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **New Parliament House** was inaugurated by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **28 May 2023** as part of the **Central Vista Redevelopment Project** in **New Delhi**.
 
• The **New Parliament** building has a seating capacity of **888** members in the **Lok Sabha** and **384** members in the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The **Sengol**, a historical sceptre from **Tamil Nadu**, was installed in the new **Lok Sabha** chamber near the **Speaker’s chair**.
 
• The first session in the new building was held in **September 2023** during a **Special Session of Parliament**, where the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** (Women's Reservation Bill) was introduced.
 
• The **Parliament** usually meets for three sessions in a year: the **Budget Session** (January/February to May), the **Monsoon Session** (July to September), and the **Winter Session** (November to December).

question: Who holds the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha prior to the completion of its tenure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 85(2)(b)** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President** has the power to dissolve the **Lok Sabha** (the **Lower House** of **Parliament**) even before the completion of its **five-year** term. ***Hence, the statement regarding the President is correct.***
 
• The **President** generally exercises this power on the advice of the **Council of Ministers**, headed by the **Prime Minister**. However, if the **Council of Ministers** loses the confidence of the house (the **majority**), the **President** may use **discretionary power** to dissolve the house or explore the possibility of an **alternative government**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the head of the **government** and can recommend the dissolution to the **President**, but the **Prime Minister** himself does not hold the constitutional authority to dissolve the house. ***Hence, the statement regarding the Prime Minister is incorrect.***
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is the **Upper House** of the **Parliament of India** and is a **permanent body**. According to **Article 83(1)**, it is not subject to dissolution; instead, **one-third** of its members retire every **second year**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the Rajya Sabha is incorrect.***
 
• The **Speaker of Lok Sabha** is the presiding officer responsible for maintaining order and adjourning the house (**sine die** or for a specific period), but the **Speaker** does not possess the legal power to dissolve the **Parliamentary** body. ***Hence, the statement regarding the Speaker is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Lok Sabha:** According to **Article 81**, the maximum strength of the **Lok Sabha** is fixed at **550** members (following the **104th Amendment Act, 2019**, which discontinued the nomination of **two Anglo-Indians**). Currently, it consists of members elected directly by the people of **India** on the basis of **universal adult suffrage**.
 
• **Tenure and Article 83:** The normal term of the **Lok Sabha** is **five years** from the **date** of its first meeting. However, during a **Proclamation of Emergency**, this term can be extended by **Parliament** by law for a period not exceeding **one year** at a time.
 
• **Summoning and Prorogation:** **Article 85** also empowers the **President** to **summon** each **House of Parliament** to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, ensuring that **six months** shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.
 
• **The Role of the Election Commission:** Once the **President** dissolves the **Lok Sabha**, the **Election Commission of India** is responsible for conducting **General Elections** to constitute a new house, typically within **six months** of dissolution.
 
• **Discretionary Powers:** In a **Hung Parliament** (where no single party or coalition has a **numerical majority**), the **President** plays a crucial role in deciding whether to dissolve the house or appoint a **Prime Minister** who can prove a majority on the **floor of the house**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Qualifications for Membership:** To become a member of the **Lok Sabha**, a person must be a citizen of **India** and at least **25 years** of age. For the **Rajya Sabha**, the minimum **age** requirement is **30 years**.
 
• **The 42nd Amendment Act (1976):** This **Act** briefly increased the tenure of the **Lok Sabha** from **five** to **six years**, but the **44th Amendment Act (1978)** restored it back to **five years**.
 
• **Difference between Adjournment and Dissolution:** **Adjournment** terminates a sitting of the **House**, which is done by the **Speaker**. **Dissolution** terminates the very life of the existing **House**, and a new **House** is constituted after **general elections**.
</ul

question: What is the tenure of a Governor in an Indian state?

**__Key Points__**
__

• The tenure of the **Governor** of an **Indian state** is governed by **Article 156** of the **Constitution of India**. According to this article, the **Governor** shall hold office for a term of **5 years** from the date on which they enter their office. *Hence, the statement regarding the 5-year term is correct.*

• The **Governor** holds office during the **pleasure of the President**. This means that the **President of India** has the authority to remove a **Governor** at any time before the completion of the **5-year** term without assigning any specific reason.

• A **Governor** may, by writing under their hand addressed to the **President**, resign from their office at any point during their tenure.

• Notwithstanding the expiration of the **5-year** term, the **Governor** shall continue to hold office until their successor enters upon their office to ensure there is no constitutional vacuum in the state administration.

• The option of **3 years** is incorrect as there is no such provision in the **Constitution** for the **Governor**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

• The option of **6 years** is incorrect because this duration typically applies to members of the **Rajya Sabha** and the **State Legislative Council**, or the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**, but not to the **Governor**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

• The option **Until retirement** is incorrect because the **Constitution** does not prescribe a retirement age for the **Governor**, unlike judges of the **Supreme Court** (**65 years**) or **High Court** (**62 years**). *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Constitutional Position**: **Article 153** mandates that there shall be a **Governor** for each state. However, the **7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956** made it possible to appoint the same person as **Governor** for **two or more states**.

• **Appointment**: The **Governor** is not elected but is appointed by the **President** by warrant under his hand and seal as per **Article 155**. This ensures the **Union Government** maintains a degree of control over state administration.

• **Qualifications**: To be eligible for the post of **Governor** under **Article 157**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and must have completed the age of **35 years**. Additionally, they should not hold any **office of profit** and should not be a member of either **House of Parliament** or a **State Legislature**.

• **Executive Powers**: The **Governor** is the **Constitutional Head** of the state. All executive actions of the **State Government** are formally taken in their name. They appoint the **Chief Minister** and, on the **Chief Minister’s** advice, other ministers.

• **Legislative Powers**: The **Governor** has the power to summon or prorogue the **State Legislature** and dissolve the **State Legislative Assembly**. They also address the first session of the **State Legislature** after each **general election** and at the commencement of the first session of each **year**.

**Important Points__**

• **Judicial Immunity**: Under **Article 361**, the **Governor** enjoys personal immunity from legal liability for their official acts. During their term of office, no criminal proceedings can be instituted against them, and they cannot be arrested or imprisoned.

• **Sarkaria Commission (1983)**: This commission recommended that the **Governor’s** **5-year** term should not be disturbed except for extremely compelling reasons. It suggested that the **Governor** should be an eminent person from outside the state and not intimately connected with local politics.

• **Punchhi Commission (2007)**: This commission on **Centre-State Relations** suggested that the phrase **during the pleasure of the President** should be deleted from the **Constitution** because it leads to the arbitrary removal of **Governors**. It recommended a fixed tenure of **5 years** with a provision for **impeachment** by the **State Legislature**.

• **Discretionary Powers**: Unlike the **President**, the **Governor** has certain **discretionary powers**, such as recommending the imposition of **President’s Rule** (**Article 356**) in the state or reserving certain bills for the consideration of the **President** (**Article 200**).

• **Oath of Office**: The oath of office to the **Governor** is administered by the **Chief Justice** of the concerned **State High Court** or, in their absence, the senior-most judge of that court.

57:T

question: Which article of the Constitution provides for the State Legislative Assemblies?
solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Article 168**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 168** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the **constitution of Legislatures in States**. It mandates that for every state, there shall be a legislature consisting of the **Governor** and one or two houses. ***Hence, Article 168 is the correct answer.***
 
• It clarifies that in states where there are two houses, they are known as the **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)** and the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)**. In states with only one house, it is the **Legislative Assembly**.
 
• **Article 170** specifically details the **composition of the Legislative Assemblies**. It stipulates that the Assembly should consist of members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies, with a maximum limit of **500** members and a minimum of **60** members. ***Hence, Article 170 is incorrect as it deals with composition rather than the provision for the house.***
 
• **Article 172** provides for the **duration of State Legislatures**. It states that every Legislative Assembly, unless sooner dissolved, shall continue for **five years** from the date appointed for its first meeting. ***Hence, Article 172 is incorrect.***
 
• **Article 174** deals with the **sessions of the State Legislature**, including **prorogation** and **dissolution**. It grants the **Governor** the power to summon the House and dissolve the Legislative Assembly. ***Hence, Article 174 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the State Legislature**: 
 
 
• The State Legislature is governed by **Part VI** of the Constitution, spanning from **Article 168 to 212**.
 
• Most Indian states have a **unicameral** system, meaning they only have a **Legislative Assembly**. 
 
• A **bicameral** system exists in only a few states where both a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Legislative Council** are present to ensure broader representation.
 
 
 
• **Membership Qualifications (Article 173)**:
 
 
• To be a member of the **Legislative Assembly**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and at least **25 years** of age.
 
• For the **Legislative Council**, the minimum age requirement is **30 years**.
 
 
 
• **The Legislative Council (Article 169)**:
 
 
• **Article 169** gives **Parliament** the power to **create or abolish** a Legislative Council in a state if the Legislative Assembly of that state passes a resolution by a **special majority**.
 
• Currently, only **six states** have a bicameral legislature: **Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direct vs. Indirect Election**: Members of the **Legislative Assembly (MLAs)** are **directly elected** by the people on the basis of **adult suffrage**. In contrast, members of the **Legislative Council (MLCs)** are **indirectly elected** through a complex process involving local bodies, graduates, teachers, and nomination by the **Governor**.
 
• **Special Provisions for Small States**: While **Article 170** sets a minimum of **60** members for an Assembly, exceptions have been made for smaller states like **Sikkim (32)**, **Goa (40)**, and **Mizoram (40)** through various constitutional amendments to ensure administrative feasibility.
 
• **Officer of the House**: The **Legislative Assembly** is presided over by a **Speaker** and a **Deputy Speaker**, who are elected by the members of the Assembly from among themselves.
 
• **Role of the Governor**: The **Governor** is an integral part of the State Legislature (under **Article 168**) even though he is not a member of either House. No bill can become law without the **Governor's assent**.

question: Which of the following statements about the All India Services (AIS) is correct?

options.text: All India Services officers can be transferred between states without the consent of the state governments.
The officers are recruited and controlled by the State Governments only.
The officers serve the Union Government exclusively.
The ultimate control lies with the Union Government.

solution:
The correct answer is __**All India Services officers can be transferred between states without the consent of the state governments.**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Article 312** of the **Constitution of India** empowers the **Parliament** to create **All India Services (AIS)** that are common to both the **Union** and the **States**.

• According to **Rule 6(1)** of the **IAS (Cadre) Rules, 1954**, while an officer is typically deputed with the concurrence of the **State Government**, the **Central Government** holds the overriding power. In any case of **disagreement** between the **Centre** and the **State**, the decision of the **Central Government** shall prevail, and the **State Government** must give effect to that decision. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• The officers of the **All India Services** are **recruited** and **appointed** by the **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** and the **President of India**, respectively. They are not recruited or controlled exclusively by **State Governments**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• These officers serve both the **Union Government** and the **State Governments** on a **rotational basis** through a system of **deputation**. They do not serve the **Union** exclusively. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• While the **Ultimate Control** regarding **disciplinary actions** and **removal** from service lies with the **Union Government**, the **Immediate Control** (such as **postings** and **transfers** within the state) lies with the **State Government**. ***Hence, statement 4 is partially correct but statement 1 is the most specific legal provision regarding inter-state transfers.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, known as the **Iron Man of India**, is considered the **'Father of All India Services'** for his vision of a unified administrative structure to maintain the **integrity** of the **country**.

• The **Indian Forest Service (IFoS)** was established in the **year 1966** as the third **All India Service**, joining the **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** and the **Indian Police Service (IPS)**.

• **Article 311** of the **Constitution** provides **protection** to civil servants against **arbitrary dismissal** or **reduction in rank**, ensuring they cannot be removed by an authority subordinate to their **appointing authority**.

• The **Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA)**, located in **Mussoorie**, **Uttarakhand**, serves as the **training** ground for **IAS** officers, while **IPS** officers are trained at the **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (SVPNPA)** in **Hyderabad**.

• The **All India Services Act, 1951** provides the legal framework for the **Government of India** to regulate the **recruitment** and **service conditions** of these officers.

**Important Points__**

• The **Cadre Allocation Policy** is designed to ensure that a **number** of officers in each **state cadre** come from outside that **state**, which helps in promoting **national integration** and preventing **parochialism**.

• The **Central Deputation Reserve (CDR)** is a specific **quota** that determines the **number** of officers from a **state cadre** who can be sent to serve in the **Union Government** at any given **time**.

• The **Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT)** under the **Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions** acts as the **cadre controlling authority** for the **IAS**.

• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** is the **cadre controlling authority** for the **IPS**, while the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** controls the **IFoS**.
</ul

question: To which state of India did Fathima Beevi, the first woman Supreme Court Judge of India, belong?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **First woman Supreme Court Judge of India**,** Fathima Beevi**, was from **Kerala**.
 
• **M. Fathima Beevi**, an Indian judge and justice of the Supreme Court of India, lived from** 30 April 1927** to **23 November 2023**.
 
 
• She was **born **at **Pathanamthitta** in the **Kingdom of Travancore**, now in the Indian state of **Kerala**.​​
 
• She was the first Muslim woman to be appointed to any of the country's higher judiciaries and the** first female judge to join the Supreme Court of India** when she was nominated to the highest court in **1989**.
 
• Following her departure from the judiciary, she held positions as a **commissioner **on the **National Human Rights Commission** and, from 1997 to 2001, as g**overnor of Tamil Nadu**, a state in India.
 
• The second-highest honor bestowed by the Keralan government, the Kerala Prabha Award, was granted to her in 2023.
 
• She, posthumously, received the **Padma Bhushan Award **in the **2024**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court ​of India**:

 
 
• The** Supreme Court of Judicature **in **Calcutta **was formed as a **Court of Record**, complete with full jurisdiction and authority, with the enactment of the **Regulating Act of 1773**.
 
• **King George III **founded the **Supreme Courts** at **Madras **and **Bombay **in **1800 **and **1823**, respectively.
 
• Prior to the** Federal Court of India'**s establishment under the **Government of India Act 1935**, these High Courts held the unique distinction of being the highest courts in all cases.
 
• The **Indian Constitution** was ratified on **January 26, 1950**, following India's independence in 1947.
 
 
• **Articles 124 to 147** in **Part V **of the Constitution deal with the **organisation**, **independence**, **jurisdiction**, **powers and procedures** of the **Supreme Court**.
 
 
 
• Additionally, the **Supreme Court of India **was **established**, holding its inaugural session on **January 28, 1950**.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Judges of Supreme Court**:
 
 
• The **President appoints **the justices of the Supreme Court.
 
• The President appoints the CJI following consultation with the Supreme Court and any other judges he thinks appropriate.
 
• The CJI and any additional Supreme Court and high court judges the President determines are required for consultation before appointing the remaining justices.
 
• When a judge other than the Chief Justice is to be appointed, a conference with the Chief Justice is required.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications Required for the Appointment of Judges**:
 
 
• A person to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court should have the following qualifications:
 
 
• He should be a **citizen of India**.
 
• He should have **been a judge of a High Court **(or high courts in succession) **for 5 years**; or
 
• He should have been **an advocate of a High Court** (or High Courts in succession) **for 10 years**; or
 
• He should be a **distinguished jurist in the opinion of the president**.
 
 
 
• The **Constitution **has **not prescribed a minimum age f**or appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court.

 __
 
• Article 110 of the Constitution deals with the definition of money bills.
 
• When a money bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for recommendation and presented to the president for assent, the Speaker endorses it as a **Money bill.**
 
• A money bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and that too on the recommendation of the president.

• **After a money bill is passed by the Lok Sabha, it is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for its consideration**.
 
• The Rajya Sabha has restricted powers about a money bill, It cannot reject or amend a money bill. It can only make recommendations.
 
• It must return the bill to the Lok Sabha within **14 days**, whether with or without recommendations.
 
• The Lok Sabha can either **accept or reject all** or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• When a money bill is presented to the president, he may either give his assent to the bill or withhold his assent to the bill but cannot return the bill for reconsideration by the Houses.

• Parliament conducts three sessions in a year namely the **Budget session, Monsoon session, and winter session.**

• Out of **250 seats** of the Rajya Sabha, **12 members are nominated by the President.**
 
• **238** are** representatives of the States** and of the two Union Territories.
 
• **Rajya Sabha **is the** Upper House of the Indian Parliament.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 81** of the Indian Constitution defines the makeup of the House of the People, Lok Sabha.

 
 
• The House of Representatives shall have no more than 550 members elected, with little than 20 from Territories.
 
 
 
• **Article 83** Duration of Houses of Parliament.
 
 
• The Council of States shall not be subject to dissolution,
 
• but as nearly as possible one-third of the members thereof shall retire as soon as may be on the expiration of every second year following the provisions made in that behalf by Parliament by law.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India makes provision regarding the ‘annual financial statement’ of the country?

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**

__
 
• Article 112 of the Constitution requires the government to present to **Parliament a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure in respect of every financial year, from April 1 to March 31.**

 
 
• This statement is called the** annual financial statement.**
 
 
 
• It is divided into three parts, **Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account. For each of these funds, the government has to present a statement of receipts and expenditure.**
 
• The Government offers it on the primary day of February in order that it can be materialized earlier than the start of the brand **new economic 12 months in April**.
 
• The price range, that is supplied by the Finance Bill and the Appropriation invoice needs to be exceeded with the aid of using Lok Sabha earlier than it could come into impact on 1 April, the beginning of** India's economic 12 months.**
 
• S**ince 1947**, there had been an overall of seventy-three annual budgets, **14 meantime budgets, and 4 unique budgets, or mini-budgets. **

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• It turned into **Mr. Arun Jaitley, the Minister of Finance **withinside the** BJP led NDA Government **beneath neath the **Prime Ministership of Mr. Narendra Modi**, who modified the date of the Annual Budget of 2017 to the primary operating day of February.
 
• Additionally, the Railway Budget turned into additionally merged with the **General Budget after 92 years in 2017.**

question: Who among the following is the only President of India to have completed two terms in office till date?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**"Rajendra Prasad"**__.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**

__
 
• Freedom fighter and Congress leader **Dr. Rajendra Prasad**, who served as the President of India for 12 years from** 1950 to 1962**, remains the country's longest-serving President.
 
• He was the** first President of India** and remains the only President to date to complete **two terms in office.**
 
• He passed away on **February 28, 1963,** at the a**ge of 78.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajendra Prasad,** (born **December 3, 1884, Zeradei, India—died February 28, 1963, Patna**), Indian politician, lawyer, and journalist who was** the first president **of the Republic of India (1950–62).
 
• He also was a **comrade of Mahatma Gandhi** early in the noncooperation movement for independence and was president of the Indian National Congress (1934, 1939, and 1947).
 
• In September 1946 Prasad was **sworn in as minister for food and agriculture **in the interim government preceding full independence.
 
• From 1946 to 1949 he presided over the Indian Constituent Assembly and helped to shape the constitution.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **President of India** is the pinnacle of the country of India and the Supreme Commander of the** Indian Armed Forces.**
 
• The president is called the **primary citizen of India.**
 
• Although vested with those powers through the Constitution of India, the placement is essentially a ceremonial one and government powers are de facto exercised through the high minister.
 
• The president is **elected** through the** Electoral College** composed of elected participants of the parliament houses, the** Lok Sabha **and the** Rajya Sabha**, and additionally participants of the Vidhan Sabha, the country legislative assemblies.
 
• Presidents can also additionally continue to be in the workplace for a t**enure of 5 years**, as said through article 56, element V, of the** Constitution of India.**

question: The Composition of the Council of States comes under the purview of which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**80.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rajya Sabha or Council of States is the upper house of the Parliament of India.**
 
• Composition/Strength of Rajya Sabha:
 
 
• Article 80 of the Constitution lays down the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha as 250.
 
• Out of 250 seats of Rajya Sabha, 12 members are nominated by the President and 238 are representatives of the States and of the two Union Territories. 
 
• The present strength of Rajya Sabha is 245, out of which 233 are representatives of the States and Union territories of Delhi and Puducherry and 12 are nominated by the President.
 
• The members nominated by the President are persons having special knowledge or practical experience in respect of such matters as literature, science, art and social service. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Rajya Sabha (Council of States):

 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the creation of a ‘Council of State’ as a second chamber of the then legislature.
 
• Rajya Sabha is the Upper house of the bicameral Parliament of India.
 
• Allocation of Seats:
 
 
• The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution provides for the allocation of seats to the States and Union Territories in Rajya Sabha. 
 
• The allocation of seats is made on the basis of the population of each State.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lok Sabha:

 
 
• Lok Sabha is composed of representatives of the people chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• Article 81 of the Constitution defines the composition of the House of the People or Lok Sabha.
 
• The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is 552.
 
• Out of 552 seats of Lok Sabha:
 
 
• Up to 530 members represent the States
 
• Up to 20 members represent the Union Territories
 
• Not more than two members of the Anglo-Indian Community to be nominated by the president if this community is not adequately represented in the House. 
 
 
 
• The house currently has 543 seats, which are filled by the election of up to 543 elected members.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R).**Assertion (A):** The Union Cabinet approved a MoU allowing India to withdraw 1.82 cusecs of water from the Feni River for Sabroom town in Tripura.**Reason (R):** Sabroom town already receives sufficient groundwater supply with low iron content.
Mark the correct option:

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Assertion (A)** is correct because the **Union Cabinet**, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, gave ex-post facto approval in **October 2019** to a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between **India** and **Bangladesh**. This agreement allows India to withdraw **1.82 cusecs** of water from the **Feni River**.

• The water is specifically intended for a **drinking water supply scheme** for **Sabroom town** located in the **South Tripura** district.

• **Reason (R)** is incorrect because **Sabroom town** actually suffers from a severe **shortage of drinking water**. The available groundwater in the region is not only insufficient but also characterized by **high iron content**, making it unsuitable for direct consumption without extensive treatment.

• The core logic behind the MoU was to address the **water crisis** in the border town, as the existing groundwater resources were inadequate to meet the needs of the population.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Feni River** originates in the **South Tripura** district, passes through **Sabroom town**, and flows into **Bangladesh** before emptying into the **Bay of Bengal**.

• The **Maitri Setu** (Friendship Bridge), which spans 1.9 kilometers over the Feni River, was inaugurated in **March 2021** to connect **Sabroom** in India with **Ramgarh** in Bangladesh, enhancing trade and connectivity.

• The water sharing of the Feni River had been a long-standing issue between the two countries since **1958**, and the 2019 MoU marked a significant step in bilateral cooperation.

• **Sabroom** is strategically important as it is being developed as a **Logistics Hub** and provides the shortest land route to the **Chittagong Port** in Bangladesh.
