__
 
• **Three-pointer:** In basketball, a shot made from beyond the three-point arc is termed as a **three-pointer.** It awards the team three points instead of the usual two for field goals. This is a defining feature of modern basketball.
 
• The **three-point arc** is a marked area on the court, and its distance varies depending on the league. For example, in the **NBA**, the arc is located at **23 feet 9 inches** from the basket at the top of the key.
 
• Players often practice extensively to develop their ability to make three-point shots, as it requires **precision, strength, and technique.** It is considered a high-risk, high-reward shot. *Hence, the correct answer is Three-pointer.*
 
• **History:** The three-point shot was introduced to professional basketball in the **1960s** and became prominent in the **NBA** during the **1979-1980 season.** It revolutionized the way the game is played, encouraging teams to space the floor and rely on outside shooting.
 
• The shot has evolved into a critical component of strategy, with teams and players relying heavily on three-point shooting to maximize scoring opportunities. *Hence, the correct answer is Three-pointer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Types of Shots in Basketball:**

 
 
• **Slam Dunk:** A high-energy shot where the player jumps and forcefully places the ball directly into the basket. It is usually performed close to the hoop and is a crowd-pleaser due to its dramatic style.
 
• **Free Throw:** A shot awarded after a foul, taken from the free-throw line, which is **15 feet** away from the basket. It is worth one point.
 
• **Layup:** A close-range shot performed by laying the ball up near the basket, often using the backboard for guidance. Layups are typically worth two points.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Three-Point Shooting:**
 
 
• The three-point shot adds strategic depth to basketball, encouraging teams to adopt a more spaced-out offensive approach.
 
• **Example:** Legendary players like **Stephen Curry** and **Ray Allen** are known for their exceptional three-point shooting, revolutionizing the game.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the Three-Point Arc:**
 
 
• The arc’s distance varies between leagues. For instance, the **WNBA** and **FIBA** use a shorter distance than the NBA. The standardized distance helps adapt the game for different levels of play.
 
• The three-point arc’s introduction has shifted basketball toward a focus on skillful shooting and away from physical dominance near the basket.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Facts:**

 
 
• **The NBA three-point arc:** The arc is **23 feet 9 inches** at the top of the key and **22 feet** at the corners.
 
• **High Scoring Potential:** Teams with strong three-point shooters often have higher-scoring games due to the additional point per shot.
 
 
 
• **Notable Moments:**
 
 
• **Stephen Curry:** Curry holds the record for most three-pointers in an NBA season, showcasing the importance of this shot in modern basketball.
 
• **Ray Allen:** Known for his clutch three-point shots, Allen holds the record for the most career three-pointers in NBA history.

question: The Indian Olympic Association was formed in which year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1927**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** was established in the year **1927**. It is the apex body responsible for the **Olympic Movement** and the **Commonwealth Games** in **India**.

• The organization was founded by **Sir Dorabji Tata** and **Dr. A.G. Noehren**. **Sir Dorabji Tata** served as the **first President**, while **Dr. A.G. Noehren** was the **first Secretary General**.

• In **1927**, the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** officially recognized the **Indian Olympic Association** as the **National Olympic Committee** for **India**.

• The formation of the **IOA** was a pivotal moment in formalizing **India's** participation in international multi-sport events, ensuring a structured approach to athlete selection and training.

• Regarding the other options: **1920** is the year **India** sent its first organized team to the **Antwerp Olympics**, but the **IOA** was not yet formed. **1930** marks the year of the first **British Empire Games** (now **Commonwealth Games**). **1947** is the year of **Indian Independence**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **First Participation:** **India** first participated in the **Olympic Games** in **1900** at the **Paris Olympics**. The country was represented by a lone athlete, **Norman Pritchard**, who won **two silver medals** in athletics (**200m** and **200m hurdles**).

• **Headquarters:** The headquarters of the **Indian Olympic Association** is located in **New Delhi**. It operates as a **Non-Profit Organization** registered under the **Societies Registration Act of 1860**.

• **Leadership:** In **December 2022**, the legendary sprinter **P.T. Usha** was elected as the **first woman President** of the **Indian Olympic Association**. She is also the first Olympian to lead the body.

• **Functions:** The **IOA** is responsible for managing the **Indian** contingents for the **Summer Olympics**, **Winter Olympics**, **Asian Games**, and **Commonwealth Games**. It also coordinates with various **National Sports Federations (NSFs)**.

• **Affiliations:** The **IOA** is a member of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**, the **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)**, and the **Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF)**.

**Important Points__**

• **Early Efforts:** Before the formal establishment in **1927**, **Sir Dorabji Tata** personally financed the **Indian** team for the **1920 Antwerp Olympics**. A provisional **All-India Olympic Committee** was set up in **1923** to handle the **1924 Paris Olympics**.

• **Legal Status:** The **IOA** is governed by the **Olympic Charter** and its own constitution. It works closely with the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, **Government of India**, although it maintains its autonomy as a **National Olympic Committee**.

• **Role in Sports Development:** Beyond event management, the **IOA** plays a crucial role in promoting the **Olympic values** of **friendship**, **solidarity**, and **fair play** across the **country**.
</ul

question: The first ever South Asian Games held in India took place in which year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1987**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **South Asian Games**, originally known as the **South Asian Federation Games (SAF Games)**, is a biennial multi-sport event held among athletes from the **South Asian** region.

• The **first ever South Asian Games** to be hosted in **India** took place in **1987**. This was the **3rd edition** of the games. ***Hence, the correct answer is 1987.***

• The **1987 South Asian Federation Games** were held in **Calcutta** (now **Kolkata**), West Bengal. This event marked the first time the country hosted this specific regional competition.

• The inaugural edition of the South Asian Games was held in **Kathmandu, Nepal**, in **1984**, and the second edition was held in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**, in **1985**.

• Option **1982** is incorrect because, in that year, **India** hosted the **9th Asian Games** in **New Delhi**, which is a different multi-sport event involving all of **Asia**.

• Options **1991** and **1995** are incorrect as the first instance of hosting occurred earlier in **1987**, although **India** did host the games again in **1995** in **Madras** (now **Chennai**).

**Additional Information__**
__

• The governing body for the games is the **South Asian Sports Council (SASC)**, which was formed in **1983** to promote sports and brotherhood among **South Asian** nations.

• There are currently **eight participating nations** in the South Asian Games: **Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka**.

• **India** has hosted the South Asian Games on **three occasions**: the **3rd edition** in **1987** (**Calcutta**), the **7th edition** in **1995** (**Madras**), and the **12th edition** in **2016** (**Guwahati** and **Shillong**).

• In the **1987 Games** held in **India**, athletes competed in **10 different sports**, including **Athletics, Basketball, Boxing, Football, Kabaddi, Swimming, Table Tennis, Volleyball, Weightlifting, and Wrestling**.

• **India** has maintained a dominant record in the competition, finishing at the **top of the medal tally** in every single edition of the South Asian Games since **1984**.

**Important Points__**

• The **13th South Asian Games** were held in **2019** in **Kathmandu and Pokhara, Nepal**. In this edition, **India** won a record-breaking **312 medals**, consisting of **174 Gold, 93 Silver, and 45 Bronze**.

• The official motto of the **South Asian Sports Council** is **Peace, Prosperity, and Progress**, reflecting the goal of regional integration through sports.

• **Afghanistan** is the newest member of the council, having joined in **2004** and making its debut in the **2006 South Asian Games** held in **Colombo, Sri Lanka**.

• The games are often referred to as the **South Asian Olympics** because they follow a similar format and provide a platform for regional athletes to prepare for larger international stages like the **Asian Games** and the **Olympic Games**.

The correct answer is __**Weightlifting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Weightlifting:

__
 
• Weightlifting is a sport in which athletes compete in lifting a barbell loaded with weight plates from the ground to overhead.
 
• Athletes compete in two specific ways of lifting the barbell overhead.
 
• These are:
 
 
• the snatch
 
• the clean and jerk.
 
 

Explanation:__

__
 
• The snatch is a wide-grip lift, in which the weighted barbell is lifted overhead in one motion.
 
• The clean and jerk is a combination lift, in which the weight is first taken from the ground to the front of the shoulders (the clean), and then from the shoulders to overhead (the jerk).
 
• The clean and press, wherein a clean was followed by an overhead press, was formerly also a competition lift but was discontinued due to difficulties in judging proper form.
 
• To keep competing the player has to increase at least 5 kg of weight between two attempts if the first one is successful.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Few rules(officiating):

 
• During the competition, the snatch event takes place first, followed by a short intermission, and then the clean and jerk event.
 
• There are two side judges and one head referee who together provide a "successful" or "failed" result for each attempt based on their observation of the lift within the governing body's rules and regulations.
 
• Two successes are required for any attempt to pass.
 
• Usually, the judges' and referee's results are registered via a lighting system with a white light indicating a "successful" lift and a red light indicating a "failed" lift.

question: Which city hosted the first Asian Games in 1951?
solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **First Asian Games**, officially known as the **First Asiad**, were held in **New Delhi**, **India**, in **1951**. This multi-sport event took place from **March 4** to **March 11, 1951**, making **New Delhi** the inaugural host city.

• The games were officially opened by the first **President of India**, **Dr. Rajendra Prasad**, at the **Irwin Stadium**, which was later renamed the **Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium**.

• A total of **11 National Olympic Committees (NOCs)** participated in the first edition, including **Afghanistan**, **Burma**, **Ceylon**, **India**, **Indonesia**, **Iran**, **Japan**, **Nepal**, **Philippines**, **Singapore**, and **Thailand**.

• **Japan** topped the medal table with a total of **60 medals** (including **24 gold**), while the host nation, **India**, finished in **second place** with **51 medals** (including **15 gold**).

• The other options provided are incorrect for the first edition: **Tokyo** hosted the **3rd Asian Games** in **1958**, **Jakarta** hosted the **4th edition** in **1962**, and **Bangkok** hosted its first games in **1966**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Guru Dutt Sondhi**: He is recognized as the **father of the Asian Games**. As an Indian sports administrator and member of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**, he proposed the concept of the **Asian Games** to foster friendship and solidarity among Asian nations after **World War II**.

• **Governing Body**: The first games were organized by the **Asian Games Federation (AGF)**. However, since **1982**, the games have been regulated by the **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)**, which is recognized by the **International Olympic Committee**.

• **Frequency and Scale**: The **Asian Games** are held every **four years** and are considered the **second-largest multi-sport event** in the world, following the **Olympic Games**.

• **India as Host**: **India** has hosted the **Asian Games** twice. After the inaugural **1951** edition, **New Delhi** again hosted the **9th Asian Games** in **1982**, which saw the introduction of the first official mascot, **Appu**, an elephant.

• **Bangkok's Hosting Record**: **Bangkok**, **Thailand**, holds the record for hosting the **Asian Games** the most number of times, having served as the host city in **1966**, **1970**, **1978**, and **1998**.

**Important Points__**

• **Sports and Disciplines**: The **1951 Asian Games** featured **6 sports**: **Athletics**, **Aquatics** (Swimming, Diving, and Water Polo), **Basketball**, **Cycling** (Road and Track), **Football**, and **Weightlifting**. A total of **489 athletes** competed in **57 events**.

• **Official Motto**: The motto for the first games was **'Play the Game, in the Spirit of the Game'**, a phrase coined by the first **Prime Minister of India**, **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru**. The official permanent motto of the **OCA** is **'Ever Onward'**.

• **Torch Relay**: The tradition of the **torch relay** for the **Asian Games** began at the **Red Fort** in **New Delhi** during the **1951** edition, where the flame was lit by the sun's rays using a parabolic mirror.

• **Notable Achievements**: Indian sprinter **Lavy Pinto** became the first **Indian** to win a **gold medal** in the **Asian Games**, securing victories in both the **100-meter** and **200-meter** sprints in **1951**.

• **Recent and Future Editions**: The **19th Asian Games** were held in **Hangzhou**, **China**, in **2023** (postponed from **2022**). The **20th edition** is scheduled to be held in **Aichi-Nagoya**, **Japan**, in **2026**.
</ul

__
 
• The **Asian Games**, also widely known as **Asiad**, is a continental multi-sport event held every **4 years** among athletes from all over **Asia**.
 
• The event is organized and regulated by the **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)**, under the supervision of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**.
 
• The primary **function** of these games is to foster **international friendship**, **unity**, and **cultural exchange** among **Asian nations** through the medium of sports.
 
• The **Asian Games** follow a cycle similar to the **Olympic Games**, usually taking place in the **even-numbered years** between the **Summer Olympics**.
 
• The **first edition** of the **Asian Games** was hosted in **New Delhi**, **India**, in the year **1951**, featuring **11 nations** competing in **6 sports**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Governing Body Evolution**: Initially, the games were managed by the **Asian Games Federation (AGF)** from **1951** to **1978**. Since the **1982 games**, the **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)** has been the governing body.
 
• **Recent and Future Locations**:
 
 
• The **18th edition** was held in **Jakarta-Palembang**, **Indonesia**, in **2018**.
 
• The **19th Asian Games** took place in **Hangzhou**, **China**, in **2023** (postponed from **2022** due to the **COVID-19 pandemic**).
 
• The **20th edition** is scheduled to be held in **Aichi-Nagoya**, **Japan**, in the year **2026**.
 
 
 
• **Sports Categories**: The games include **Olympic sports** such as **Athletics**, **Swimming**, and **Archery**, as well as **non-Olympic sports** that are popular in **Asia**, such as **Kabaddi**, **Sepak Takraw**, and **Squash**.
 
• **Participating Nations**: Currently, **45 National Olympic Committees (NOCs)** that are members of the **OCA** are eligible to participate in the games.
 
• **The Symbol**: The official **symbol** of the **Asian Games** is a **red sun** with **16 rays** and a **white circle** in the center, representing the "**Ever Onward**" spirit of the continent.

question: In which year were the first Asian Games held?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The first edition of the **Asian Games**, also known as the **Asiad**, was held in the year **1951**. The event was hosted in **New Delhi**, **India**, making it the first major multi-sport event in **Asia** after **World War II**.

• The games were officially opened on **March 4, 1951**, by the then **President of India**, **Dr. Rajendra Prasad**, at the **Irwin Stadium**, which was later renamed the **Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium**.

• A total of **11 nations** participated in this inaugural event, including **Afghanistan, Burma, Ceylon, India, Indonesia, Iran, Japan, Nepal, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand**.

• The **1951 Asian Games** featured **57 events** in **six sports**: **Athletics, Aquatics (Swimming, Diving, and Water Polo), Basketball, Cycling (Road and Track), Football, and Weightlifting**.

• **Japan** topped the medal tally with a total of **60 medals** (24 Gold, 21 Silver, and 15 Bronze), while the host nation, **India**, finished second with **51 medals** (15 Gold, 16 Silver, and 20 Bronze).

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Visionary Leadership:** The idea for the **Asian Games** was proposed by **Guru Dutt Sondhi**, a member of the **International Olympic Committee**, who sought to promote **Asian** unity and sportsmanship. The **Asian Games Federation (AGF)** was formed in **1949** to manage the event.

• **Motto and Symbolism:** The official motto of the games, **'Ever Onward'**, was given by **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first **Prime Minister of India**. The logo featured a **red sun** with **16 rays** and a **white circle** in the center, symbolizing the rising spirit of **Asia**.

• **Frequency and Governance:** The **Asian Games** are held every **four years**. Since **1982**, the **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)** has been the governing body, taking over from the **Asian Games Federation**.

• **India as a Host:** **India** has hosted the **Asian Games** twice. Following the **1951** edition, the **9th Asian Games** were held in **New Delhi** in **1982**, which saw the introduction of the famous mascot **Appu**, the elephant.

• **Recent and Future Games:** The **19th Asian Games** were held in **Hangzhou, China**, in **2023** (postponed from 2022). The **20th edition** is scheduled for **2026** in **Aichi-Nagoya, Japan**.

**Important Points__**

• **Global Recognition:** The **Asian Games** are recognized by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** and are considered the **second-largest** multi-sport event in the world after the **Olympic Games**.

• **Torch Relay Tradition:** A unique tradition of the **Asian Games** is that the **torch relay** always commences at the **National Stadium in New Delhi**, honoring the site of the very first games.

• **Historical Context:** The **1948** option in the question refers to the **London Olympics**, while **1954** was the year of the **second Asian Games** held in **Manila, Philippines**. The **1960** option coincides with the **Rome Olympics**.

• **Impact on Sports:** The **1951** games played a crucial role in reviving **Japanese** sports participation on the international stage following their exclusion from the **1948 London Olympics**.
</ul

question: The first Commonwealth Games were held in which country?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Canada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The first Commonwealth Games** were held in **1930** in the city of **Hamilton, Canada.** This marked the beginning of an international sporting competition among the member nations of the British Empire.
 
• The games were initially called the **British Empire Games,** and they aimed to promote goodwill and friendly rivalry among the Commonwealth countries.
 
• A total of **11 countries** participated in the first edition of the games, featuring **400 athletes** competing in six sports and 59 events. *Hence, the correct answer is Canada.*
 
• Canada played a significant role in organizing these games, and the city of Hamilton provided financial support of **$30,000** to host the event successfully.
 
• The Commonwealth Games have evolved significantly since 1930, now involving more countries and a larger number of sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context of the Commonwealth Games:**

 
 
• The **Commonwealth Games** originated as the **British Empire Games** in 1930, reflecting the unity and cooperation among countries in the British Empire.
 
• The name was later changed to the **British Empire and Commonwealth Games** in 1954, and then to the **British Commonwealth Games** in 1970, before finally being called the Commonwealth Games in 1978.
 
 
 
• **Features of the First Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• The first edition of the games included **six sports:** athletics, swimming, rowing, boxing, wrestling, and lawn bowls.
 
• **Participants:** The games witnessed participation from 11 countries, including **Canada, Australia, England, South Africa, and New Zealand.**
 
• **Hamilton's Contribution:** The city of **Hamilton, Ontario,** funded and supported the games, showcasing its commitment to international sports.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• Over the years, the games have grown to include over **70 member countries** and territories, competing in a wide range of sports.
 
• The Commonwealth Games is unique because it includes sports that are often popular in Commonwealth nations, such as **netball, rugby sevens, and lawn bowls.**
 
• The games also emphasize **equality** by featuring events for athletes with disabilities in the same program as able-bodied athletes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Developments in Commonwealth Games History:**

 
 
• **1954:** The games in Vancouver introduced the **Queen's Baton Relay,** a tradition that continues to this day, symbolizing the unity of the Commonwealth.
 
• **1998:** Kuala Lumpur games were the first to include **team sports** like cricket and hockey.
 
• **2010:** The Commonwealth Games were held in **India** for the first time, in New Delhi, featuring an extensive program of sports and cultural events.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Games:**
 
 
• The games promote **international cooperation** and bring together athletes from diverse backgrounds, fostering mutual respect and understanding.
 
• They also showcase the **cultural diversity** and sporting talents of the Commonwealth nations.

question: Where was the first Cricket World Cup held in 1975?
solution:
The correct answer is __**England**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **first-ever Cricket World Cup** was officially known as the **Prudential Cup** and was held in **England** in **June 1975**. **England** was the only nation at that time that had the resources and infrastructure to host such a massive international event.

• The tournament was organized by the **International Cricket Conference** (now known as the **International Cricket Council** or **ICC**). It featured **eight teams**: **Australia**, **England**, **India**, **New Zealand**, **Pakistan**, the **West Indies**, **Sri Lanka**, and **East Africa**.

• The matches in the **1975** edition were played in a **60-over** format per side, which is different from the current **50-over** standard. Players wore **traditional white clothing** and used **red cricket balls**.

• The **West Indies** emerged as the inaugural champions by defeating **Australia** in the final by **17 runs**. The final was held at the iconic **Lord’s Cricket Ground** in **London** on **June 21, 1975**.

• Regarding the other options: **India** did not host the World Cup until **1987**; **Australia** first co-hosted the event in **1992**; and the **West Indies** hosted their first World Cup much later in **2007**. Hence, **England** is the correct location for the **1975** event.

**Additional Information__**

__

• **West Indies Dominance**: The **West Indies** team, captained by **Clive Lloyd**, was a powerhouse in early world cricket. They won the first two editions of the World Cup in **1975** and **1979**, both held in **England**. **Clive Lloyd** scored a brilliant **102 runs** in the **1975 final** to secure the victory.

• **Host Rotation**: **England** hosted the first three World Cups (**1975**, **1979**, and **1983**). It was only in **1987** that the tournament moved out of **England** to the **Indian subcontinent** (hosted by **India** and **Pakistan**).

• **Evolution of Format**: The **1987 World Cup** saw the reduction of overs from **60** to **50** per innings to accommodate the shorter daylight hours in the **Asian subcontinent** compared to the **English summer**.

• **Historical Significance**: The **1975 World Cup** marked the global expansion of **One Day International (ODI)** cricket, which had only begun in **1971**. It paved the way for cricket to become a major commercial and televised sport worldwide.

• **East Africa Team**: A unique feature of the **1975** tournament was the participation of the **East Africa** team, which represented players from **Kenya**, **Uganda**, **Tanzania**, and **Zambia**.

**Important Points__**

• **First Match**: The opening match of the **1975 World Cup** was played between **England** and **India** at **Lord’s**. It is famously remembered for **Sunil Gavaskar** scoring an unbeaten **36 runs** off **174 balls**, a very slow innings for an **ODI**.

• **Sponsorship**: The tournament was sponsored by the **Prudential Assurance Company**, which provided a total prize fund of **£9,000**, with the winners receiving **£4,000**.

• **Venue Details**: Matches were spread across several historic venues in **England**, including **The Oval** (London), **Old Trafford** (Manchester), **Trent Bridge** (Nottingham), **Headingley** (Leeds), and **Edgbaston** (Birmingham).

• **Recent Edition**: The most recent **ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup** was held in **2023** in **India**, where **Australia** defeated **India** in the final to claim their **sixth title**.

• **Alappuzha**, often referred to as the **"Venice of the East"**, is located in the state of **Kerala**, India.
 
• The city is globally renowned for hosting the prestigious **Nehru Trophy Boat Race**, an annual event held on the **Punnamada Lake**.
 
• This championship draws thousands of spectators and participants, showcasing **traditional snake boats**, also known as **"Chundan Vallams"**, which are unique to Kerala. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*
 
• The boat race is not just a sporting event but also a cultural celebration, reflecting the **rich heritage** and traditions of Kerala.

• **Alappuzha, Kerala:**

 
 
• Known for its **backwaters**, houseboats, and scenic landscapes, Alappuzha is a popular tourist destination in Kerala.
 
• It is a hub for **traditional boat racing events**, which are deeply rooted in the **culture** and **history** of the region.
 
• **Example:** The **Nehru Trophy Boat Race** was initiated in **1952** to commemorate the visit of the first Prime Minister of India, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, to Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Snake Boats:**

question:
Consider the following statements about Indian women at the Winter Olympics:**1) Shailaja Kumar was the first Indian woman to compete in 1988.
2) Neha Ahuja was the first to qualify by standards in 2006.
3) India has regularly sent multiple women athletes since 1988.
Which of the statements is/are correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2 are Correct**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shailaja Kumar** made history as the first **Indian woman** to compete in the **Winter Olympics**. She participated in the **1988 Winter Olympics** held in **Calgary**, **Canada**. She competed in the **Alpine Skiing** event, specifically the **Women's Slalom**, where she finished in **28th place**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Neha Ahuja** was a trailblazer for **India** at the **2006 Winter Olympics** in **Turin**, **Italy**. She was the first **Indian woman** to qualify for the **Winter Games** by meeting the rigorous qualification standards set by the **International Ski Federation (FIS)**, rather than entering through a wildcard or invitational spot. She competed in both the **Slalom** and **Giant Slalom** events. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **India** has not regularly sent multiple women athletes to the **Winter Olympics**. Since **1988**, **India's** participation has been very limited, often consisting of only a single athlete (frequently **Shiva Keshavan** in **Luge**). There have been many editions of the **Winter Games** where no **Indian women** qualified or participated at all. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Only 1 and 2 are Correct.***

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of India at Winter Olympics:**
 
 
• **India** first participated in the **Winter Olympic Games** in **1964**, which were held in **Innsbruck**, **Austria**.
 
• The first **Indian** athlete to compete was **Jeremy Bujakowski**, an **Alpine skier** of **Polish** descent who represented **India** in **1964** and **1968**.
 
• After a long hiatus, **India** returned to the **Winter Games** in **1988**, which saw the debut of **Shailaja Kumar**, **Gul Dev**, and **Kishor Rahtna Rai**.
 
 
 
• **Prominent Indian Winter Olympians:**
 
 
• **Shiva Keshavan:** He is the most decorated **Indian** winter athlete, having represented the **country** in **six consecutive Winter Olympics** from **1998** (**Nagano**) to **2018** (**Pyeongchang**) in the **Luge** event. He has won multiple medals at the **Asia Cup**.
 
• **Arif Khan:** An **Alpine skier** from **Gulmarg**, **Jammu and Kashmir**, who was the sole representative for **India** at the **2022 Winter Olympics** in **Beijing**, **China**. He was the first **Indian** to qualify for two different events (**Slalom** and **Giant Slalom**) in the same edition.
 
 
 
• **Governance and Geography:**
 
 
• The **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** is the governing body responsible for **India's** participation in the **Olympic Games**.
 
• Winter sports in **India** are primarily promoted by the **Winter Games Federation of India (WGFI)**.
 
• The primary locations for winter sports training and competitions in **India** are **Gulmarg** (**Jammu and Kashmir**), **Auli** (**Uttarakhand**), and **Manali** (**Himachal Pradesh**).
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Participation Trends:** **India's** contingents at the **Winter Olympics** are typically very small, often ranging from **1 to 4 athletes**. This is due to the lack of specialized infrastructure and the high cost of training for winter sports.
 
• **Women's Representation:** Following **Shailaja Kumar** in **1988** and **Neha Ahuja** in **2006**, other women like **Alpana Kumari** (**2006**, though she did not start) have been part of the **Indian** winter sports narrative, but consistent multi-athlete female representation remains a goal for the future.

question: How does the IMEC Alliance impact global supply chains?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Strengthens supply chain efficiency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** is a multi-modal **infrastructure project** designed to **strengthen supply chain efficiency** by creating a seamless **ship-to-rail transit network** connecting **India**, the **Arabian Gulf**, and **Europe**.

• One of the primary objectives of the **IMEC Alliance** is to reduce **transit time** for goods by approximately **40%** compared to existing maritime routes through the **Suez Canal**.

• The corridor aims to achieve a **30% reduction in transit costs**, thereby making **global trade** more **cost-effective** and accessible for participating **nations**.

• By diversifying **trade routes**, the alliance enhances **global supply chain resilience**, ensuring that **logistics** remain functional even during **geopolitical tensions** or maritime **disruptions**.

• The project is not limited to transport; it also integrates **digital connectivity** through **undersea cables** and **energy security** via **clean hydrogen pipelines**, which boosts the overall **efficiency** of resource distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Launch and Participants:** The **IMEC** was officially announced on **September 9, 2023**, during the **G20 Summit** held in **New Delhi**. The signatory **countries** and entities include **India**, the **United States**, the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, **Saudi Arabia**, **France**, **Germany**, **Italy**, and the **European Union**.

• **Corridor Structure:** The project is divided into two main segments: the **East Corridor**, which connects **Indian ports** to the **Arabian Gulf**, and the **Northern Corridor**, which connects the **Gulf** to **European ports**.

• **Infrastructure Components:** It involves the construction of a **high-speed railway line**, **electricity grids**, **high-speed data cables**, and **pipelines** for **renewable energy**, specifically **green hydrogen**.

• **Strategic Importance:** **IMEC** is often viewed as a strategic **alternative** to **China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**, emphasizing **transparency**, **sustainability**, and **sovereign equality** among **partners**.

• **Economic Impact:** The alliance is expected to stimulate **economic growth**, facilitate **cross-border trade**, and create significant **employment opportunities** across **Asia**, the **Middle East**, and **Europe**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Logistics and Transit:** The use of **railway systems** to supplement **maritime transport** helps in bypassing **congested chokepoints**, thereby increasing the **reliability** of **global logistics**.

• **Sustainability:** The **IMEC** aligns with **global climate goals** by promoting **clean energy** trade and reducing the **carbon footprint** of **international shipping** through shorter **transportation distances**.

• **Geopolitics:** This alliance fosters closer **diplomatic ties** and **economic integration** between **Israel**, **Arab nations**, **India**, and the **West**, contributing to **regional stability**.

• **Trade Volumes:** The corridor is anticipated to handle a significant **volume** of **container traffic**, which will strengthen **India’s** position as a **global manufacturing hub** and a key **exporter** to **European markets**.

question: which country hosted the first in-person Quad Leaders' Summit in 2021?
solution:
The correct answer is __**United States**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The first in-person Quad Leaders’ Summit** was held in **2021**, hosted by the **United States** in **Washington, D.C.**
 
• This summit marked the first time that the leaders of the **Quad nations (India, Japan, Australia, and the United States)** met face-to-face to discuss important global and regional issues.
 
• The Quad Summit aimed to strengthen the **strategic partnership** among the member nations and focused on **shared democratic values** and **commitment to ensuring a free, open, and inclusive Indo-Pacific region**.
 
• The **agenda** of the summit included discussions on key global challenges, such as **COVID-19 pandemic response, climate change, technology cooperation, and regional security issues**.
 
• The leaders also announced initiatives, including a focus on **vaccine distribution** in the Indo-Pacific region to combat the ongoing pandemic.
 
• The United States played a pivotal role in organizing this summit, underscoring its **leadership in global diplomacy** and its commitment to working with regional allies to address critical challenges.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is United States.***

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **What is the Quad?**

 
 
• The **Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad)** is a strategic forum consisting of four nations: **India, Japan, Australia, and the United States**. It was initially formed in **2007**.
 
• The Quad aims to promote a **free, open, inclusive, and rules-based Indo-Pacific region**. It is not a formal military alliance but a platform for strategic cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 2021 Quad Leaders' Summit:**

question: Which countries are part of the IMEC alliance?

options.text: India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Israel, European Union, USA
India, China, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Russia
India, Pakistan, UAE, Iran, European Union
India, UAE, Qatar, Turkey, European Union

solution:
The correct answer is __**India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Israel, European Union, USA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** is a planned economic corridor that aims to bolster economic development by fostering connectivity and economic integration between **Asia**, the **Arabian Gulf**, and **Europe**.
 
• The project was launched on **September 9, 2023**, on the sidelines of the **G20 Summit** held in **New Delhi**, **India**.
 
• The signatories of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) include **India**, the **United States of America**, the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, **Saudi Arabia**, the **European Union**, **France**, **Italy**, and **Germany**.
 
• While **Israel** was not an initial signatory to the MoU, it is a critical geographical and logistical partner in the alliance as the corridor is designed to pass through the **Port of Haifa** in **Israel** to connect to **Europe**. ***Hence, the option containing India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Israel, European Union, and USA is correct.***
 
• The corridor is divided into two distinct parts: the **East Corridor**, which connects **India** to the **Arabian Gulf**, and the **Northern Corridor**, which connects the **Arabian Gulf** to **Europe**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of Infrastructure:** The **IMEC** alliance focuses on multiple layers of infrastructure including a **railway network** designed to provide a reliable and cost-effective **ship-to-rail transit**; an **electricity cable** network for renewable energy; and a **high-speed data cable** for digital connectivity.
 
• **Strategic Energy Goals:** A significant application of this corridor is the transport of **green hydrogen** via pipelines from **India** and the **Middle East** to **Europe**, aligning with global climate goals and **energy security**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** Experts suggest that the corridor will increase **trade efficiency** by reducing the transit time between **India** and **Europe** by **40%** and lowering transit costs by **30%** compared to existing maritime routes like the **Suez Canal**.
 
• **Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII):** The **IMEC** is considered a landmark project under the **PGII**, which is a **G7** initiative to fund infrastructure projects in developing nations, often viewed as a strategic alternative to **China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**.
 
• **Geopolitical Context:** The project facilitates the normalization of ties in the **Middle East**, particularly between **Israel** and **Arab nations** like **Saudi Arabia** and the **UAE**, under the broader umbrella of **United States** diplomatic efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the European Union:** As a single entity, the **European Union** coordinates the participation of its member states like **France**, **Germany**, and **Italy** to ensure seamless connectivity from the **Mediterranean ports** to mainland **Europe**.
 
• **Port of Haifa:** Located in **Israel**, this port is a vital link where the rail network from the **Arabian Peninsula** meets the sea route to **Piraeus** in **Greece** or other **European** ports.
 
• **India's Role:** For **India**, the corridor enhances **strategic autonomy** and provides a direct route to **European markets**, bypassing **Pakistan** and reducing dependency on the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)** that passes through **Iran** and **Russia**.
 
• **Year of Implementation:** Following the **2023** announcement, member countries have committed to meeting regularly to develop a **technical design** and a **working timeline** for the phased construction of the rail and pipe links.
</ul

question: Which Indian company is managing the operations of Chabahar Port?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Ports Global Limited (IPGL)**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Indian Ports Global Limited (IPGL)** is the specialized entity established by the Government of India to develop and operate the **Shahid Beheshti terminal** of the **Chabahar Port** in **Iran**.

• IPGL was originally formed as a joint venture between **Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT)** and **Deendayal Port Trust** (formerly Kandla Port Trust) to facilitate India's strategic investments in overseas ports.

• In **May 2024**, a historic **10-year long-term contract** was signed between **IPGL** and the **Port and Maritime Organisation (PMO)** of Iran, ensuring continuous Indian management of the terminal.

• The primary objective of managing this port is to create a reliable trade route to **Afghanistan** and **Central Asian countries**, bypassing the land route through **Pakistan**.

• While **JNPT** is a stakeholder in the venture, the direct operational management is handled by the dedicated subsidiary, **IPGL**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Chabahar Port** is located on the **Gulf of Oman** in southeastern Iran and is the only Iranian port with direct access to the **Indian Ocean**.

• The port is a crucial link in the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**, a multi-modal transportation network connecting India, Iran, Azerbaijan, and Russia.

• Strategically, Chabahar is seen as a counter to the **Gwadar Port** in Pakistan, which is being developed by **China** as part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

• The **Shipping Corporation of India (SCI)** handles maritime logistics but does not manage the port operations, and **Adani Ports** is a private entity not currently managing the state-led Chabahar project.
</ul

• The MEC is envisioned to connect **India, the Middle East, and Europe** through a comprehensive network of **infrastructure projects**, including railways, ports, and energy pipelines.
 
• It aims to reduce the shipping time of goods between India and Europe by creating an efficient and sustainable trade route.
 
• **Example:** A railway line in the Middle East will connect to ports that ship goods to Europe, facilitating faster trade and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Significance of MEC:**
 
 
• It promotes **regional connectivity**, enhances trade, and strengthens geopolitical partnerships among participating countries.
 
• The corridor is expected to serve as a counterbalance to **China’s Belt and Road Initiative**, emphasizing **transparency, environmental sustainability**, and **economic inclusivity**.
 
• It also aligns with the broader goals of global economic integration and sustainable development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Belt and Road Initiative (BRI):**

 
 
• **China’s BRI** is a global infrastructure initiative launched in **2013** to connect Asia, Europe, and Africa. However, it has been criticized for creating **debt traps** for participating nations.
 
• In contrast, the MEC emphasizes **collaborative partnerships**, transparency, and economic sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Involvement of Key Players:**
 
 
• **India:** A central player in the MEC, contributing to the development of trade routes and infrastructure.
 
• **United States:** Promotes the initiative as part of its strategy to counterbalance China’s growing influence.
 
• **European Union:** Seeks to strengthen trade ties with Asia and the Middle East while ensuring sustainable development.

question: Which initiative is linked to India-Bangladesh defence cooperation and involves maritime domain awareness using a radar-based system?

options.text: Joint Bangladesh-India Naval Command Centre in Chattogram

solution:
The correct answer is __**Coastal Surveillance Radar System MoU**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• The **Coastal Surveillance Radar System (CSRS) MoU** is a key initiative under the India-Bangladesh defence cooperation, aimed at enhancing **maritime domain awareness**. 
 
• This initiative involves the installation of advanced **radar-based coastal surveillance systems** along the Bangladeshi coastline to monitor and secure maritime regions. 
 
• The CSRS supports both nations in **combatting maritime threats** such as illegal fishing, smuggling, piracy, and other illicit activities in shared waters. 
 
• India has provided technical and logistical assistance to Bangladesh under this MoU, demonstrating its commitment to fostering **regional maritime security** and bilateral cooperation. 
 
• The implementation of the system aligns with India’s broader vision of ensuring stability and security in the **Indo-Pacific region**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **India-Bangladesh Defence Relations:** 
 
• India and Bangladesh have strengthened their defence partnership in recent years through joint exercises, training programs, and technology sharing. 
 
• Key initiatives include the signing of defence MoUs, cooperation in counter-terrorism, and joint naval exercises like **Bongosagar**. 
 
 
 
• **Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA):** 
 
• MDA refers to the effective understanding of activities and threats in the maritime environment. 
 
• The Coastal Surveillance Radar System is a tool that enhances MDA by providing **real-time data** on maritime traffic and potential threats. 
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Indo-Pacific Region:** 
 
• The Indo-Pacific is strategically significant as it hosts major sea routes, facilitating global trade and commerce. 
 
• India’s focus on the region aligns with its **Act East Policy** and efforts to ensure **freedom of navigation** and regional stability. 
 
 
 
• **Other Defence Initiatives:** 
 
• **Indo-Bangla Coordinated Patrols (CORPAT):** These are joint patrols conducted to enhance security and combat transnational maritime crimes. 
 
• **Joint Training Programs:** Indian armed forces provide training to Bangladeshi military personnel, fostering interoperability and mutual trust. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Comparison of Options:** 
 
• **Joint Bangladesh-India Naval Command Centre in Chattogram:** No such command centre exists. This option is incorrect. 
 
• **Indo-Bangla Coastal Defence Protocol (ICDP):** This is a fictitious term and is not a recognized initiative. Hence, incorrect. 
 
• **Indo-Pacific Maritime Initiative Agreement:** While relevant to regional maritime security, this is not specifically tied to India-Bangladesh cooperation. Incorrect. 
 
 
 
• **Technological Features of CSRS:** 
 
• Equipped with **high-frequency radars** that can monitor vast maritime zones. 
 
• Supports **data sharing** between India and Bangladesh for coordinated security efforts.

question:
**Consider the following statements regarding recent India-Maldives bilateral developments:****1. India announced a financial assistance package of USD 1.4 billion to Maldives during President Solih's 2018 visit.
2. The 6th Joint Commission Meeting (JCM) in 2019 included signing MoUs between the Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs) of both countries.
3. In 2020, India and Maldives signed an agreement for mutual support in climate risk insurance for island territories.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?**
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **December 2018**, during the state visit of Maldives President **Ibrahim Mohamed Solih** to **India**, the Indian government announced a comprehensive financial assistance package of **USD 1.4 billion**. This package was designed to assist the **Maldives** in its socio-economic development and included **budgetary support**, **currency swap agreements**, and **concessional lines of credit**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **6th Joint Commission Meeting (JCM)** between **India** and the **Maldives** was held in **New Delhi** on **13 December 2019**. It was co-chaired by India's External Affairs Minister and the Maldivian Foreign Minister. During this meeting, multiple **Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs)** were signed, including one specifically for cooperation between the **Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs)** of the two countries to strengthen the framework against **money laundering** and **terrorism financing**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• In **2020**, the bilateral relationship was characterized by the **USD 500 million** assistance for the **Greater Male Connectivity Project (GMCP)** and a **USD 250 million** budgetary support to mitigate the impact of **COVID-19**. There is no historical record of a specific agreement signed in **2020** regarding "mutual support in climate risk insurance for island territories" as a primary bilateral development between these two nations. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The diplomatic relationship between the two nations follows the **"India First"** policy of **Maldives** and the **"Neighborhood First"** policy of **India**, aiming for **security and growth for all in the region (SAGAR)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geopolitical Significance:** The **Maldives** is strategically located in the **Indian Ocean**, sitting astride vital **Sea Lines of Communication (SLOCs)** through which a significant portion of world trade and energy supplies pass. It is separated from India's **Minicoy Island** by the **Eight Degree Channel**.
 
• **Operation Cactus (1988):** This was a landmark military intervention where **Indian Armed Forces** assisted the **Maldivian government** in neutralizing a **coup attempt** by mercenaries. This established **India** as a reliable security partner in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• **Operation Neer (2014):** Under this operation, **India** dispatched heavy-lift aircraft and naval ships carrying **bottled water** to **Male** after the city's only **desalination plant** caught fire, demonstrating India's role as a **first responder**.
 
• **Greater Male Connectivity Project (GMCP):** Launched with Indian support, it is the **largest infrastructure project** in the **Maldives**, consisting of a **6.74 km bridge and causeway link** connecting the capital **Male** with the neighboring islands of **Villingili**, **Gulhifalhu**, and **Thilafushi**.
 
• **Economic Cooperation:** **India** is one of the largest **trading partners** of the **Maldives**. In **2021**, India emerged as the **3rd largest** trade partner. The bilateral trade includes exports of **rice**, **spices**, **fruits**, **vegetables**, and **poultry products** from India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Defence Ties:** **India** provides the largest number of **training opportunities** for the **Maldivian National Defence Force (MNDF)**, meeting around **70%** of their total training requirements. Joint exercises like **"Ekuverin"** and **"Dosti"** are held regularly.
 
• **Health Cooperation:** During the **COVID-19 pandemic**, the **Maldives** was the first country to receive **Made-in-India vaccines** (Covishield) in **January 2021** under the **Vaccine Maitri** initiative.
 
• **International Forums:** Both countries are members of the **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)**, the **Commonwealth**, and the **Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)**. India supported the **Maldives'** bid for the **Presidency** of the **76th session** of the **United Nations General Assembly** in **2021**.

__
 
• **Kargil Vijay Diwas**__

 __
 
• Every year **26th July** is observed as the **Kargil Vijay Diwas.**
 
• It is in the memory of the recapture of the Kargil hills after defeating the Pakistani troops in the Kargil district in the Ladakh division.
 
• The mission was named 'Operation Vijay' by the Indian Army, while the Air Force named it 'Operation Safed Sagar'.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Operation Vijay**__

 
 
• In the year **1999,** India and Pakistan signed the **Lahore Agreement** to mutually resolve the Kashmir issue in a peaceful manner.
 
• However, the Pakistani troops began infiltrating toward the Indian side of the Line of Control (LoC) under **Operation Badr**, hoping to cut off Indian Troops in Siachen. 
 
• Indian Army responded by launching **Operation Vijay**.
 
• On **3rd May 1999**, Pakistan started this war when it had infiltrated into the high altitudes in the rocky mountainous region of Kargil with around 5000 soldiers and captured it.
 
• When the Indian Government got the information about it,** ‘Operation Vijay’** was launched by the Indian army to throw back the intruders who had treacherously occupied Indian Territory.

subject: GK
question: The Gothic architectural style originated in which continent?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Europe**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Gothic architectural style** originated in the continent of **Europe**, specifically in **France**, during the **mid-12th century**. It remained the dominant architectural language for religious and secular buildings until the **16th century**.

• The style evolved from **Romanesque architecture** and is characterized by its move toward greater height, light, and structural efficiency. The transition was marked by the reconstruction of the **Abbey Church of Saint-Denis** near **Paris**, initiated by **Abbot Suger** in **1140**.

• The core innovation of the **Gothic style** was the **pointed arch**. Unlike the rounded arches of the **Romanesque** period, the pointed arch allowed for the weight of the roof to be directed more vertically, enabling the construction of much taller walls.

• Other defining features include the **ribbed vault** and the **flying buttress**. These structural elements allowed architects to create thinner walls and incorporate massive **stained-glass windows**, filling the interiors with light, which was a significant departure from the dark, heavy interiors of earlier styles.

• From **France**, the style spread rapidly across the **European** continent, reaching **England**, **Germany**, **Spain**, **Italy**, and **Central Europe**, with each region developing its own unique variations, such as **Perpendicular Gothic** in **England** or **Sondergotik** in **Germany**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Etymology**: The term **Gothic** was originally used as a derogatory label by **Renaissance** writers like **Giorgio Vasari**. They associated the style with the **Goths**, a Germanic tribe that had invaded the **Roman Empire**, viewing the medieval style as barbaric compared to classical **Greek** and **Roman** standards.

• **Structural Components**: The **flying buttress** is perhaps the most iconic feature. It is an external masonry structure that resists the lateral thrust of a roof or vault. This allowed for the creation of the **Clerestory**, the upper part of the nave containing windows that let in direct sunlight.

• **Artistic Elements**: **Gothic** cathedrals are famous for their **Rose Windows**, which are large, circular stained-glass windows typically found at the ends of the transepts or the west facade. These windows often depicted complex theological narratives through **stained glass**.

• **Famous Examples**: Some of the most renowned **Gothic** structures in **Europe** include **Notre-Dame de Paris** (France), **Chartres Cathedral** (France), **Westminster Abbey** (England), **Cologne Cathedral** (Germany), and **Milan Cathedral** (Italy).

• **Gothic Revival**: In the **18th** and **19th centuries**, a movement known as **Neo-Gothic** or **Gothic Revival** emerged. This movement sought to revive medieval **Gothic** forms and was used extensively in the design of university campuses, government buildings (like the **Palace of Westminster** in **London**), and churches across the world.

• **UNESCO Recognition**: Many of these **European** cathedrals are now protected as **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**, recognized for their **architectural** genius and their role as centers of **medieval** culture and learning.
</ul

question: Which of the following forts is located in Rajasthan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrangarh Fort.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Mehrangarh Fort is a **1,200-acre (486-hectare) fort** located in **Jodhpur,** Rajasthan, India.
 
• It was constructed** in 1459** by **Rajput ruler Rao Jodha**, though most of the existing structure is from the **17th century.**
 
• The** chhatri of Kirat Singh Soda**, a soldier who died defending Mehrangarh, is located to the **left of the fort.**
 
• There are **seven gates**, including **Jai Pol** (which means "victory gate"), which was built by **Maharaja Man Singh** to celebrate his triumphs over the troops of **Jaipur and Bikaner in 1806.**
 
• The** Fattehpol** (also known as the "victory gate") celebrates** Maharaja Ajit Singh's** triumph over the** Mughals.**
 
• On a **vertical cliff, four hundred feet** above Jodhpur's skyline, the Mehrangarh Fort rises a hundred feet in majesty.
 
• It is also known as the **Citadel of the Sun.**
 
• Its proportions are so massive that **Rudyard Kipling **referred to it as **"the creation of giants.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sindhudurg Fort:**__

 __
 
• It is a medieval fort located on an island in the** Arabian Sea** just off the coast of **Maharashtra, India.**
 
• **Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj **constructed the fort.
 
• The fortress is located on the coast of** Malvan town** in Sindhudurg District, Maharashtra's Konkan area, **450 kilometers** south of Mumbai.
 
• The original killedars, the** Sakpal Naik family,** still live in one of the **fort's 16 houses.**
 
 
 
• **Bidar Fort**:__
 __
 
• Bidar Fort is a fort at **Bidar, Karnataka, India.**
 
• In** 1427**, **Sultan Ahmad Shah I** of the **Bahmanid Dynasty** relocated his capital from **Gulbarga to Bidar** and constructed a fort and a variety of Islamic structures.
 
• The fort of Bidar contains about **30 monuments.**
 
• In** 2014, UNESCO **added the complex to its "tentative list" of potential World Heritage Sites.
 
• The rise and fall of the Bahmani dynasty, the emergence and split of the five Deccan Sultans, capture by the Barid Shahi and Adil Shahi dynasties, and eventually being won by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the blockade of Bidar in 1657 have all been** **witnessed** **by the Bidar Fort.
 
 
 
• **Asigarh Fort:**__
 
 
• It is also known as** Hansi Fort**, which is a fort on the **eastern bank of Amti Lake** in Hansi, **Haryana, India.**
 
• The fort is regarded to be one of ancient **India's most impenetrable forts**, and ASI named it a** centrally protected monument in 1937**.
 
• **King Anangpal Tomar** is thought to have built the current Asigarh fort building, which was later improved by **Prithviraj Chauhan.**
 
• The fortress was regarded as the **"key to the Deccan"** because it commands a path through the** Satpuras** connecting the** Narmada and Tapti river basins**, one of the most significant routes from northern India to the Deccan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On the sidelines of the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting, the first-ever India-France-Australia Trilateral Foreign Ministerial Dialogue took place in London, United Kingdom.
 
• Dr. S. Jaishankar, India's External Affairs Minister, Mr. Jean-Yves Le Drian, France's Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, and Senator Marise Payne, Australia's Minister for Foreign Affairs, all attended the conference.
 
• The trilateral meeting between France, India, and Australia was launched in September 2020 at the level of Foreign Secretaries, but was quickly elevated to ministerial level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The G7 foreign ministers conference is the first in-person meeting of the grouping's foreign ministers in the wake of the pandemic, with the last one occurring in 2019.

subject: GK
question: Which of the following best reflects the distinguishing operational philosophy of India's 'Neighbourhood First' policy compared to its 'Act East' policy?

options.text: Neighbourhood First targets ASEAN security; Act East delivers SAARC health aid.
Neighbourhood First offers non-reciprocal aid in South Asia; Act East builds strategic ties in Southeast Asia.
Both focus solely on infrastructure in BIMSTEC and QUAD.
Act East builds communities in neighbours; Neighbourhood First leads Indo-Pacific navies.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Neighbourhood First offers non-reciprocal aid in South Asia; Act East builds strategic ties in Southeast Asia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Neighbourhood First** policy is a core component of India's foreign policy that focuses on managing relations with its immediate neighbours in **South Asia**. It is based on the principle of **non-reciprocity**, derived from the **Gujral Doctrine** of **1996**, which suggests that India, as the largest country in the region, should give to its smaller neighbours what it can without expecting an equal return in kind. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **Act East Policy** (AEP) was formally launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** at the **12th ASEAN-India Summit** in **Myanmar** in **November 2014**. It serves as an upgrade to the **Look East Policy** of **1991**. The primary objective is to promote **economic cooperation**, **cultural ties**, and develop **strategic relationships** with countries in the **Asia-Pacific** and **Southeast Asian** regions.
 
• While **Neighbourhood First** targets immediate neighbours like **Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka**, the **Act East** policy specifically targets **ASEAN** countries and the **Indo-Pacific** region. Statement A incorrectly swaps the target groups for security and aid. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Both policies involve multi-dimensional engagement. They are not restricted **solely to infrastructure** but include **maritime security**, **digital connectivity**, **people-to-people contact**, and **trade**. They utilize platforms like **BIMSTEC** and **QUAD**, but their scope is much broader. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Act East Policy** is heavily focused on the **Indo-Pacific** maritime domain and security architecture, whereas **Neighbourhood First** is primarily concerned with **territorial integrity** and **border management** within the subcontinent. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Neighbourhood First Policy:**
 
 
• This policy covers countries such as **Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka**.
 
• It focuses on **connectivity** (rail, road, and port development), **energy cooperation** (hydropower with **Nepal and Bhutan**), and **humanitarian assistance** (as seen during the **2022 Sri Lankan economic crisis**).
 
• India uses institutional frameworks like **SAARC** and **BIMSTEC** to implement this policy, though **SAARC** has remained dormant due to tensions with **Pakistan**.
 
 
 
• **Act East Policy (AEP):**
 
 
• AEP is based on the **4 C's**: **Culture, Commerce, Connectivity, and Capacity Building**.
 
• It involves major regional powers like **Japan, South Korea, and Australia**, focusing on the **ASEAN**-centricity of the **Indo-Pacific**.
 
• Key projects include the **India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway** and the **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project**, which aim to link **North-East India** with **Southeast Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Security and Growth for All in the Region (SAGAR):**
 
 
• Launched in **2015**, this initiative complements both policies by focusing on **maritime cooperation** in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• It emphasizes **blue economy**, **disaster management**, and safeguarding **sea lanes of communication**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Policy:** The transition from **Look East** to **Act East** marked a shift from purely **economic engagement** to a **security-oriented** and **proactive strategic** role in the **Asia-Pacific**.
 
• **Geopolitical Context:** Both policies are crucial for India to counter the **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)** of **China** and to maintain **regional stability** through **bilateral** and **multilateral** forums.
 
• **Key Summits:** India frequently engages in the **East Asia Summit (EAS)** and the **ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF)** to further the **Act East** agenda.
</ul

question:
Which of the following statements about the India–Japan strategic and economic partnership are correct?
1) Japan is India’s 5th-largest FDI source, with over $43 billion invested and key roles in metro and bullet train projects.
2) CEPA (2011) led to 11 Japanese industrial townships in 8 Indian states and 1,400+ Japanese firms in India.
3) CEPA launched a Digital Skills Exchange Program on AI and Kaizen-based public governance.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 2 only**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• **Statement 1 is correct:** **Japan** is currently the **5th-largest** source of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in India. Between April 2000 and March 2024, cumulative FDI from Japan reached approximately **$41.5 billion to $43 billion**. Japan has played a pivotal role in India's infrastructure development, providing technical and financial assistance for various **Metro Rail projects** (like Delhi and Mumbai) and the prestigious **Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR)**, commonly known as the **Bullet Train** project.

• **Statement 2 is correct:** The **Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)**, signed in **2011**, has been a cornerstone of bilateral trade. It facilitated the establishment of **Japanese Industrial Townships (JITs)** to provide ready-to-use infrastructure for Japanese companies. Currently, there are **12 JITs** across various Indian states (including Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh). Furthermore, the number of **Japanese companies** registered in India has grown significantly, exceeding **1,400**.

• **Statement 3 is incorrect:** While India and Japan do cooperate on **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Kaizen-based governance**, these initiatives were not launched under the **2011 CEPA**. The **India-Japan Digital Partnership (IJDP)** was specifically launched in **October 2018** to focus on **Digital Transformation**, **AI**, and **IoT**. **Kaizen** principles are promoted through the **Japan-India Institute for Manufacturing (JIM)** and other skill development programs, which are separate from the trade-focused CEPA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The relationship between India and Japan was elevated to a **Special Strategic and Global Partnership** in 2014.

• Japan is the largest provider of **Official Development Assistance (ODA)** to India, supporting projects in power, transport, and environmental sectors.

• Both nations are members of the **QUAD** (alongside the USA and Australia) and the **Supply Chain Resilience Initiative (SCRI)**, aimed at diversifying global supply chains.

• The **Act East Forum**, established in 2017, focuses on the development of India's **North Eastern Region (NER)** through Japanese investment and connectivity projects.
</ul

question: Which of the following best characterizes India's strategic use of the IORA platform as demonstrated at the 2024 Goa seminar?

options.text: Led action on IUU fishing in the Indian Ocean.
Invited SAARC to draft a humanitarian charter.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Led action on IUU fishing in the Indian Ocean.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• India's strategic engagement at the **2024 Goa seminar** focused on addressing the challenge of **Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing**, which is a major threat to the **maritime economy** and **biodiversity** of the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.

• By leading this action, India utilized the **Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)** platform to strengthen **maritime security** and promote **sustainable fishing practices** among member nations.

• The initiative involves enhancing **maritime domain awareness** through the **Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR)** to track suspicious vessel movements and 'dark vessels' that bypass traditional tracking systems.

• This leadership role reinforces India's position as a **Net Security Provider** and its commitment to the **Blue Economy**, ensuring that ocean resources are used responsibly for the benefit of all littoral states.

• The other options are incorrect because **IORA** generally avoids bilateral **maritime border disputes**, and while trade is a priority, the specific 2024 Goa seminar was centered on **maritime safety** and **IUU fishing** rather than **SAARC** charters or general **Indo-Pacific trade deals**.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)** was established in **1997** and currently comprises **23 member states** and **12 dialogue partners**.

• India's approach to the region is guided by the **SAGAR** (Security and Growth for All in the Region) initiative, launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** in **2015**.

• The **IORA Secretariat** is located in **Ebene, Mauritius**, and the organization focuses on six priority areas, including **maritime safety and security**, **trade and investment facilitation**, and **fisheries management**.

• **IUU fishing** accounts for a significant portion of the global catch, leading to billions of dollars in economic losses and depleting fish stocks that millions of people rely on for protein.

question: Examine the statements below and select the most appropriate option.**Assertion (A):** India and Chile's signing of the CEPA Terms of Reference in May 2025 signified a strategic move beyond the underperforming Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA).**Reason (R):** The April 2024 Joint Study Group recommended a broader CEPA to boost cooperation in digital services, critical minerals, and MSMEs.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
A is true, but R is false

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Assertion (A)** is correct because **India** and **Chile** officially signed the **Terms of Reference (ToR)** for a **Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)** in **May 2025**. This move signifies a shift from the existing **Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA)**, which was limited in scope, to a more holistic economic framework.

• The **Reason (R)** is also correct and provides the direct justification for the assertion. The **Joint Study Group (JSG)**, which concluded its assessment in **April 2024**, found that the current trade setup did not fully capture the potential of modern economic sectors.

• The **JSG** specifically recommended a **CEPA** to address and enhance cooperation in **digital services**, **critical minerals** (such as **lithium** and **copper**), and the **MSME sector**, which are crucial for the future growth of both economies.

• Since the recommendations of the **Joint Study Group** (Reason) were the primary driver behind the decision to sign the **ToR** for the **CEPA** (Assertion), **R** is the correct explanation of **A**.

**Additional Information__**

• The **India-Chile PTA** was first signed in **March 2006** and implemented in **August 2007**, with a major expansion taking place in **2017** to increase the number of tariff lines.

• **Chile** is the first country in the **Latin American region** to sign a **PTA** with India, making it a pioneer in India's **'Focus LAC'** policy.

• **Critical minerals** are a focal point of this upgraded agreement because **Chile** holds some of the world's largest reserves of **lithium**, which is essential for India's **National Electric Mobility Mission**.

• A **CEPA** is more comprehensive than a **PTA** or **FTA (Free Trade Agreement)** as it covers **trade in services**, **investment**, and other areas of **economic partnership** beyond just goods and tariffs.
</ul
